But those elicited afterward shall have no force unless they accord with public laws [Note: [Col. 0143D] l 1: *sua*, corrected to *suam*.] [Note: [Col. 0143D] m 1: *consentaneas*, corrected to *consentanea*.] [Note: [Col. 0143D] n 1: *leges*, corrected to *legibus*.]; especially since it is both proper and permitted for us alone to examine the interpretation interposed between equity [Note: [Col. 0143D] o 1: *aequitate*, corrected to *aequitatem*.] and law [Note: [Col. 0143D] p At this point the text ends on the first leaf of manuscript 1; what follows was restored by P. from Cod. Just. 1, 14, 1; but manuscripts Pl. 1, 2, Bg., Hal. also have *jus*, “law.”].

Given on the third day before the Nones of December, in the consulship of Sabinus and Rufinus (316).

## ON ACCUSATIONS AND FORMAL CHARGES

[Note: [Col. 0143D] q In the upper margin of manuscript 4 there are traces of some word ending in *-dosiana*, written in large letters, most of which has been cut away. I think I have made out the letters *dosiana*. “Of the Theodosian [Code]?” The manuscript itself begins: “*** on accusations and formal charges.” The asterisks indicate a gap plainly visible [Col. 0144B] at the beginning of the line. Thus the book-heading and title number are missing. A recent hand adds: “Book Nine, Title I, of the Theodosian Code.” See my published *Summaries of the Theodosian Code*, p. IV. As regards corrections in the manuscript, discussed in the same work, p. VIII: I indicate those made by the copyist himself as “copyist”; the very ancient ones as “earlier hand” or “second hand”; annotations painted in ink, chiefly in Books XIII–XVI, as “recent hand”; and finally all the others in the respective colour in which they are written. 15: “On Formal Charges and Actions.” Some manuscripts: “Charges.” Moreover Til.: “Of the Theodosian Code,” and 15: “Book VIII.” See C. Th., p. 95, note e, and p. [Col. 0144C] 177, note q.]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Octavianus [Note: [Col. 0144C] r 15: “From Octavianus.” Then 19: “Spain”; 40: “Spain”; in other manuscripts *Hisp-* is omitted.] Count of the Spains.

Whoever [Col. 0144A] [Note: [Col. 0144C] a 6–8, 12, 14: “Whatever.”] abducts a virgin of senatorial rank [Note: [Col. 0144C] b 10, 18: “of senatorial rank.” Cod. Just.: “Whoever, endowed not with illustrious but only with senatorial rank, abducts a virgin.”], or invades any boundaries [Note: [Col. 0144C] c Til.: “thieves,” but in my copy corrected by an earlier hand to “boundaries.” 20: “boundaries invaded through some fault.”], or is caught in any fault or crime [Note: [Col. 0144C] d 19, 20: “in any crime,” omitting “fault or.” 16, 17: “any fault.”], shall immediately [Note: [Col. 0144C] e Cod. Just. omits “immediately.” Then 8: “province.”] be subjected, within the province in which he committed the offence, to public laws [Note: [Col. 0144C] f 20: “to legal punishments,” corrected; 9, 13, 25: “is subjected.” Cod. Just. omits “nor—reported.”]. No report concerning him shall be made to our cognizance, nor may he employ a plea of forum [Note: [Col. 0144C] g Some manuscripts: “prescription.”]. For criminal liability excludes every honour [Note: [Col. 0144C] h 15: “liability excludes honour.” Cod. Just.: “For liability excludes every honour of this sort,” omitting “when—a case is brought.”], since a criminal case [Note: [Col. 0144C] i *caussa* omitted in manuscript 19.] rather than a civil or monetary matter is at issue [Note: [Col. 0144C] j 19 omits “matter.” 20: “civil matters.”] [Note: [Col. 0144D] k 6, 10, 12, 14, 16: “peculiar”; first printed Ri.: 19, 20: “money.” 15: “matter but monetary.”].

Given on the day before the Nones of December at Serdica [Note: [Col. 0144D] l 20: third day before the Ides of December; 42: “Nones of November.” Cod. Just. omits “at Serdica—at Corduba.” “Serdica—and” is absent in manuscript 8, and *prid.* in manuscript 24. 38: “Sirdice,” corrected by a later hand. 42: “Serditie.” 20, 43: “Sirdicae.” 21, Sich.: “Serdice.”], received on the fifth day before the Nones of March at Corduba [Note: [Col. 0144D] m 15: “at Sirmium.”] [Note: [Col. 0144D] n 6, 24, Til. omit V.] [Note: [Col. 0144D] o Most manuscripts: “Corduba” or “Cordoba.”], in the consulship of Gallicanus [Note: [Col. 0144D] p Some manuscripts: “Galliganus,” “Gallianus,” “Galicanus.” Aur. Lugd.: “in the consulship.”] and Bassus (317).

**Interpretation.** Whoever commits a culpable [Note: [Col. 0144D] q 6, 7: accusative *damnabilem*.] or legally punishable crime [Note: [Col. 0144D] r 8: “in punishing”; 20: “punishable from antiquity.” Rio: “has committed a crime.”] shall not claim that he must be prosecuted in his own forum—that is, in the place where [Note: [Col. 0144D] s This interpretation was first printed by Go.] [Note: [Col. 0144D] t 6, 7: “to which.”] [Note: [Col. 0144D] u 20 adds “publicly or.”] he lives—but shall be punished by the judges of the place where the crime was committed; nor shall a report concerning his person be made to the emperor.

In the year of the Lord 317, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus.

[Col. 0144B]

## ON DECURIONS

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Octavianus [Note: [Col. 0144D] v 4, Til.–Ri*: “Octabianus.”] Count of the Spains.

[Col. 0145A] Those [Note: [Col. 0145B] a 4, Til.–Ri*: “Hii.”] who have wished to seize the insignia of an unmerited honour, when the leading men and municipal councillors are summoned to the council [Note: [Col. 0145B] b Go. in notes: “and council.”], stand while those sit [Note: [Col. 0145B] c Be.: “are summoned, stand.” Go. Be. in notes restore *assistant*, “stand,” correctly; but *assistunt*, “they attend,” can also be defended.], to whom every honour is deservedly due by right on account of services completed. [Note: [Col. 0145B] d Fol. 219 [ [Col. 0145B] b Go. in notes: “and council.”] of manuscript 4.]

Therefore, Your Sublimity shall permit no one at all to enjoy the prerogative of a governorship unless he has passed through all ranks in his native city in due order [Note: [Col. 0145B] e Go. in notes: “And completed.”] [Note: [Col. 0145B] f Go. Be. in notes restore *ordine*, “in order,” for *per ordinem*, which the editions have. 4 reads: “of governorship—having passed through by prerogative to rejoice unless he has passed through all ranks in his native city by order”; but the words “by prerogative—having passed through,” which are written twice, are deleted with points by an ancient hand. They are later deleted again in red, and the word *per* before *ordine* is also erased; I think this was an error that passed into the editions. I have therefore restored the correct reading *per ordinem*. Rein. conjectures the same; for he adds: “*per*: so in law 75: ‘Those who have reached the priesthood of a province and the chief honour gradually and in due order, after completing public duties and service.’”], so that even those who obtained a governorship prematurely may enjoy its distinctions after completing their civic honours [Note: [Col. 0145C] g 4: *civiens*, corrected by a second hand to *civicos*.] and rendering the prescribed services.

Published on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0145C] h Aur. Lugd.: “in the consulship.”] (317).

## TO THE CLAUDIAN SENATUS CONSULTUM

Emperor Constantine Augustus . . . . . . [Note: [Col. 0145C] i The law itself has perished, nor can its true meaning be gathered from the interpretation. On triple summons and triple appearance, see Go. in commentary on this constitution; W., note t; Zimmern, cited work, vol. I, p. 730, note 5; Haubold’s Works, vol. II, p. 912, note c; and the *Treatise on Triple Appearance*, published from my papers by Haubold, cited work, p. 910.]

Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of February [Note: [Col. 0145D] j Go.–Be. wrongly omit “February.”], in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

**Interpretation.** In the presence of seven witnesses, Roman citizens, a third summons must be issued under the Claudian senatorial decree.

## TO THE JULIAN LAW ON MAJESTY

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Prefect of the City. If anyone violently invades another’s landed estate, he shall be punished capitally [Note: [Col. 0145D] k Fol. 17 [ [Col. 0145B] a 4, Til.–Ri*: “Hii.”] of manuscript 4 begins with the letters *niatur*.]. Whether someone from the party of one attempting to inflict violence, or from that of one repelling injury, has been killed, punishment shall bind the person who wished violently to dispossess the possessor [Note: [Col. 0145D] l Ri*: “with.”].

Given on the sixth day before the Ides of March [Note: [Col. 0145D] m Go. considers the month erroneous, since the author of the *Notitia of the Urban Prefects* states that this Septimius Bassus entered upon the urban prefecture on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May. Go. therefore, followed by Ri., emends to May; but because this does not appear sufficient to Be.—since the anonymous *Series of Urban Prefects* dates Bassus’s urban prefecture only from the Ides of May (see Corsini, cited work, p. 173)—he suspects either that Bassus was then not Prefect of the City or that the law was issued later. Tillemont had already expressed this opinion, cited work, vol. IV, p. 131, note XXXIX, where he wishes to read the sixth day before the Ides of July or August. March is undoubtedly false, since the law would be earlier than the first law under this title; May cannot stand, because Constantius was then present at Rome, where this law was given. Thus Go., in notes and in Chronicle, [Col. 0146B] p. XIII, understands *Dat.* as “returned” or “published.” It seems to me that Tillemont judged this passage correctly, although I do not reject another month. Go., indeed, at c. 7 C. Th., *On Appeals* (XI, 30), emends to June. For he says that the subscription here must be corrected from the cited c. 7; but that was given on the eighth day before the Ides of June.], at Rome, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

## ON THOSE WHO MAKE DISCLOSURES

[Col. 0146A]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the Rationales [Note: [Col. 0146B] a Go. in Chronicle; Cuj. in Cod. Just.: singular “to the Rationalis.” Cod. [Col. 0146C] Just.: “Emperor Constantine Augustus to Maximus, Rationalis of the Spains.”] of the Spains.

The person to whom an inheritance has been entrusted under a secret trust [*fideicommissum*] [Note: [Col. 0146C] b 4: *tacita*, corrected in yellow to *tacitae*. Aur. Lugd.: “secret trusts.”] shall immediately report it to your office [Note: [Col. 0146C] c 4, Cuj. 1–2*, Ri. Ri*: passive “shall be reported.” Go.: plural “shall report,” and in notes, because of the heading and what follows: “By himself. Moreover he attempts *nuntiet*, ‘let him report,’ and so forth.” Be., from Cod. Just., emends to *nuntiet*, by which correction everything proceeds correctly.], disclose the record, and promptly report what has been done; and after this disclosure he shall receive a third share from all the property of the deceased [Note: [Col. 0146C] d Cod. Just. begins fol. 102 verso of manuscript 4 with “From the words *Cum V.*”].

But if this has been revealed to your office of devotion by the deceased’s wife [Note: [Col. 0146C] e Cod. Just.: “this to the office,” first printed Go.], she herself [Note: [Col. 0146C] f 4 and editions before Be.: accusative *ipsam*. Be., following Go., from Cod. Just. restores *ipsa*, correctly.] too [Note: [Col. 0146C] g Cod. Just. adds “person.”], if she reveals the record, though the deceased wished her to be heir [Note: [Col. 0146C] h Cod. Just.: “shall appear,” first printed Go.; but some manuscript copies of Cod. Just. have “shall reveal,” as C. Th. does. Cf. Cuj., commentary on c. 1 of cited Cod. Just., cited place, p. 246, and Dirksen, cited work, p. 496.], shall receive such a reward that she obtains half the entire estate and shares the division with our fisc [Note: [Col. 0146C] i 4 and editions: “her,” except Be., who, at Go.’s urging, from Cod. Just. restores *cum*, “with,” correctly.], having also the privilege of choosing her portion first [Note: [Col. 0146D] j Cod. Just.: “choice,” first printed Go.]. Then that concealer of the records, equally an enemy of the fisc and of the woman, stripped of all his property, which shall be claimed by the fisc, shall be deported to an island.

Given on the Ides of March, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0146D] k Aur. Lugd.: “in the consulship.”] (317).

## TO THE JULIAN LAW ON PUBLIC [Note: [Col. 0146D] l “the way.”] AND [Note: [Col. 0146D] m Some manuscripts: “and which”; Just.: “or.”] PRIVATE VIOLENCE

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Catulinus [Note: [Col. 0146D] n See c. 1 C. Th., *On Jurisdiction* (II, 1), note o. 4, Til.–Be.: “Catullinus.” Some manuscripts: “Catolinus,” “Catholinus.” 42: “Catellinus.” 15: “Catulinus, proconsul of Africa.” The rank is omitted in some manuscripts. 4: *pu*; Til.: *PV*. See C. Th. XI, 16, 1, note m.] Proconsul of Africa.

Whoever is manifestly discovered in court to have committed violence [Note: [Col. 0146D] o 20: “manifestly.”] [Note: [Col. 0146D] p 6, 10: “now not”; 12 omits “not now”; 14: “now.”] shall no longer be punished by relegation or deportation to an island [Note: [Col. 0146D] q 6–8, 10, 12, 14, 18 omit “or” and write “relegation of deportation.” 21: “relegation or of deportation.” 17: “of deportation.”] [Note: [Col. 0146D] r The words “is punished, who is discovered to have committed manifest violence” recur in c. 14 C. Th., *Whose Appeals* (XI, 36).], but shall undergo capital punishment [Col. 0147A]; nor shall an appeal lodged suspend the sentence pronounced against him [Note: [Col. 0147B] a Sich.: “nor, a proposed appeal”; 6: *urocatione*; 14: “do not interpose.”] [Note: [Col. 0147B] b 7, 10, 15, 20, 21: “the sentence which.” Then 21, Sich.: “in that,” and 14: “had been pronounced.”].

For many crimes are included under the single name of violence [Note: [Col. 0147B] c From here begins c. 1 of the cited Cod. Just. 1, 18: “suspend, because not many.”], since, when some attempt to inflict violence upon others [Note: [Col. 0147C] d Cod. Just.: “when they contend.”], and others resist indignantly [Note: [Col. 0147C] e 6–10, 14, 16–18, 21, Cod. Just., Sich., Capit.: “resisting.” Thus also manuscript 20, anciently.], blows and killings are often found to have been committed [Note: [Col. 0147C] f Thus 4, Br. Alr. manuscripts, Cod. Just., and editions before Be., except Sich., who from manuscript 21 prints “are discovered.” Cap. agrees. Be. restores “may be discovered,” unnecessarily; yet Go. also in notes has “may be discovered.” Manuscript 20, anciently: “to have committed.”].

Accordingly [Note: [Col. 0147C] g “Accordingly” is absent from Cod. Just.], it was decided [Note: [Col. 0147C] h Til.–Ri* add “that” from manuscript 4, which Be. rightly deletes. It is absent from all Br. Al. manuscripts, from Sich., and from Cod. Just.] that, if perhaps anyone either from the possessor’s party [Note: [Col. 0147C] i 6–8, 10, 14, 16–18: “from the possessors’ party.” 10, 18 omit “from” after “either,” and 13: “or from the party.”] or from that of the person who attempted rashly to disturb the possession [Note: [Col. 0147C] j 20: “share,” with “suffering” above the line, erroneously. Then 6: “attempted.”] has been killed, punishment shall be inflicted on the person who attempted violence [Note: [Col. 0147C] k Sich.: “judgment be issued.” Cod. Just.: “be exercised.” 14: “go out.” 20: “be burned.”] [Note: [Col. 0147C] l 20, Cod. Just.: “attempted.” 4: *temptauit*, with two letters erased. 10, 18: “and to either.” 20: “and to either party.”], and who furnished either party with the cause of the evils [Note: [Col. 0147D] m Some manuscripts: *caussa*.] [Note: [Col. 0147D] n Cod. Just.: “has furnished,” and transfers “shall no longer—suspend” to this place, while omitting “Whoever—violence.”].

Given on the fifteenth [Note: [Col. 0147D] o 24: eleventh; 8 omits fifteenth.] day before the Kalends of May at Serdica [Note: [Col. 0147D] p See c. 1 of the preceding title.], in the consulship of Gallicanus [Note: [Col. 0147D] q 6, 7, 12, 14, 16: “Gallicus,” wrongly. 8 omits “Serdica, Gallicanus.”] and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0147D] r 6, 7, 10, 14, 16–18 add “for the second time.”] (317).

**Interpretation.** A person convicted in court [Note: [Col. 0147D] s Some manuscripts: “court,” and then “are punished.”] of the evident crime of violence shall be punished capitally, and the person condemned shall not suspend the judge’s sentence by any appeal whatsoever. If, moreover, killings have perhaps been committed by both parties, punishment shall be exacted from the person [Note: [Col. 0147D] t Sich.: “upon that person.” Some manuscripts: “shall be punished.”] who violently entered in order to expel another by killing [Note: [Col. 0147D] u 6–8, 12, 14, 16, 18 and other manuscripts: “who, in order to drive another away by killing”—an ungrammatical reading; but in 7 a second hand corrected it to “to expel.”].

## ON APPEALS

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Prefect of the City. Litigants have leave, even when written petitions have not been prepared [Note: [Col. 0147D] v Cod. Just.: “unwritten.”], to appeal immediately by word of mouth when the matter requires it, after judgment [Note: [Col. 0147D] x Cod. Just. adds: “both in civil and criminal cases.”].

Given on the eighth day before the Ides of June at Sirmium [Note: [Col. 0147D] y Be., Cod. Just.: “at Sirmium.”], in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

## ON CAESARIANS

[Col. 0148A]

Emperor [Note: [Col. 0148C] a With the heading of this constitution begins fol. 86b of manuscript 4.] Constantine Augustus to the Bithynians. Caesarians, while they are merely employed in active service, ought not to be admitted to the ranks of *perfectissimus*, the two-hundred-thousand or one-hundred-thousand dignities, or the rank of *egregius*. But if they have completed their office blamelessly and are free from every fiscal liability, such a rank, bestowed by judicial decision, ought to benefit them [Note: [Col. 0148C] b Til.–Cui. 2: “fiscal liability, bestowed by judicial decision.”].

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0148C] c See c. 3 C. Th., *On Cohorts* (VIII, 4), note.] (317).

## ON PRIMIPILARES

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the Bithynians. After completing military service, *primipilares* may be granted the rank of *perfectissimus*, the two-hundred-thousand or one-hundred-thousand dignity, or the rank of *egregius*.

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0148C] d Go., Chronicle, p. XIII, annotates concerning this law and those which I have said above are connected with it: “Either these laws are to be attributed to Licinius, who possessed Bithynia, or they are to be referred to other consuls, perhaps Gallicanus and Symmachus—that is, A.D. 330.” If so, add “at Constantinople.” See Vatican Fragments §248.] (317).

## ON MUREX-WORKERS AND GYNAECIARII [Note: [Col. 0148C] e 4: *gyneceariis*, corrected in red to *gyneceiariis*. Til.–Ri*, in the index of headings, *gynaecειariis*, and likewise here in Til.–Cui. 2*; Go.–Ri* instead: *gynaeceiariis*. Cod. [Col. 0148D] Just.: “On Murex-workers and Gynaeceum Officials, Procurators of the Gynaeceum, Moneyers, and Carriers.”] AND MONEYERS AND CARRIERS

[Col. 0148B]

Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0148D] f Cui. 2, 2*: “Constantius,” erroneously. Then 4 and Ri*: “Bythynians.”] Augustus to the Bithynians. Moneyers must always remain in their condition [Note: [Col. 0148D] g Cod. Just. reverses the order: “must remain always in their condition.”], and the rank of *perfectissimus*, the two-hundred-thousand or one-hundred-thousand dignity, or the rank of *egregius* must not be bestowed on them [Note: [Col. 0148D] h Cod. Just.: “nor are they to be released from such a condition by the privilege of any rank whatsoever.”].

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

## ON DECURIONS

Constantine Augustus to the Bithynians. Those who have served in the palace, those to whom provinces have been entrusted, and those who have deservedly [Note: [Col. 0148D] i Go. rightly criticizes the reading *merito* in earlier editions; this word is so written adverbially.] attained the honour of the most distinguished administrations, with the rank of *perfectissimus* or *egregius* [Note: [Col. 0148D] j Go. incorrectly: “honour.”], and likewise those who, having been made decurions or chief municipal officers, have performed all the public duties of their native city [Note: [Col. 0148D] k 4 has *tamen*, “nevertheless,” for *non et*, “and likewise”; corrected by the copyist to *non et*. The same hand repeated it in red.], must enjoy the rank granted to them.

But if a decurion, having procured by influence [Note: [Col. 0148D] l “Decurion” is omitted in manuscript 4, but restored by the copyist.] [Note: [Col. 0148D] m 4: *comparat*, corrected by the copyist through addition of *o*, *comparato*.] the rank of *perfectissimus*, the two-hundred-thousand or one-hundred-thousand dignity, or the rank of *egregius* [Note: [Col. 0148D] n 4: plural *meruerint*, wrongly.], wishes to evade his municipal council, he shall lose his codicils of appointment and be returned to his original condition, so that, after discharging all civic honours and duties [Col. 0149A] [Note: [Col. 0149B] a Fol. 220 [ [Col. 0150C] a 13: “alteration.” 21: “of adulterous imitation.” 20: “of adulterous alteration.”] of manuscript 4 begins with the letters *ctus*.], he may obtain some prerogative in accordance with municipal law [Note: [Col. 0149B] b 4: “prerogative,” corrected in red.].

Nor does the rank of *perfectissimus* obtained through influence protect from the municipal council the person summoned to it on grounds of origin, residence, or the condition of landholding [Note: [Col. 0149B] c 4: *vocatum*, corrected by an earlier hand to *vocatur*.]; once that rank is removed, he must be delivered to the council.

Given on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus [Note: [Col. 0149B] d See C. Th. VIII, 4, 3, note *. Ri. approves Go.’s opinion that the consuls of the year 330 should be restored. What prevents me from agreeing is the chronological sequence of the laws; this constitution would then have to be placed after c. 18 under this title, which place seems to me much too remote.] (317).

## IF ANYONE CUTS AWAY THE OUTER RIM OF A SOLIDUS [Note: [Col. 0149B] e Some manuscripts: “Outer Rim” and “Cuts Away.” 15: “If he introduces false coinage.” 24: “If anyone rims solidi or fraudulently introduces them in selling.” Other manuscripts omit “or—introduces.” 21: “for selling.” Formerly 20: “in selling.”] OR INTRODUCES AN ADULTERATED ONE IN SELLING

[Note: [Col. 0149C] f Fol. 35a of manuscript 4.] Emperor Constantine Augustus to Leontius [Note: [Col. 0149C] g Many manuscripts: “Leoncius.” 20: “prefect.” 15 omits “Constantianus.”] Prefect of the Praetorian Guard.

All solidi in which our image and veneration are one [Note: [Col. 0149C] h 6–8, 13, 14, 16 omit “in.” Then 15 omits “and,” consistently with Go.’s conjecture.] [Note: [Col. 0149C] i Sich.: “our veneration is present.” Then 20: “to be valued.”] shall be valued and sold at one price, although their dimensions of form differ [Note: [Col. 0149C] j 15, 20: “different forms.” 12, omitting *formae*: “different dimension”; 13: “different dimensions.” 20: “future,” but “dimensions” above the line.]. For a coin whose facial image extends over a larger area [Note: [Col. 0149C] k 15: “in the circuit of the face”; 20: “the act of making.”] [Note: [Col. 0149C] l 7, 8, 10, 12–14, 16, 18: “is extended.” 21, Sich.: “will be extended.” 20: “larger.”] is not to be considered of greater value; nor is one confined within a narrower impression to be regarded as worth less [Note: [Col. 0149C] m Til.–Lugd. have “to have,” as manuscript 4; Cui. 2–Be.: “to be held,” from Cujacius’s conjecture. I do not doubt that the copyist of manuscript 4 erred. All Br. Al. manuscripts and Sich. have “to be worth,” which I have restored. The reading of manuscript 1 is uncertain, for it has *minoris . . . . re*. Moreover 20: “less.”] [Col. 0149B], since the weight remains the same.

But if anyone acts otherwise [Note: [Col. 0149C] n 15 omits “But” before “if.” 20: “For if something is lacking.”], he must either be punished capitally, handed over to the flames, or subjected to another deadly punishment [Note: [Col. 0149D] o Sich. notes at *vel*, “or,” that a verb such as *adfici*, “be subjected,” is missing. Certainly these words are suspect unless joined to the preceding *puniri debet*, “must be punished.” The manuscript variations also matter: 6–8, 12, 14 have *plena* for *poena*. 6–8, 14: “let him bear death”; 10: “deadly, let him”; 13, 16: “deadly, let him”; 18: “deadly, let him”; 12 omits “deadly—of the rim.” Further, manuscript 4 reads “For he” for “But he,” and manuscript 20 “than above but.” Write: “let him be struck with death.”]. The same punishment shall be suffered by the person [Note: [Col. 0149D] p 15: “also that person.”] who shaves away the measure of the outer rim [Note: [Col. 0149D] q Ri*: “of the little circle.”] [Note: [Col. 0149D] r 1, 4, 20, 21, Til.–Lugd.: *adroserit*, that is, “has cut around.” See C. Th. 7, 2. Sich.: *arroserit*; 6–8, 10, 12–14, 16, 18: *abraserit*, “has scraped away”; 15: *arraserit*; Cuj. 2–Be.: *adraserit*. Go. says that although *adroserit* is not wrongly used, being the proper term in this matter, he nevertheless retains *adraserit*.] so as to reduce its quantity of weight, or who introduces, in selling, a stamped solidus made by adulterated imitation [Col. 0150A] [Note: [Col. 0150C] a 13: “alteration.” 21: “of adulterous imitation.” 20: “of adulterous alteration.”].

Given on the seventh [Note: [Col. 0150C] b 20, 28, 33, 34, 36, 40: sixth. 1, 6–8, 12–14, 16 and other manuscripts omit “seventh”; 8 also omits “and Bassus.”] day before the Kalends of August [Note: [Col. 0150C] c 20: June. Go., Chronicle, p. XIV, notes: “And below, A.D. 319, I. 1, *On Accountants*, which is said to have been published at Hierapolis. Therefore these laws may appear attributable to Licinius.”], in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

**Interpretation.** Whoever clips a solidus, introduces an adulterated one [Note: [Col. 0150C] d Some manuscripts: “If anyone has clipped the rim of a solidus or suppressed an adulterated one.” 6, 7, 20, 21 and other manuscripts omit “or” before “adulterated.” Sich.: “or has introduced another.”], or makes counterfeit money, shall be punished capitally [Note: [Col. 0150C] e 6, 7, 21, 43 and other manuscripts: “shall be punished.”].

## ON THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNORS OF PROVINCES

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus . . . [Note: [Col. 0150C] f Bassus’s rank is not mentioned in manuscript 5. Cl. and W. think Septimius Bassus, then urban prefect, is meant; this does not seem admissible to me because provincial decrees are mentioned here [Col. 0150D]. Perhaps he is that Bassus who, according to the sole constitution C. Th., *If Anyone* (IX, 8), was Vicar of Italy, which Go. assigns to the year 320.]

Decrees of provincials [Note: [Col. 0150D] g On these decrees see Go. on the title and c. 3 C. Th., *On Envoys and Decrees of Embassies* (XII, 12).] must not be carried to the imperial court [Note: [Col. 0150D] h See c. 3 C. Th., *On the Office of Vicars* (I, 15).] until each individual petitioner has examined and approved them and authenticated them with his subscription [Note: [Col. 0150D] i The manuscript is not clearly written here; nor is Cl.’s reading clearer, where it has *ad stluccione(?)*. According to my transcript, the reading is either *adstinccione* or *adstruccione*. Cl. W.: *adscriptione*, probably; Schro. Pu., from Taf.’s conjecture: *adstipulatione*, first printed by Schro. *Adscriptio* seems to mean the same as *subscriptio* in c. 15 C. Th., *On Envoys* (XII, 12).]. If anything is done contrary to this, an appropriate punishment shall be imposed [Note: [Col. 0150D] j 5. Pu.: *execretur*, which Taf. also seems to admit, first printed by Schro.; Taf. conjectures *exsequatur*, as in c. 1 C. Th., *On the Office of the Praetorian Prefect* (I, 14). Cl. W. emend to *exerceatur*, approved by Schro.].

Published on the eighth day before the Kalends of October at Caralis [Note: [Col. 0150D] k 5 and editions: “Caralis,” but already W. in corrections: “Carali.”], in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

## ON FUGITIVE SLAVES

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Valerianus. Whoever receives a fugitive slave into his house or onto his estate without the owner’s knowledge shall return him together with another slave of equal value, or with twenty solidi. If he receives him a second or third time, he shall, besides the slave himself, provide two or three other slaves, respectively, or the aforesaid valuation for each slave to the owner. In the case of minors, the same penalty shall threaten tutors or curators.

If the recipient is altogether unable to pay the aforesaid penalty, punishment shall be imposed upon him according to the valuation of the competent judge. But if the fugitive slave has falsely claimed to be freeborn and has been employed for wages by someone, the person who had him cannot be accused of anything. The slave, however, must be tortured so that he may reveal whether, in order to obtain profit, he was cleverly sent by his owner to the house or estate of the person who received him, or not [Col. 0150C]. If interrogation of the slave reveals that this was maliciously done, the person who did it must be deprived even of his own slave, and that slave shall belong to the fisc.

[Col. 0151A] Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of July, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus, 317. (From Cod. Just.)

## WHERE SENATORS OR MEN OF SENATORIAL RANK ARE TO BE SUED, CIVILLY OR CRIMINALLY

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Octavianus, Count of the Spains. Whoever, endowed not with illustrious but only with senatorial rank, abducts a virgin, invades any boundaries, or is caught in any fault or crime, shall be subjected within the province in which he committed the offence to public laws, and shall not use a plea of forum. For criminal liability excludes every honour of this kind.

Given on the second day before the Nones of December, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317).

## ON INTEREST
The Emperor Constantine Augustus to the People. In the conduct of litigation, the trustworthiness of documents has the same force as the depositions of witnesses. Given at Rome, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Bassus (317). (From the Code of Justinian.)

In the year of the Lord 318, in the consulship of Licinius Caesar and Crispus Caesar.

## CONCERNING VETERANS

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Florianus, Praetorian Prefect. [Note: “[Col. 0151C] *a* I have received “Praetorian Prefect” from the correction in Cuiacius 2, 2*. The manuscript of Cuiacius 1 reads “Praes.”; Gothofredus likewise, but Gothofredus, in his note, has Florianus as Praetorian Prefect of the East, or at least governor or proconsul of Asia. Ritter, Ritter’s second edition, and Besseler read “Prefect.” Moreover, this title, in red, begins the second page of folio 73 of the manuscript.]

To veterans who obtained discharge from the fifth day before the Nones of July, when the first victory through Thrace shone upon the whole world, and to those who subsequently obtained discharge at our Nicomedia, we have granted by edict certain privileges: namely, permission for them to write these matters on tablets, or to set them down in ink and white lead. [Note: “[Col. 0151C] *b* The manuscript reads *Traciam victuria universo urbi inl.*—“through Thrace, victory shone upon the whole city.” Gothofredus notes: “Others say ‘at Chalcedon,’ which comes to the same thing.” Gothofredus is speaking not about manuscripts or interpreters of this passage, but about writers on Roman affairs.] [Note: “[Col. 0151C] *c* Some have removed *nostram* (“our”); see Gothofredus, *Chronology*, p. 14. It must, however, be construed with “at Nicomedia.” Shortly afterward the manuscript reads *eruerunt* for *meruerunt*.] [Note: “[Col. 0151C] *d* Gothofredus, Reinesius, and Besseler direct that one should read *scribi licentia*, and correctly so.]

We have sent the edict containing our grant to your devotedness, so that both your devotion and all others may recognize what we have bestowed upon those mentioned. Posted on the fourth day before the Ides of April, in the consulship of Licinius for the fifth time and Crispus Caesar (318). [Note: “[Col. 0151C–D] *e* Thus Besseler emended from the manuscript; Gothofredus correctly. Editions before Besseler read, in inverted order, *et ut*. Reinesius wishes *dignatio* in place of *dicatio*.] [Note: “[Col. 0151C–D] *f* That the subscription should be restored as ‘Posted on the fourth day before the Ides of April, at Cyzicus, in the consulship of Constantine III and Crispus III, Caesars’ (324), is shown by Gothofredus in his commentary on this constitution and in his *Chronology*, pp. 14 and 24; Petavius, *Doctrina Temporum*, vol. II, book XI, ch. 43; Pagius, *Critica* on the years 316, 317, and 318; and Reinesius in his notes at this passage. Valesius also observed that the received subscription is false, adding the reason that Constantine did not come to Nicomedia until after Licinius had been defeated. See Gothofredus’s commentary and Ritter’s notes appended to it; Reland, p. 300; and Petavius and Pagius in the two cited passages. The number of the year is absent in Gothofredus.]

## CONCERNING PARRICIDE

[Note: “[Col. 0151D] *g* Manuscript 4 and Tilius–Lugdunensis: ‘Concerning Parricides.’ Is ‘Concerning Parricides’ preferable? Sichardus correctly has ‘Concerning Parricide,’ and below *paricidii* (“of parricide”). Cuiacius 2, 2 has *patricidii*. Title 15 has ‘Concerning Assassins’; the copyist has confused the rubrics of this and the preceding title. See the preceding title, ‘On the Lex Cornelia concerning Assassins,’ note h. Manuscript 21 has *parrhicidio*; manuscript 38, *paracidio*. The Code of Justinian: ‘Concerning those who kill parents or children.’ Manuscript 37 omits the rubric.]

### 1. The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Verinus, Vicar of Africa

[Note: “[Col. 0151D] *h* Manuscript 15: Verrinus; manuscript 25: Virum; several manuscripts: Virinum.] [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *a* Manuscripts 9 and 42 omit ‘Africae’; manuscripts 10 and 18 have ‘to the distinguished man of Africa.’]

If anyone hastens the death of a parent or child, or indeed of a person bound to him by that affection which is embraced under the name of parricide, whether he has attempted this secretly or openly, he shall not be subjected to the sword, to fire, or to any other customary punishment; rather, sewn into a sack, he shall be enclosed amid its deadly narrow confines in the company of serpents, and, as the nature of the country permits, shall be cast either into the neighboring sea or into a river, so that, while living, he begins to be deprived of the use of all the elements: so that heaven may be taken from him while he survives, and earth when he is dead. [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *b* The Code of Justinian omits *in* (“upon”).] [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *c* Manuscripts 6–8, 10, and 18: ‘parents’—likewise manuscript 21—‘or children,’ with manuscript 8 omitting *aut*, ‘or’; manuscript 7 has *omnia* for *omnino*. Manuscripts 12 and 14: ‘all affection of that kind’; manuscript 20: ‘parents or children.’] [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *d* Manuscripts 10, 12, 18, and 20 read *facta* (“deeds”), as do certain editions of the Code of Justinian. See Dirksen, cited passage, p. 486.] [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *e* Manuscripts 6–8, 10, 14, 16, and 18: *innisus*; Sichardus: *enixus*. The Code of Justinian reads: ‘if he has attempted it, let him be punished with the penalty for parricide’; manuscript 10 reads *gladium* (“sword”).] [Note: “[Col. 0152B] *f* Besseler printed ‘to any other customary punishment,’ apparently taken from Sichardus and the Code of Justinian. We follow manuscript 4, Bruns, Alciatus, and the manuscripts from Tilius through Ritter: *ulla alia solenni poena*. Manuscript 15 has *pompa* for *poena*; manuscript 9 has *ulla alia*, erroneously. Sichardus omits *alia*. Manuscript 14 has *subjungitur*; manuscripts 9 and 16, *subjungetur*; manuscript 21 omits *sed*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *g* Sichardus notes in the margin: ‘Elsewhere: sewn into a sack with a dog, a cock, a viper, and an ape, from the Code of Justinian,’ where the words ‘with a dog,’ etc., are inserted after *culeo*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *h* Manuscript 4, Tilius, Cuiacius 1, Cuiacius 2 through Besseler: *culleo*. Some manuscripts have *colleo*. Manuscript 14 omits *et*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *i* Sichardus and the Code of Justinian read *eas* (“those”); Aur. and Lugdunensis, *feralas* (“deadly”).] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *j* Manuscript 20: *comprehensum serpentem*, “an enclosed serpent.”] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *k* Manuscript 16: *ut et*; manuscript 20 has the corrupt fragment *misc. ut se religionis* (‘be mixed … so that himself/of religion’ [meaning uncertain]); manuscript 14 omits from *et* through *projiciatur*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *l* Manuscript 4 and the witnesses from Tilius through Ritter omit *in*, but it was added in manuscript 4 by a later hand. Compare Cicero, *Pro Roscio Amerino*, ch. 26.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *m* Manuscript 15, Sichardus, and the Code of Justinian: *et ei*; manuscripts 10 and 18: ‘while living, of use—while surviving’; manuscript 20: ‘of the use of the elements—while surviving.’]

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the consulship of Licinius for the fifth time and Crispus Caesar (318). Received on the day before the Ides of March at Carthage, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *n* Manuscript 4, Tilius–Lugdunensis, the Code of Justinian XI.9, and manuscripts 20, 29, 30, 32–34, 38, and 42 read the fifteenth day before the Kalends; the Epitome Monacensis, L. R. U., reads the seventeenth.] [Note: “[Col. 0152C] *o* Manuscripts 15 and 44 read September. Shortly afterward Aur. and Lugdunensis have *Cons.*, and this is absent from the Code of Justinian; manuscript C omits the words after *Crispo*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *p* In the manuscripts of Bruns and Alciatus and in Sichardus, the consuls of the year 318 are absent; in manuscript 4 and in Tilius–Lugdunensis, the words from ‘Received’ through ‘consuls’ are omitted.] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *q* Manuscripts 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18 read ‘the third day.’] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *r* The city name is absent in manuscript 13 and 20; manuscript 28 has *Grat.* in its place; Cuiacius 2 through Ritter have Carthage. In what follows, copyists of manuscripts A, V, C, A.V., or C variously omit the names or the words *Augusto* or *Caesare*. Manuscript 21 has ‘in the consulship of Caesar Licinius’; manuscript 38, ‘Licinius, count and consul’; manuscript 44, Crispus in place of Licinius. Some manuscripts write Lycinio or Licinnio.]

### Interpretation

If anyone kills his father, mother, brother, sister, son, daughter, or other relatives, all other kinds of torments being set aside, a sack shall be made of hides, called a *culeus*; once he has been put into it, serpents shall also be shut in with him; and, if there is no sea nearby, he shall be thrown into any deep water, so that one condemned to such a penalty shall never obtain burial. [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *s* ‘Brother’ is absent from the editions, but occurs in most manuscripts, apparently with Ritter’s approval.] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *t* Many manuscripts add ‘or.’] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *u* This is the reading of most manuscripts. Some read ‘or any others,’ and shortly afterward ‘has killed.’ The editions read ‘or others.’] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *v* Manuscript 20: ‘all kinds of evils being removed, a sack made of hides.’ The editions read *coreis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0152D] *x* Manuscripts 6, 8, and others: *appellatur*, “is called.”] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *a* The manuscripts read ‘in which, when sent’ or ‘committed,’ and disturb the order of the words. Read: ‘when he has been put into it.’] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *b* *Cum* is absent in many manuscripts.]

## WHERE FISCAL CASES OR CASES OF THE DIVINE HOUSEHOLD …

The same Augustus to Bulephorus, *rationalis* of the chief treasury. We determine that your gravity ought to act as adjudicator for imperial coloni and those belonging to the patrimony. For military commanders, commanders of soldiers and of forts, and provincial governors must refrain from summoning and compelling the attendance of coloni. Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Licinius. (From the Code of Justinian.)

In the year of the Lord 319, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar.

## CONCERNING ACCUSATIONS

Constantine Augustus to Januarinus. … Whoever, from the day on which he has been summoned as a defendant in court, refuses to appear for trial within the space of a year, let his property be claimed for the fisc; and if he is afterward found and discovered guilty, let him be subjected to a harsher sentence. But even if he is able to clear his innocence by manifest arguments and clear proof, nevertheless his property shall remain with the fisc. [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *c* The rank of Januarinus is absent also in the Code of Justinian. According to Gothofredus, add ‘Proconsul of Achaia’; according to Reinesius, ‘Praetorian Vicar.’ But see *Theodosian Code* IX.37.1, note n. Manuscript 4 and the editions read *Januarium*. I restore *Januarinum*. See *Theodosian Code* IX.21.2, note y; IX.34.3, note u; IX.37.1, note n.] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *d* The Code of Justinian: *severiori* (“more severe”).] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *e* Manuscript 4 and Gothofredus through Ritter: *etsi*; Gothofredus in the note: *et si*.] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *f* The letters *it* were cut away in manuscript 4 at the beginning of folio 1.] [Note: “[Col. 0153C] *g* The Code of Justinian: ‘if he has cleared himself, nevertheless.’]

Given on the Ides of January. Received on the fifth day before the Kalends of August at Corinth, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0153C–D] *h* The Code of Justinian likewise has January. Gothofredus and Ritter prefer June, since it is scarcely believable that this constitution should have reached Corinth only in the seventh month.] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *i* Besseler: *Corinthi*. The Code of Justinian omits the words from ‘Received’ through ‘Corinth.’] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *j* Tilius–Lugdunensis: *Licinnio*.]

## CONCERNING SORCERERS, ASTROLOGERS, AND OTHER PERSONS OF THE SAME KIND

[Note: “[Col. 0153D] *k* Many manuscripts and Tilius through Ritter read ‘Concerning Sorceries’; but Gothofredus already approved ‘Concerning Sorcerers.’ In manuscripts 6, 7, 9, 10, 18, 21, 31, and 39, and in the editions of Sichardus—also in the title-index—Aur. and Lugdunensis omit *et*, “and.” Manuscript 15 has ‘and similar persons’; manuscripts 8 and 37, ‘others and astrologers.’] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *l* Manuscript 4 and Tilius–Lugdunensis, both here and in the title-index: ‘and persons similar to these.’ Sichardus’s title-index has ‘etc.’ and omits *similibus*. Several manuscripts have an overwritten reading for ‘and other similar persons.’]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Maximus. No *haruspex* shall approach another’s threshold, nor on any other pretext; rather, even long-standing friendship with persons of this kind shall be rejected. The *haruspex* who enters another’s house shall be burned alive; and the person who has summoned him by persuasion or reward shall, after confiscation of his goods, be sent to an island. [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *m* The rank is absent both here and in the Code of Justinian. Gothofredus and Besseler direct that ‘Urban Prefect’ be added.] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *n* Folio 22 of manuscript 4.] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *o* Manuscript 4 has *se*, but *sed* was restored by an earlier hand.] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *p* *Quamvis vetus*, ‘however old,’ is enclosed in brackets in the editions from Tilius through Lugdunensis.] [Note: “[Col. 0153D] *q* Gothofredus: ‘and he who.’]

Those who wish to serve their own superstition may publicly perform their proper rite. We judge that the accuser of this crime is not an informer, but rather is worthy of a reward. [Note: “[Col. 0154B] *a* Ritter separates the words incorrectly; the text has been corruptly transmitted.] [Note: “[Col. 0154B] *b* Manuscript 4: *adoptionem*, an error for *ademptionem*, “confiscation.”]

Posted on the Kalends of February at Rome, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0154B–C] *c* The Code of Justinian likewise has February. Since laws addressed to Maximus, Urban Prefect, are found only from the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November in this year onward—see *Theodosian Code* III.17.1, note y—Gothofredus emends February to September or November, and Besseler to November or December. Both are wrong, because the constitution would then be later than the following one. I therefore think that only fragments of a larger subscription, such as we had in constitution 1 of the preceding title, survive through the carelessness of the compilers of constitutions. Perhaps this constitution was issued in 319 but posted under the consuls of the following year. The day upon which the law was issued was omitted, and the day on which it was posted retained, while the consuls of the preceding year were nonetheless preserved. Hence the confusion in the subscription.]

## CONCERNING NOTICE OR THE PRODUCTION OF PLEADINGS

[Note: “[Col. 0154C] *d* Most manuscripts and Sichardus read ‘Concerning Ediction’ or ‘Ediccione’; manuscript 15, ‘Indiction’; manuscripts 10 and 18 omit ‘or Production.’]

### 1. The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Symmachus

If a suit is to be brought against minors or young adults, or if a claim is to be instituted by the minors or young adults themselves against anyone, the running of time shall not begin otherwise than after formal notice, according to established practice, has been given to all who are bound by the responsibility of their office—that is, to tutors appointed either by testament or decree, or to curators through whom minors are defended; or after notice has been given to all these persons. [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *e* Sichardus adds ‘Barroniatus’; manuscripts 20 and 21, ‘Barroniacus.’ Many other manuscripts have Simmacus or Simmachus. Valesius adds ‘Proconsul of Achaia.’ The Code of Justinian: ‘The Emperors Constantine and Licinius Caesars to S.’ See *Theodosian Code* III.17.1, note x, and Reland, cited passage, p. 302.] [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *f* Sichardus, in correction, proposes *adolescentibus*, “young persons.”] [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *g* Manuscript 21: *velut*; manuscript 15 omits ‘a suit shall be brought’ and ‘minors or young adults’; manuscript 16: *inlaeserit*.] [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *h* Manuscript 15: ‘a claim is brought against anyone’; manuscript 8: ‘a claim has injured anyone.’] [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *i* Manuscript 9 and Sichardus: *alius* for *alias*.] [Note: “[Col. 0154C] *j* Cuiacius 1 through Cuiacius 2, in the margin: ‘at the proper times.’] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *k* Aur. and Lugdunensis: ‘without—without’; manuscripts 9 and 16: ‘tutors appointed by testament.’] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *l* Manuscripts 5, 7, 10, 14, 16, and 21: *dati sunt*, ‘have been appointed’; manuscript 8: *dictata sint*; the editions: *sint*; manuscript 15: *datis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *m* Manuscripts 10 and 18: *minoribus*.] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *n* Manuscript 15: ‘defended, if notice has been given to them too,’ omitting ‘all.’] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *o* Manuscript 16 omits *lis*; manuscript R: *insinuata*, “has been notified.”]

§ 1. But if the responsibility of administration is divided among provinces, notice must be given to all such persons only, and the suit must be brought by those who exercise the office of guardianship or curatorship in that province, lest defenders of minors be brought to court from other provinces. [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *p* The second constitution in the cited Code of Justinian begins with the syllable *si*.] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *q* Gothofredus and Ritter: *divisim*, “severally.”] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *r* Sichardus: *tamen*, “nevertheless.”] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *s* Manuscripts 20 and 21 and Sichardus: *inferre litem*, “to bring the suit”; manuscript 15: *inferre legem*, “to bring the law.”] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *t* Cuiacius 1a and Cuiacius 2, 2, in the margin: *nec*. Manuscripts 6, 7, 10, 14, and 16–18, and R: ‘lest [defenders] from other provinces’; manuscripts 5, 15, 19, and the Code of Justinian: ‘concerning others’; manuscripts 20, 21, and the editions: ‘other provinces.’] [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *u* Manuscript 8, after a blank space, omits *producantur*; manuscripts 6, 7, and 17–21, and R, read *perducantur*, “be led”; manuscript 15, *pertrahantur*, “be dragged.”]

Given on the day before the Nones of February at Sirmium. Received on the eighth day before the Ides of March at Corinth, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0154D] *v* Manuscript 33: ‘Given on 9 February’; manuscript 40: ‘Given on the Kalends of March’; manuscript 8: ‘Given on the third day before the Nones’; manuscript 15: ‘Given on the second,’ omitting *Non.*; others omit *pridie*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155B] *a* Manuscripts 20 and 21: Firmum; Sichardus, Cuiacius 1, Aur., and Lugdunensis: Firmium. Most manuscripts, however, have Sirmium, as do Tilius, Cuiacius 2 through Ritter; Besseler and W.: Sirmii; or Syrmium. Manuscripts 24 and 30 omit *pridie* and Sirmium; manuscript 26 omits from ‘Received’ through ‘and’; another manuscript ends at ‘Sirmium—Corinth.’] [Note: “[Col. 0155B] *b* Manuscripts 8, 9, 16, and 19–21, with Sichardus, read the seventh day.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *c* Editions before Besseler and many manuscripts: Corintho; the remaining manuscripts: Chorinto or Corinto.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *d* Manuscript 8: Constantio.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *e* Editions before Besseler omit ‘Caesar.’]

### Interpretation

If anyone happens to bring a suit against persons under age, or if a defendant is charged on their behalf, time is to be counted from the point at which the minor’s tutor or curator has, either through a judge or through the municipal council, brought or received the action. Yet if persons holding this office—that is, curators or tutors who protect the causes of minors—are in different provinces, those who are in the same province where the claim is shown to have arisen shall themselves bring or receive the actions; for we do not wish defenders of minors to be taken to another province for the necessity of a hearing. This has been added concerning the law. [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *f* Manuscript 5 omits *aliquis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *g* Sichardus, in the margin: *vel*, “or.”] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *h* Some manuscripts read ‘perhaps—plainly—at the time—minors.’] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *i* Sichardus, Cuiacius 1, and Aur.–Lugdunensis omit *aut*; manuscript 20 then reads *ut*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *j* Many manuscripts, Sichardus, Cuiacius 1, and Aur.–Lugdunensis have *istius modi homines*, “persons of this kind”; but the margins of Sichardus, Cuiacius 1, and Aur.–Lugdunensis preserve *istius officii*, “of this office.”] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *k* Some witnesses have *cultores* for *curatores* and *tuentur* for *tueantur*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *l* Manuscript 20, with other manuscripts and Sichardus, has *fuerit*, singular.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *m* Manuscript 20: *proturbatur* for *probatur*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *n* Manuscript 5: *volumus*, “we wish.”] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *o* The words following survive in manuscripts 5–10, 12–14, and 16–19; they end in the remaining manuscripts and in Sichardus.]

## CONCERNING REPORTS TO THE EMPEROR

Constantine Augustus to Profuturus, Prefect of the Grain Supply. If any judge considers that a report should be made, let him pronounce nothing; rather, concerning the point on which he judges that he must hesitate, let him consult our knowledge. Or, if he has given judgment, let him not afterward frighten the litigants, lest an appeal be made from him, by promising a report. [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *p* The Code of Justinian: ‘The Emperor Constantine Augustus—let him pronounce nothing between the parties.’] [Note: “[Col. 0155C] *q* Manuscript 4 and editions before Besseler, following the Code of Justinian: *ex quo*.] [Note: “[Col. 0155C–D] *r* The Code of Justinian: *praemissa*, “previously sent”; Gothofredus prints this, but Halaeus correctly retains *promissa*, “promised.”] [Note: “[Col. 0155D] *s* The Code of Justinian continues: ‘knowing that, if he does this, the case will nonetheless be pursued by right of appeal. Nor should anything be sent to us which requires full instruction. Whenever a judge promises to refer a matter to our knowledge, he shall immediately order a copy of the consultation to be issued to the litigants in the official records, so that, if anyone perhaps considers the report insufficient or contradictory, he may likewise submit refutatory petitions in the records without any dilatory delay.’ These words have been taken, with altered wording, from constitution 1 of the following title.]

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of February at Sirmium, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0155D] *t* The Code of Justinian: ‘Kalends.’] [Note: “[Col. 0155D] *u* Besseler and the Code of Justinian: Sirmii. Shortly afterward the Code omits ‘Caesar.’]

## CONCERNING THE SONS OF MILITARY ATTENDANTS AND VETERANS

[Note: “[Col. 0155D] *v* Cuiacius 1 through Ritter’s second edition, in the title-index: ‘of military officials and attendants.’ The Code of Justinian: ‘Concerning the sons of military officials who die in war.’ This title in red begins folio 78 of the manuscript.]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Optavianus. We order that the sons of veterans who are fit for military service—some of whom, through idleness, refuse the performance of military duties, while others are so cowardly that they seek to evade the obligation of service through bodily mutilation—if, after their fingers have been cut off, they are judged unfit for military service, shall without any ambiguity be assigned to the duties and services of curials. [Note: “[Col. 0155D–0156C] *x* Gothofredus emends *Optavianum* to *Octavianum*, who was Corrector of Lucania and Bruttium in this year. See *Theodosian Code* XVI.2.2.]

Given on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of March at Sirmium. Received on the seventh day before the Ides of April at Rhegium, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *a* Thus the manuscript and Cuiacius 1 through Ritter’s second edition; Besseler: Sirmii.] [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *b* Thus the manuscript and Cuiacius 1 through Ritter’s second edition; Besseler: Regii. Shortly afterward Aur., Lugdunensis, and Gothofredus have *Cons.*]

## CONCERNING VACANT PROPERTY

Constantine Augustus to Priscus, *Rationalis*. Lest anyone, forestalled by imperial generosity, seek ownership of another’s property, we order that whenever, by legal warrant, the property of any persons has been seized through your office, the fullest inventories thereof shall be sent to the most perfect count and our friend, so that they may not be diminished through the frauds of Caesarian officials, nor anything be denied to petitioners. A penalty is prescribed against the *rationalis* and his office if he permits a petitioner to possess beforehand that which has been granted to him, before the aforesaid inventories have been produced. [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *c* Manuscript I: *comet* for *comitem*.] [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *d* Tilius through Cuiacius 2, 2*: *prius, quam*; Gothofredus through Ritter’s second edition: *prius quam*.]

Given on the fifth day before the Ides of March at Sirmium, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *e* Folio 87 of manuscript 4. Shortly afterward Besseler: Sirmii.]

## CONCERNING COUNTERFEIT COINAGE

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Verinus. Whoever makes counterfeit coins shall suffer punishment according to the distinction of sex and the difference in his condition: that is, if he is a decurion or the son of a decurion, he shall be banished from his native soil and sent, under the condition of perpetual exile, to any city situated at a distance; and a report concerning his property shall be made to our knowledge. If he is a plebeian, let him, after loss of his property, be consigned to perpetual condemnation; if he is of servile condition, let him be subjected to the ultimate punishment. [Note: “[Col. 0156C] *f* Reinesius adds ‘Urban Prefect’; Gothofredus, ‘Vicar of Africa.’ See above IX.15.1.] [Note: “[Col. 0156D] *g* Manuscripts 1 and 4 and Tilius through Ritter’s second edition: *nomismata*.] [Note: “[Col. 0156D] *h* Tilius erroneously has *faculatibus*.] [Note: “[Col. 0156D] *i* Besseler correctly explains: ‘that is, to the mines; Godefroy’s emendation *deportationi* must not be admitted,’ although the ancient summaries of the Theodosian Code, edited by me at Leipzig in 1834, octavo, p. 5, confirm the alternative reading: ‘if a plebeian, let him be consigned to perpetual exile.’]

Given and received on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0156D] *j* Thus manuscript 4 and the editions before Besseler. Besseler places three dots between *Dat. et* and says, not implausibly for his chronology: ‘and seems to be deleted. For issue and receipt could not have occurred on the same day; the day of issue has fallen out.’ At that time Constantine was at Sirmium in Pannonia, Verinus at Carthage. Besseler therefore correctly marked a lacuna; I would have followed him in marking it, had I not preferred to reproduce the manuscript. The true reading seems to lie concealed in manuscript I, which has *pp. id.* in place of ‘Received on the fifteenth day before the Kalends.’ I therefore think that the original copyist wrote: ‘Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April and posted—or received—on the Ides of April.’]

## CONCERNING DEFAMATORY LIBELS

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Verinus, Vicar of Africa. Whenever infamous libels are found, those whose acts or names they contain shall suffer no calumny therefrom; rather, the author of the writing shall be sought out, and, once found, shall be compelled with all rigor to prove the matters which he thought should be alleged. Nor, even if he establishes something, shall he be exempted from punishment. [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *a* Manuscripts 14, 16, 38, and 42: Virinum; manuscripts 20, 32, 39, and 43: Valerianum, incorrectly printed by Ritter; manuscript 26: Clarianum. Certain manuscripts omit ‘of Africa.’ Gothofredus: ‘The Emperors.’] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *b* Manuscript 20: *fabelli*, but *famosi libelli* has been restored above the line. Shortly afterward manuscript 4 and Sichardus through Ritter: *hii*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *c* Manuscript 8: ‘all’; manuscript 20: ‘their conduct,’ approved by Besseler; manuscript 21: ‘and names’; Sichardus: ‘and their names.’] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *d* Many manuscripts: *inscriptionis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *e* Manuscript 20: ‘these matters,’ omitting *de*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *f* Manuscripts 18 and 25: ‘which he believed should be composed’; manuscript 12: ‘believed.’] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *g* Manuscript 8: ‘nor with such punishment’; manuscript 13 omits *nec*; manuscript 25: ‘if he proves, nor’; manuscript 16: *ostenderint*.]

Posted on the fourth day before the Kalends of April at Carthage, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *h* Manuscripts 28, 36, and 42: *Dat.*; manuscripts 6, 7, 10, 12–16, 18, 20, 31, 32, 34, 38, 39, and 43; Cuiacius 2, 2*; and Gothofredus: ‘third’; some manuscripts omit ‘fourth’ and, in what follows, either Augustus, Augustus V, or Caesar. Manuscript 8 omits from ‘Carthage’ through ‘and.’] [Note: “[Col. 0157C] *i* Manuscripts 6–8, 10, 12–14, 16, and 18: June.] [Note: “[Col. 0157C–D] *j* Manuscript 4 and Tilius through Ritter: *Carthag.* Many manuscripts: *Carth.*—as Besseler prints—or Cartag.; manuscript 36 omits Carthage. Subsequently some manuscripts have *Constancio*, others *Lycinio*, and Aur.–Lugdunensis has *Cons.*]

### Interpretation

Whoever writes an infamous paper to injure and stain anyone, and either secretly or publicly posts it and throws it down so that it may be found, shall not harm the person against whom the paper has been posted, nor shall it detract at all from his reputation. But if the person who made such a paper can be found, he shall be compelled to prove what he wrote. Even if he can prove what he wrote, he shall be flogged, because he preferred to defame rather than to accuse. [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *k* Sichardus, Cuiacius 1 through Lugdunensis: *chartulam*, “a little paper.”] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *l* Manuscripts 6–8 and other manuscripts: ‘has written to the injury and stain of anyone.’ Subsequently Sichardus, Cuiacius 1 through Lugdunensis read *inveniendam*, and omit *que*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *m* Very many manuscripts, including 6, 7, 10, 18, and 20, have *et*, “and”; *et* is inserted above the line in *supplicio*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *n* Manuscripts 6, 8, 20, 21, 42, and others: *illum*, “him.” A little later manuscript 20 has ‘posted and formerly someone’; manuscript 21, ‘composed.’ Many manuscripts have *derogavit*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *o* Manuscripts 6 and 7: *facit*, “makes.”] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *p* Manuscripts 6–8, 10, 18, and others read: ‘let him prove what he wrote. If he cannot prove it …,’ omitting ‘what he wrote, even if’; this is contrary to the tenor of the law. Manuscript 20: ‘who, even if he can prove what he wrote.’]

## CONCERNING APPEALS

Constantine to Bassus, Urban Prefect. The law remains in force which prescribes within how many days a judge must provide private persons with a copy of his opinion or report, and within how many days refutatory petitions must in turn be offered to judges. In both private and fiscal causes, from the day on which the issue has been decided, or from that on which the judge has promised a report by his judgment, we require that within twenty days everything which pertains to the instruction of the case be brought with the greatest speed to our court. [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *q* See constitution 1 of this title. Manuscript 4 has *quod* for *quot*; Aur. and Lugdunensis: *opinionis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *r* Folio 182 of manuscript 4. Manuscript 4 then repeats *quod* for *quot*.] [Note: “[Col. 0157D] *s* Besseler emends *sint* for *sunt*.] [Note: “[Col. 0158C] *a* Manuscript 4 and Tilius: *quecumque*, that is, ‘whichever.’ Manuscript 4 and editions before Gothofredus: *vicensimum*.]

If this is not done, we order that, from the entire office, after twenty days have elapsed—days which we have directed to be counted after judgment has been rendered—there shall be paid into our fisc, within the following twenty days, as much as the *rationalis* can most faithfully estimate to be the profit of the litigation whose instruction had been suppressed. The *rationalis* shall face capital punishment if he attempts in any manner to soften the rigor of the law.

§ 1. The same penalty being imposed upon the office, if, while an appeal or consultation is pending, or after causes have been decided by our responses, it wishes to lend blameworthy connivance to that which has been obtained in any manner. For it must bring our decrees before the judge, so as, even if the judge himself dissimulates, to resist and, as though hands had been laid upon them, draw those persons from the tribunal and, once delivered to the office of accounts, bind them with the chains of the earlier statute—those persons whose demands it has observed to violate our enactments. [Note: “[Col. 0158C] *b* Folio 183 of manuscript 4. Shortly afterward manuscript 4 and Tilius through Ritter’s second edition: *conhibentiam*; Besseler: *connibentiam*. See above VI.30.17, note v.] [Note: “[Col. 0158C] *c* Manuscript 4 has *judicantia ut*, but the *a* in *judicantia* has been deleted. Tilius: *judicantia, ut*; Cuiacius 1 through Lugdunensis: *judicantia, aut*, which Besseler incorrectly says is found in Cuiacius 2, where, rather, as also in Cuiacius 1, the reading is *judicanti, aut*. Besseler, Gothofredus, Ritter, and Ritter’s second edition: *judicanti aut*. Although Besseler’s reading gives an easier sense, I have printed the manuscript’s *ut*, that is, *uti*, ‘so as to,’ following it just as I retain *reluctari*. Or is *ut* an error for *uel*, ‘or’?] [Note: “[Col. 0158C] *d* See constitution 6 of this title.]

Posted on the fourth day before the Kalends of April at Rome, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING AN UNDUTIFUL WILL

[Note: “[Col. 0158C] *e* In the margin of manuscript 15: ‘An undutiful will is one which uselessly disinherits children contrary to the duty of natural affection.’]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Lucrius Verinus. Uterine brothers shall be excluded from actions concerning undutiful wills; but only to full brothers, against heirs instituted in the will and proved to bear the branded marks of detestable disgrace, shall access to a petition be opened without the aid of the praetor, provided that agnation continues. [Note: “[Col. 0158C] *f* Manuscript 37: ‘the Emperors Constantine and Theodosius Augustus.’] [Note: “[Col. 0158C–D] *g* Manuscript 10: Lugrius; manuscript 20: Lucrinus; manuscript 16: Lucretius Virinus; manuscript 25: Lucricius Verinus; manuscript 26: Ducarius Virinus; manuscript 27: *a Lucritium V.*; manuscript 38: ‘to L. Virinus’; manuscripts 39 and 42: ‘to Lucrum V.’; manuscript 44: Locrius V. Sichardus proposes Lucius in the margin; Tilius, Lucretio Verino in the margin. Manuscript 33 and the Code of Justinian omit Lucrius; manuscript 29: ‘to L. V.’ The manuscripts used by Gothofredus have Lucretius or Lucritius.] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *h* Add ‘Vicar of Africa’; compare constitution 1 of the title ‘Concerning Defamatory Libels,’ Gothofredus at this place and in his *Prosopography*, under Verinus. The Code of Justinian has Verino.] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *i* Manuscript 26: *eius*, “him.”] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *j* Manuscripts 6–8, 14, 18–20, 33, Sichardus, and Ritter’s second edition: *injustas*, “unjust,” in place of *inustas*, “branded.”] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *k* Manuscripts 20 and 33 and Sichardus: *constituerit*; but Sichardus’s margin supports *inustas constiterit*. Manuscripts 10 and 18: *esse const.*] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *l* Some manuscripts read *detestabiles*, “detestable”; others, *detestabili turpitudine*, “of detestable disgrace.”] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *m* Manuscript 20: *hac natione*; manuscripts 10, 15, 18, 26, and 33: *turp. agnitione*; manuscript 19: *ac actione*; Sichardus: *hac notatione*.] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *n* Some manuscripts read *durantis*, others *durantes*.] [Note: “[Col. 0158D] *o* Manuscripts 9 and 15: *auditus reseratur*, “a hearing shall be opened”; manuscript 33: *auditus recreatur*, “the hearing shall be renewed”; manuscript 26: *aditus servetur*, “access shall be preserved.”]

Given on the Ides of April at Sirmium, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *a* The Code of Justinian reads: ‘Uterine brothers or sisters shall be entirely excluded from an action concerning an undutiful will against the testament of a brother or sister. But blood relatives, whether agnation continues or not, may raise the question of an undutiful will against the testament of their brother or sister, if the instituted heirs are stained with the blemish of infamy, disgrace, or even slight disrepute; or if freedmen, who have improperly and without merit obtained their patron through the greatest benefits, have been instituted—except for a necessary slave instituted as heir.’] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *b* Thus most manuscripts and Tilius through Ritter’s second edition. Some manuscripts and Sichardus: Syrmium; Besseler and W.: Sirmii. The Code of Justinian: the Ides of August.] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *c* Many manuscripts and Sichardus through Lugdunensis omit ‘fifth.’] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *d* Manuscripts 6–8, 14, and 16: Vicinio.] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *e* Many manuscripts have ‘V. C.’; some have *et*; Tilius omits ‘Caesar.’]

### Interpretation

Uterine brothers—that is, those born of different fathers but of one mother—may not bring an action concerning an undutiful will against the testament of a brother. But if brothers born of one father have been passed over, and the inheritance has been left to disgraceful persons—that is, either to prostitutes through lust, to natural children through dishonorable affection, to actors (*thymelici*), or to one’s own freedmen—the right to bring an action against the will is reserved; provided, however, that that same brother on the father’s side has not been assigned to exile for his own crime, has not become a slave through captivity, and has not lost the rights of succession or action through emancipation. [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *f* Manuscripts 20 and 42, and Sichardus, add *de*, “concerning.”] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *g* Manuscript 20: *effectu* for *affectu*.] [Note: “[Col. 0159C] *h* Manuscripts 6, 7, 20, and many others, with Sichardus: *temelicis*; Cuiacius 1 and Aur.–Lugdunensis: *timelicis*.] [Note: “[Col. 0159D] *i* Some manuscripts, Sichardus, Cuiacius 1, and Aur.–Lugdunensis omit *de*, “or.”]

## CONCERNING THEIR PRIVILEGES
Idem A. to Rufinus, Praetorian Prefect. [Note: [Col. 0159D] j Codex: PPO. Cui. 1, Ri.: Praepositum; Go., conjecturally, *abjecta sua ipsius*: “Prefect of the Bedchamber” proposed; “Praetorian Prefect,” received by Be., is supported not only by Cod. Just. and the writing of the Lugdunensis manuscript, but also by other laws of this year, and had already been corrected by Go. in Corr. Cui. 2, 2. In c. 3 Cod. Just. cited, *ad Rufinum Pf. P.* appears as *ad Numphidium PP.*, doubtless erroneously. Moreover see above, c. 1 *On Betrothals* (III, 5), note l; Wenck on the same c. 1, note z.] We wish those granted exemption from service in our bedchambers [Col. 0159B], or in the various palatine services, or in the bureaux of records, letters, and petitions, or in the office of the comital largesses or of the individual cities, and likewise in the office of admissions, to enjoy the privileges of our laws, so that neither they themselves nor their sons nor grandsons may be summoned to the curia, to honours, burdens, or [Note: [Col. 0159D] k Be., from Cod. Just., adds *vel*, absent from the manuscript and Cui. 1–Ri.; Go. in the commentary: *munerave*] municipal offices.

And deservedly we join with these [Note: [Col. 0159D] l Thus the manuscript; the editions read *ingerimus*, wrongly (see § 3 of this constitution). Go., Ri.: *Metitoque*, an error. A little later the manuscript wrongly has *copulatuit*; the second page of fol. 41 begins with the words *trensi militant*.] the officials of the largesses of the individual cities, lest those whom an almost similar rank has joined should be separated in privilege—for the aforesaid belong to the registers of the palatine officials—since they serve under the military establishment. To all these we grant remission from undertaking the duty of exactors or *turmarii* [Note: [Col. 0159D] m Reinesius conjectures *temoniarorum*. The manuscript reads *capitularius*.], whom they call *capitularii*, or the service of *temoniarii* or of *prototypia* [Note: [Col. 0159D] n Cod. Just.: *pentaprotiae*.].

[Col. 0160A] For they are so worthy of our benefits that, even if after palatine service anyone should attain various administrative offices, he must enjoy the same privileges [Note: [Col. 0160B] a Cui. 1, Ri.: *hisdem*. Aur. and Lugd. have *perveverit*, an error.], since no higher dignity [Note: [Col. 0160B] b The words *major … facere* were transferred into c. 3 of Cod. Just. cited, which is worded thus: “No higher dignity ought to prejudice the privileges of an earlier dignity or service,” and thereafter follows the subscription of this constitution.] ought to cause prejudice.

§ 1. Therefore none of the sons of the aforesaid persons, nor slaves acquired through the military peculium [Note: [Col. 0160C] c Manuscript, Cui. 1, Lugd.: *cumquisitis*.], shall be entered in the professions subject to the census, nor substituted in the place of the additional number or of those lacking [Note: [Col. 0160C] d Go. corrected *locove*, rightly.], unless he has been enrolled in the census registers.

§ 2. Let them also be free from personal and bodily public services, whether they are still serving in the palace or have been granted their desired repose [Note: [Col. 0160C] e Thus Be. from Cod. Just.; manuscript, Cuj. 1, Ri.: *sunt*.].

§ 3. To all these privileges we join the *agentes in rebus*, although they are seen to be supported by military merits [Note: [Col. 0160C] f Above, the manuscript wrongly reads *corpolibus muner.* The reading *meritis*, absent from Cuj. 2 and Be. and not in Cod. Just., ought, in my judgment, to be restored from Cui. 1 and Lugd., especially since Cujacius in his commentary, p. 467, reports this reading of the Theodosian Code; hence Go. notes unnecessarily: “namely, by privileges.” In fact the manuscript has *V. meritis*.] [Note: [Col. 0160C] g In Cod. Just. this constitution, with other changes, additions, and omissions, reads as follows: “We wish that the palatine officials, also the record-keepers entered in the bureaux of records, letters, petitions, and sacred dispositions, and also all serving in either office of the palatine officials of the comital largesses or of the cities, in the office of admissions, and in the military establishment of the sacred palace, shall have the privileges that neither they themselves … nor their sons or grandsons are summoned to honours or municipal offices” (omitting “And deservedly … they serve”). “Let them undertake neither the care of *temoniarii* or *pentaprotia*, nor even the presentation of recruits. For they are so worthy of our benefits … that they shall also be free from census obligations and from personal and bodily services, and shall have military peculium, whether they still serve in the palace or have received desired,” etc.].

Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of May at Sirmium [Note: [Col. 0160D] h Thus manuscript, Cui. 1–Ri*; Be. and Cod. Just.: Sirmii. Aur. and Lugd. shortly afterward: Licino.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING THE REPAIR OF ROADS

[Note: [Col. 0160D] i See title I of this book, note aa.]

[Col. 0160B]

The Emperor [Note: [Col. 0160D] j 4, Til.–Go., Cod. Just. add *Imp.*; Ri.–Be. omit it.] Constantine Augustus to Proculus, Proconsul of Africa. Possessors under emphyteusis, who by the favour of our clemency are not summoned to extraordinary obligations, shall nevertheless, like [Note: [Col. 0160D] k Cod. Just.: “are not summoned to public services, just as”; Go. does not maintain that our text is false. Above, manuscript 4: *Enfyteuticarii*.] the other provincials, devote their service to repairing roads [Note: [Col. 0160D] l Cod. Just.: “to roads needing repair.”]; for they ought in no way to be separated from that which [Note: [Col. 0160D] m 4: *quo*, corrected in red ink to *quod*.] will benefit all in common [Note: [Col. 0160D] n Cod. Just. has *sejungi* in place of *esse sejuncti*, and shortly afterward Carthage.].

Posted on the Nones of May at Carthage, in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING THE CORRECTION OF SLAVES

[Col. 0161A]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus [Note: [Col. 0161B] a Add: Urban Prefect.] … If a master has beaten a slave with rods or thongs [Note: [Col. 0161B] b Peyron, cited work, p. 187, says: “Law I can scarcely be read; yet what is visible agrees with the edition” (Ri*).] [Note: [Col. 0161B] c Cod. Just.: *loris dom. serv.*], or has put him in chains for the sake of custody [Note: [Col. 0161B] d Thus Be. from Cod. Just.; 4, Til.–Ri*: *vincla*.], he shall, if the slave dies, incur no fear of criminal liability, the distinction or interpretation of days being set aside [Note: [Col. 0161C] e Cod. Just.: “the slave having died, he shall bear no fear,” etc.].

Yet he must not use his right without restraint; but he shall then be guilty of homicide if he kills him intentionally [Note: [Col. 0161C] f Fol. 18 of manuscript 4.] or [Note: [Col. 0161C] g *Vel* is absent from Cod. Just.] with the blow of a club or stone; or, using a weapon, inflicts a mortal wound; or orders him to be hanged by a noose; or gives the savage order that he be thrown headlong; or administers the poison of venom; or rends his body by public punishments, cutting his sides with the tracks of beasts [Note: [Col. 0161C] h Go. conjectures *ferrearum* or *ferratarum*.] [Note: [Col. 0161C] i Cod. Just.: claws.] or burning his limbs with applied [Note: [Col. 0161C] j Cod. Just.: offered.] fires; or by a cruelty worthy of savage barbarians compels his wasting limbs, flowing with foul matter mingled with black blood [Note: [Col. 0161C] k Petrus Faber, Sem. III, 16, judged that the words *atro sanguine* should be deleted, as though introduced into the text from the interpretation’s *sanies*. Go. rightly objects to him; see note r. Aur. and Lugd.: *tabebescentes*.], to leave life almost amid the very torments [Col. 0161B] [Note: [Col. 0161C] l Cod. Just.: *relinquere*.] [Note: [Col. 0161C] m Aur. and Lugd. wrongly: *barborum*; 4: *varbarorum*, corrected in red to *barbarorum*.].

Given [Note: [Col. 0161C] n According to Go., read “issued” in place of “given,” since Constantine was not at Rome in this year; see Chronicle in Go., p. 17.] on the fifth day before the Ides of May at Rome, in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0161C] o The numeral is absent from Cod. Just.; Ri. prints 312.] and the consulship of Licinius (319).

## CONCERNING PACTS AND SETTLEMENTS

[Note: [Col. 0161C] p 1, P.: “Settlements.” 15 and the Old Collection of Jurists omit “and Settlements.” 8: “Concerning Pacts and Transferred Actions.” Cui. 1, in the titles’ index: “settlements.”]

The Emperor Constantine to Rufinus, Praetorian Prefect. After other matters: We do not permit lawsuits terminated by judgments or settlements [Note: [Col. 0161D] q 1: *Tra. actionibus P. tra(ns)actionibus*.] to be reopened.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of May [Note: [Col. 0161D] r Perhaps add “at Sirmium”; see c. 1, C.
