Th., *On Betrothals* (III, 5).], in the fifth consulship of the Augustus himself and [Note: [Col. 0161D] s The following words, “Licinius Caesar, consuls,” cut off in manuscript 1, are restored by P.] the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## TITLE V. CONCERNING BETROTHALS AND GIFTS BEFORE MARRIAGE

[Note: [Col. 0161D] t Many manuscripts and Till.: “marriage”; others: “marriages”; but shortly afterward, “a nuptial gift.” 5: “Concerning … marriage” || “Concerning gifts which they may give in betrothals.” Cod. Just. (V, 1): “Concerning hope, betrothal earnest-money, and matchmakers.”]

### 1.

The Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0161D] u 19 adds “and Honorius.” Some manuscripts: “Augustus to Rufinus, Praetorian Prefect”; 20: *ppu.*; 38 omits “to Rufinus, Praetorian Prefect.”] Augustus to Rufinus, Praetorian Prefect. [Note: [Col. 0161D] v Wenck vigorously opposes Go., who here and in the Prosopography thinks that this law and two other laws of this year—c. 3 C. Th. *On Their Privileges* (VI, 35), and the sole constitution C. Th. *On the Property of Decurions* (V, 2)—were wrongly attributed by the compilers of the Theodosian Code to Constantine and should rather be assigned to Constantius and dated to 352. See Reland, p. 369.]

Our father [Col. 0162A] [Note: [Col. 0162B] a 15 adds Constantine.] wished no gift to be valid unless it had been entered in the public acts [Note: [Col. 0162B] b 9: *libertatem*; 16 omits *voluit*.]. We likewise decree that, among betrothed men and women and among all persons, from the time of the promulgated law only that gift shall be valid which has been followed by certification in the public acts [Note: [Col. 0162B] c 6–8, 10, 14–16, 18–21, Cui. 2–Ri. add *quoque*, which can be tolerated. For it is opposed by *nullam*, nor is it an obstacle that “we likewise” refers to “our father.” Some manuscripts: *inter sponsis*.] [Note: [Col. 0162C] d 10, 18: *sanximus*.].

Given on the fourth [Note: [Col. 0162C] e Thus 9, 12, 19–21, 24, 33, 34, 45, Sich.; Til.–W. III; but see c. 1 C. Th. *On Pacts*, with which this law must be joined. 10, 18 omit IV.] day before the Ides of May [Note: [Col. 0162C] f Some manuscripts, Mad. 32, 36, 40: March; 10: *Marci*; Sich.: Kalends of May.] at Sirmium [Note: [Col. 0162C] g Thus manuscripts and editions, Sich.–Ri*; though some manuscripts have Sermium, others Syrmium and Firmium. Be. and W.: Sirmii.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0162C] h 21 and Sich.–Lugd. omit V.] and the consulship of Licinius Caesar [Note: [Col. 0162C] i 10: “Licinius Clarus”; 14 omits “Caesar, consuls”; 6, 7, 18, 20, 32 and Til. omit Caesar; 38: “and Licinius Caesar”; 33, 34, Sich.: “Licinius, fifth consul, Caesar, consuls”; 24: “At Sirmium, in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and …,” omitting Licinius.] (319).

**Interpretation.** Before the time of this law, gifts were valid even without certification in the public acts. But now, after this law, neither a nuptial gift nor any other [Note: [Col. 0162C] j Some manuscripts: *qualibet alias*; 20: “neither nuptial gifts nor any other”; 21: “neither nuptial gifts nor any other.”] gift between any persons, concerning any things whatever, can be valid [Note: [Col. 0162C] k 20 adds *non*.] if it has not been entered in the acts [Note: [Col. 0162D] l 20: *olligata*; 21, Sich. in margin: *alligata*, but 21 in margin: *obligata*.].

## CONCERNING MAGICIANS

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to the people. We prohibit haruspices, priests, and those accustomed to serve this rite from approaching a private [Col. 0162B] house or crossing another’s threshold under pretext of friendship, a penalty being prescribed against them if they disregard the law. But those of you who think this advantageous [Note: [Col. 0162D] m I have corrected *existimatis* for *extimatis*, which 4 and Til.–Be. have. Go. and Be. had already proposed *aestimatis* or *existimatis*.] may approach public altars and temples and celebrate the solemnities of your custom; for we do not prohibit the offices of an earlier usage from being performed openly [Note: [Col. 0162D] n In Cod. Just., c. 1 and 2 of this title are fused thus: “No haruspex, no priest, none of those accustomed to serve this rite, may approach another’s threshold … Let even long-standing human friendship be repelled … and let him who summoned him by persuasion or rewards be deported to an island after confiscation of his property. But we judge an accuser of this kind …,” followed by the subscription of c. 1 C. Th.].

Given on the Ides of May, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0162D] o Fol. 22 of manuscript 4.] and Licinius [Note: [Col. 0162D] p Be. rightly adds *Caesar*, as in the preceding constitution; Aur. and Lugd.: *Cons.*] (319).

## CONCERNING THE LAW OF THE FISC

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Severus [Note: [Col. 0162D] q 15: Severinus; 25, 38: Serum; 20, 32, 39: Senatum. This Severus is different from the one mentioned [Col. 0163B] in c. 2 C. Th. *On Maternal Property* (VIII, 18), and c. 9 C. Th. *On Appeals* (XI, 30).], Rationalis [Note: [Col. 0163B] a 17, 27, 40: *rationabilem*. Many manuscripts: Africae. Go., because this constitution is said to have been posted at Rome, prefers “rationalis of the city [Rome]” and omits *Africae* in the Chronicle. Shortly afterward “After other matters” is absent. Manuscripts 17, 36, 40 add after these words “and cited, etc.,” i.e. “and the rest.”] of Africa. After other matters: We have given certain persons estates [Col. 0163A] and slaves removed from the patrimony of the fisc [Note: [Col. 0163B] b 20: *Possessionem*.]. We wish these [Note: [Col. 0163B] c 13: “and slaves excepted”; 15: “slaves which were removed”; 21 omits *exempta*; 12: “given directly”; Sich.: “slaves of the fisc, which we have given from the patrimony, these.” Aur. and Lugd.: *patrimonia*, wrongly; 20: *exempla f. patrimonium*.] to be possessed by direct and perpetual right [Note: [Col. 0163B] d See C. Th. V, 14, 7, 20: “by ancient order.”] without any question [Note: [Col. 0163C] e 4: “all question,” corrected in red to “any”; 20, 21, Sich.: “sequestration,” but in 20 corrected to “requisition.” Many manuscripts shortly afterward: *obtinere*.], with a penalty prescribed against rationales, masters of the private property [Note: [Col. 0163C] f In manuscript 15 *privatae rei* is omitted; in the remaining Breviary of Alaric manuscripts and in Sich., *rei*, but Sich.: *privatim*, and 20: *privatos*.], and officials, should they attempt anything [Note: [Col. 0163C] g 14, 20: *qui*.] to the contrary [Note: [Col. 0163C] h The letters *rint* begin fol. 78 of manuscript 4; Sich. omits etc.].

Posted on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June [Note: [Col. 0163C] i Thus 9, 13, 24, 27, 29, 38, 42, 44, Sich.; 4, Til.–Lugd.: “Posted XVI Kalends of July.” I prefer June because of the following constitution of this title. Cui. 2–Be.: “Posted X Kalends of June,” perhaps because of c. 3 C. Th. *On Shipowners* (XIII, 5), said to have been posted nearly on the same day. 15: XV Kalends of July; 6–8, 12, 14, 16, Epit. Mon.: XIII Kalends of June; 10, 18, Anian., Reg. in Go.: XII Kalends of June; L. R. U.: “Given XV Kalends of July”; 20, 32, 39, 43: “Given XV Kalends of January”; 21: XVII Kalends of June; 17, 28, 36, 40: VI Kalends of January; 33, 34: XI Kalends of June; 38: *ag.*] at Rome, in Trajan’s Forum [Note: [Col. 0163C] j Some manuscripts: Roma; 20, 24, 28: Trojani; 32: *tuajano*. [Col. 0163D] 8 omits “in the Forum … and”; in manuscripts 17, 28, 36, 40 the names of Constantine and the consuls are absent.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0163D] k In manuscripts 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, V is absent. 34: Constantinople for Constantine.] and the consulship of Licinius Caesar [Note: [Col. 0163D] l Many manuscripts omit C. or “C., consuls”; 38: “and Licinius C.”; 24, 32: *Dic. v c Coss.* Some manuscripts: Lycinio; Aur. and Lugd.: Licino.] (319).

**Interpretation.** We desire that whatever lands and slaves are given from the right of our fisc [Note: [Col. 0163D] m 21: “our persons given.”] to whatever persons shall remain with those to whom they have been given without any suspicion, a penalty being prescribed against the administrators of the imperial estates if they are known to act contrary to the ordinance [Note: [Col. 0163D] n 20: *perscriptionem*, with *praescriptionem* written above the line.] [Note: [Col. 0163D] o 9, 20, and other manuscripts: *cognoscantur*.].

## CONCERNING SHIPOWNERS

[Col. 0163B] The Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0163D] p See preceding note.] Augustus to Amabilianus [Note: [Col. 0163D] q Cui. 2, 2: Ambilianus, wrongly. See preceding note. Go.: “the same Augusti.”], Prefect of the Annona. If any shipowner obtains immunity by deception or by any device whatever, we in no [Note: [Col. 0163D] r 4: *admitti nullo*; editions before Be.: *admitti in ullo*. Cui. 1–2, in margin: “Greek, *nullo*,” which Go. also proposed and Be. rightly received. The error arose not because the letters were wrongly divided, as B. writes, but from the preceding letter, which the scribe doubled, as Go. had already observed. Summary of C. Th.: “A shipowner does not deserve exemption.”] way permit him to be admitted to an excuse.

§ 1. Further, if anyone possesses a patrimony liable to the service of shipowner, although he be of higher rank, the privileges of his honour shall not assist him, at least in this respect; but whether for the whole or according to a proportion, he shall be liable to this service [Note: [Col. 0164C] a Cui. 2–Ri.: *teneantur*, an error.]. For it is not equitable that, when a patrimony liable to this function has been excused, not all should bear the common burden according to their due share.

Posted on the fifth [Note: [Col. 0164C] b Go. in the Chronology: “posted X Kalends.”] day before the Kalends of June at Constantinople [Note: [Col. 0164C] c This word must be deleted, having been inserted here due to the following name; for Constantinople had not yet been built. See C. Th. XI, 30, 12, note i.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING THE LAW OF THE FISC

The Emperor Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0164C] d 4, here and in the following law: “the same Augusti to.”] to the Provincials. We order that even the just and valid actions of the fisc be burned, solely because they were not brought in their proper time [Note: [Col. 0164C] e Cod. Just.: “have been brought, so that now”; rightly corrected by Cujacius in commentary, p. 228, and by Go. See Dirksen, cited work, p. 492.]. Let the vexatious suits of private persons now at least be restrained by the example that we order even the just lawsuits of the fisc to remain silent [Note: [Col. 0164C] f Til. wrongly: *eos saltem*.] [Note: [Col. 0164C] g Ri* wrongly: *justa*.].

Given on the third day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING NUMERARII AND ACTUARII

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Leontius [Note: [Col. 0164C] h Cod. Just.: “Concerning accountants and chartularies, assistants, the bureaux and bureaux of the exalted seat of the other judges, military as well as civil.” Aur. and Lugd.: “Concerning scrinarii.”]. We decreed long ago [Note: [Col. 0164D] i *Dignitas* is absent from the manuscript and editions; Go. approves; Be., from c. 1 C. Th. *If Anyone [has clipped] a Solidus* (IX, 22) and c. 1 Cod. Just. *On Leave* (XII, 43), wishes “Praetorian Prefect” added. Fol. 81 of the manuscript begins with the heading of this title.] that no one should attain, through influence, the administration of any of the individual offices, especially the tabularii, unless he belongs to the order or corps of the particular office. We order such persons to perform the offices entrusted to them as long as it is evident that they are fit, or they are shown, without hindrance of age, to be able to fulfill them, so that, where administration remains continuously in one person’s hands, his trustworthiness may likewise be evident. Therefore, if anyone enters offices liable to the fisc through the recommendation of influence, he shall be required to pay ten pounds of gold as a fine [Note: [Col. 0164D] j Go. had already noted that this enactment did not reach our time.].

Posted on the fifth day before the Ides of June at Hierapolis [Note: [Col. 0164D] k Be. in the note adds “in” or “at”; but see C. Th. VI, 26, 14, note b; VI, 35, 1, note p; and below X, 20, 2.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar [Col. 0164C] (319) [Note: [Col. 0164D] l Aur. and Lugd. omit *Id.* Go. notes: “From this subscription it seems possible to infer that this law was issued by Licinius, not Constantine, since the East obeyed him at this time; see Zosimus, II, p. 679” (chapter 20). For this reason perhaps Ri. and Ri*. print 318 in place of 319.].

## CONCERNING APPEALS

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Severus, Vicar … [Note: [Col. 0164D] m The place of whose vicariate he held is not mentioned even in Cod. Just. Blondel, *On the Primacy in the Church*, p. 513, suspects that he was Vicar of Illyricum, without giving a reason; Go., in the Chronicle, calls him Vicar of Italy. In c. 2 C. Th. [Col. 0165B] *On Maternal Property* (VIII, 18), he is called Julius Severus. It is remarkable that in other laws addressed to Severus his rank is either wholly omitted or, when mentioned, suspect.]

[Col. 0165A] Lest cases which have come to our cognizance must again be transferred to courts, we order that the necessary statements of evidence be fully entered in the acts. For we are compelled to refrain from pronouncing judgment, since we have decreed [Note: [Col. 0165C] a See c. 6 and 8 of this title.] that our rescripts issued on the opinions or reports of judges ought not to be reconsidered [Note: [Col. 0165C] b The words “since we have decreed … ought not” are absent from Cod. Just.], because there is danger that a dispute may be decided while the matter remains unknown, the opportunity to complain having been removed [Note: [Col. 0165C] c 4: *conquaerendi*.]. Therefore let a judge be marked with perpetual infamy if all that litigants have recited for purposes of information and proof [Note: [Col. 0165C] d 4: *causas*, with final s deleted in red ink.] [Note: [Col. 0165C] e Fol. 183 of manuscript 4.] cannot be found entered in or appended to the acts.

Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of July at Aquileia [Note: [Col. 0165C] f Cod. Just.: “Kalends” (July absent), “Aquileiae.” Aur. and Lugd.: Aqui.; and shortly afterward *Cons.* Cui. 1: Licino. Cod. Just.: CC.], in the fifth consulship of Constantine and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## THAT LAND CANNOT BE BOUGHT WITHOUT ITS ASSESSMENT OR ARREARS

[Note: [Col. 0165C] g Very many manuscripts, including 4, have *comparare*, but manuscript 4 corrects it in an early hand. 15: “Land not to be bought without assessment.” 25: “They must not dare to buy land without assessment or arrears.”]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Antonius [Note: [Col. 0165C] h Reinesius emends Auxonius; Cod. Just.: to Marcellus, and the rest is absent. Ri*. omits *Imp.*] Marcellinus [Col. 0165B], Governor of the First Province of Lugdunensis. In dealing with the revenues of the annona [Note: [Col. 0165C] i Aur. and Lugd.: *emolumentu*, i.e. *emolumentum*.], in order that we might learn [Note: [Col. 0165C] j Cod. Just. omits “in order that we might learn … remained outstanding.”] how great were the arrears remaining from payments of this kind in each province and under what names, we learned that the chief cause of arrears was that some persons, taking advantage of [Note: [Col. 0165C] k Cod. Just.: *captantes*. Go. rightly says nothing should be changed. See Salmasius on Solinus, p. 39, Trajectine edition. Vatican Fragments §35: “persuaded by the clever artifices of another to an adverse advantage.” What if one should read *capitali* for *captati*?] the temporary needs of certain others [Note: [Col. 0165D] l 4 and Til. add *nomen*.], purchased rich and choice estates on the condition [Note: [Col. 0165D] m Cod. Just.: *comparant*, omitting *opimos* and *et electos*, wrongly according to Go.] that they should neither pay the owners’ arrears into the fisc nor possess the estates subject to them. Therefore it has pleased us that, if anyone is found [Note: [Col. 0165D] n 4: *onstiterit*, corrected by the scribe.] to have made a contract of this kind and to have purchased possession on this basis [Note: [Col. 0165D] o Cod. Just.: *atque ac lege.*], he shall be liable both for the ordinary assessments [Note: [Col. 0165D] p 4 and editions: *solidis*. Go., who conjectured *solvendis*, later rejects it. Cod. Just., Val. in margin: *solitis*, rightly. Thus C. Th. XI, 5, 4: *devotionis solitae*; IV, 12, 2: *solitae praestationi*; IV, 12, 6: *octavas solite constitutas*; XI, 1, 24: *species solitas*.] of the purchased estate and for all the arrears [Note: [Col. 0165D] q With *quam* begins fol. 134 of manuscript 4.] of the same property [Note: [Col. 0165D] r Cod. Just. adds: “since it is necessary for one who has bought to acknowledge the assessment of the thing purchased, and it is not permitted for anyone to buy or sell a thing without its assessment,” taken from the beginning of c. 2 C. Th. *On Contracting Sales*, cited.].

Given on the Kalends of July at Agrippina [Col. 0166A], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar [Note: [Col. 0166B] a Go.–Ri.* omit the year. Since Constantine was not in Gaul this year but in Pannonia or Dacia, Go. assigns this law to 312, in the second consulship of Constantine Augustus and Licinius Augustus, saying that it concerns Gaul and the Gallic census, and that Constantine granted remissions of arrears to Lugdunensis Prima, where lay Augustodunum, in whose name the orator Eumenius of Augustodunum had given thanks in a special manner in 312. Against this Bou. observes that Go.’s proposed consuls cannot be reconciled with the subscription’s words “and Licinius Caesar,” which can be referred only to Licinius Junior, created Caesar in 317; that Eumenius’ panegyric was delivered not in 312 but in 313; and that this law does not concern remission of arrears. Since Constantine was not at Agrippina at this time, perhaps Aquileia should be restored. Pagius also writes differently in his Critique on 313, note 20: Constantine was in Italy throughout 312; Eumenius delivered his speech not in 312 but in 311, when Constantine celebrated his Quinquennalia, mentioned by the same orator in chapter 13; and he gave thanks for a special benefit granted to the Augustodunenses alone, not for a general benefit granted by this law to the entire province of Lugdunensis. He therefore assigns this law to 313, in the third consulship of Constantine Augustus and Licinius Augustus. Compare Reland, cited work, p. 302; Tillemont, cited work, vol. IV, Notes, p. 128, no. 30, who, retaining the year 319, locates the error in the city’s name and emends Agrippinae to Aquileiae. Go. in his Chronicle for 319 also proposes Aquileia, though he prefers 312.] (319).

## CONCERNING DECURIONS

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Patroclus … [Note: [Col. 0166C] b The rank is absent, without any indication of a lacuna, in manuscript 4, Til.–Cui. 2*, Be., and Cod. Just.; Go. and Ri. indicate a lacuna by four dots, Ri*. by five; Cod. Just. reads “The Emperor Constantine Augustus.”] Although it seems unworthy for those possessing no rank to descend to sordid unions with slave women, yet [Note: [Col. 0166D] c Til.: *et si*. In manuscript 4 *conubium, conubia* is always written. Go., reversing the words, wishes: “although it is in no way forbidden by the laws, yet it seems unworthy”; nevertheless he concedes that the received text can be defended.] it is by no means prohibited by the laws. But no lawful marriage can exist with persons of servile condition, and slaves are born from a union of this kind [Note: [Col. 0166D] d Here begins c. 3 Cod. Just.: “There can be no marriage with female slaves; for slaves are born from a union of this kind. Therefore we order that …” Manuscript 4: *contubernio*.].

We therefore order that decurions, led by lust [Note: [Col. 0166D] e Cod. Just. adds *servarum*.], shall not take refuge in the households of the most powerful families. For if a decurion, without the knowledge of the stewards and agents [Note: [Col. 0166D] f Cod. Just. adds *et*.], has united himself secretly with another’s female slave, we order that the woman be sent to the mines [Note: [Col. 0166D] g Cod. Just.: *detrudi*.] by sentence [Note: [Col. 0166D] h Go.–Ri*. read *sententia* in place of *per sententiam*, from an unknown source.] of the judge [Note: [Col. 0166D] i 4: *juvemus*, corrected in red ink to *jubemus*.], and the decurion himself deported to an island; his movable property and urban slaves shall be confiscated, while his estates and rural slaves [Col. 0166B] shall be assigned to the city [Note: [Col. 0166D] j Cod. Just. has the shorter sentence: “deported, all his property being assigned to the city.”] of whose curial order he was a member [Note: [Col. 0166D] k Fol. 220 of manuscript 4.], provided that he has been freed from paternal power and has neither children, parents, nor relatives who are called to his succession according to the order [Col. 0167A] of the laws [Note: [Col. 0167B] a Cod. Just.: *vocentur*.].

But if the managers or agents of the place in which the disgraceful act was committed were aware of it [Note: [Col. 0167B] b Cod. Just.: *fuerint.*], or did not wish to reveal the discovered crime [Note: [Col. 0167B] c Cod. Just.: *promere noluerint.*], they ought to be condemned to the mines. If, however, the master [Note: [Col. 0167C] d Cod. Just. adds *loci*, “of the place.”] allowed this to occur or afterward concealed it when discovered, then, if it was done on an estate, the estate, together with its slaves, livestock, and all the other things maintained for agricultural cultivation [Note: [Col. 0167C] e 4: *sustinetur*, corrected in red by adding n, *sustinentur*. Cod. Just.: “shall be claimed for the rights of the fisc,” rightly corrected by Go.], shall be claimed by the resources of the fisc. But if it occurred in a city, we order half of all his property to be taken, increasing the punishment because the crime was committed within domestic walls and he did not wish to make it public immediately upon learning of it [Note: [Col. 0167C] f Cod. Just. omits what follows.].

Accordingly, if from the day of the law anyone is found to have alienated his patrimony and transferred it into the ownership [Note: [Col. 0167C] g In manuscript 4 the letter i seems to have been added by a second hand above the line: *dominium*. Summary of C. Th.: “In the lodging of a slave woman.”] of the slave woman, the curial order shall be permitted to investigate diligently, so that what has been diminished from the resources of the aforesaid person may thus be made good to the public treasury of the city in money [Col. 0167B] [Note: [Col. 0167C] h 4: *supradicti*, with s added in red, so that it should read *supradictis*; perhaps *diminutum*.] [Note: [Col. 0167C] i 4: *pecunias* || fol. 221 begins. Go.: *penunia*.].

Given on the Kalends of July at Aquileia [uncertain: the text reads *Aqui. Jullea*], in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus and the consulship of Licinius Caesar (319).

## CONCERNING THOSE MANUMITTED BY A PERSON WHO WAS NOT THEIR MASTER

[Note: [Col. 0167C] k Thus emended by Be. and W. from manuscript 6 and Cod. Just.; this correction is confirmed by manuscripts 7, 10, 14, 16, 18. The remaining manuscripts and Sich.–Ri*. read “Concerning Those Who Not by a Master.” According to Go., some manuscripts have “not by their own master,” though I do not find this in his Breviary of Alaric manuscripts, but it occurs in manuscripts L, R, U.]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus [Note: [Col. 0167D] l Add: Urban Prefect. Compare below c. 4 C. Th. *On Gifts* (VIII, 12), c. 2 C. Th. *On the Julian Law concerning Violence* (IX, 10), and c. 8 C. Th. *On Appeals* (XI, 30). Some manuscripts and Cod. Just.: Praetorian Prefect, improbably according to Go., Be., and W. Most manuscripts and Sich., Cui. 1–Ri.: *de Hiis*.]. If freedom is given to another’s slave by persons who are not [Note: [Col. 0167D] m Thus Be., approved by W., emended from Cod. Just., with which, apart from Bas., manuscripts 14, 16, and 40 agree. Although the latter omits the text, it has after the heading, from the text, *Si N.*, i.e. *Si non*, which are the law’s first words. 10, 18: “If a slave [is freed] by a master.” The rest: “If not by.”] his masters, and this is obtained from those judges [Note: [Col. 0167D] n Sich., Cui. 1–Cui. 2*: *hiis*; Ri*: *iis*.] who have the right of granting it [Note: [Col. 0167D] o Go. conjectures *imperabitur*, though he himself prefers *impetrabitur*.] [Note: [Col. 0167D] p 9: “Where there is a right of giving damage, without …” Sich. in the margin: “Perhaps it should be read: *quibus dandi jus non est*, ‘who do not have the right to grant it.’” See Go., note e.], there is an easy dissolution, without any fear of penalty.

But if it is shown that anything has been done by law on our order, and that a person not the master requested that the other’s slave [Note: [Col. 0167D] q 10, 18: *jubentur*.] [Note: [Col. 0167D] r 16 omits *mancipium*.] [Col. 0168A] be manumitted [Note: [Col. 0168B] a 12 omits *petiisse*. Cod. Just. adds *probetur*.], then, once the person who is shown to have obtained freedom in our presence [Note: [Col. 0168B] b 18 omits *in*.] [Note: [Col. 0168C] c Cod. Just. adds “from one who was not his master.”] has been restored immediately to the person to whose ownership he belongs [Note: [Col. 0168C] d 19, 20: *restituta*. The same manuscripts shortly afterward: *conscientia* and Go.: *manumissit*.], the person who, by deceiving the emperor’s awareness, manumitted another’s slave shall be compelled to give that slave’s master two slaves of the same sex, age, and skill [Note: [Col. 0168C] e 9: *de re hujusmodi*; 19, 20: *hujusmodi*; 10, 18: *ejusmodi*. Cod. Just.: *ejusdem*.] [Note: [Col. 0168C] f 20 adds *ut*, as also Cod. Just.: *cujus*.] as the manumitted slave is found to be, and three others to the fisc [Note: [Col. 0168C] g This word, absent from most Breviary of Alaric manuscripts and from the editions Sich.–Ri*., was already noted in the margins of Cui. 1–Cui. 2* as requiring supplementation, with this difference: the margin of Cui. 1–Lugd. reads “it seems *a fisco* is lacking,” while the margin of Cui. 2, 2* reads “it seems *fisco* is lacking.” Be. and W. received it from Cod. Just., rightly, as manuscripts 12, 14, 17 confirm. Go. attempted “and three others, likewise similar in account to the treasury.” 16 omits *tria fisco*, and Cod. Just. reads *eadem rat.*], likewise similar in the same respects.

This penalty is not always imposed, but rather ceases [Note: [Col. 0168C] h 8: *se*; 20 above the line: *vel saepius*.] if perhaps the freed slave can exclude a status action brought against him [Note: [Col. 0168C] i 14 omits *si*.] [Note: [Col. 0168C] j 8, 10, 12, 14, 16: *man. in parentem sibi*.] by pleading a lawful limitation [Note: [Col. 0168C] k 14, 21: *subjecta*, but 21 in margin: *objecta*.] [Note: [Col. 0168D] l 19, 20: *perscriptione*.], since the person who has by silence confirmed acts to his own detriment must impute to himself the loss of the slave [Note: [Col. 0168D] m 19, 20: *amissa*.] [Note: [Col. 0168D] n 16: *debeant*.] [Note: [Col. 0168D] o Cod. Just. adds *is*.] [Note: [Col. 0168D] p Cod. Just.: *firmavit*.].

Posted on the day before the Ides [Note: [Col. 0168D] q 13, 20, 24: “Given on the day before the Ides”; 15, 19, 32: “Given on the Ides.”] of July, in the fifth consulship of Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0168D] r 8, 20: “at Constantinople, Augustus II”; 19: “Augustus II”; 31, 32, 39 omit V.] and the consulship of Licinius Caesar [Note: [Col. 0168D] s Many manuscripts and Til. omit *Caes.*] (319).

[Col. 0168B] INTERPRETATION. If anyone has presumed to manumit another’s slave, and has done so in the presence of the emperor or in a church, he shall be held liable to this penalty: both the freed slave shall be recalled by his owner, and he shall be compelled to give two other slaves of the same age or sex, or at least of the same trade which the person who was manumitted knew. [Note: [Col. 0168D] t 20 “If anyone—this penalty—to him—trade—he is manumitted—(also 21 ‘he is manumitted’) he shall be compelled to know.” 8, Sich. “he knew, he shall be compelled to give”; 7 “he is manumitted”; 6 “of the trade—he knew.”] But if the person said to have been manumitted defeats the owner reclaiming him under this prescription, so that he may now protect the validity of his status by lapse of time, then the man who manumitted him is not to be bound to the penalty, since the person who reclaims him has incurred prejudice to his ownership or has fostered it by silence. [Note: [Col. 0168D] u 28 “under this inscription,” others “prescription.”] [Note: [Col. 0168D] v 20 “so that also the validity”; 6, 7 “by validity.”] [Note: [Col. 0168D] x 20 “bound to fulfil the penalty—he is reclaimed—he incurs, fostering through silence.” Go. prefers “of ownership,” which 6 has.]

## ON MATERNAL PROPERTY

[Col. 0169A]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Julius Severus. [Note: [Col. 0169B] a “A[ugustus]” is absent in some manuscripts. In manuscript 40, both “A.” and “Severus” are omitted.] [Note: [Col. 0169B] b 38 “Reverus.” Add. according to Go., “Vic[arius].” See above, col. 164, On Appeals. That Severus who is named in the inscription of ch. 9, C. Th. On the Law of the Treasury (X, 1), seems to be another person.]

When anything has come to a father from a maternal succession, after formal acceptance of the inheritance, and successions in maternal property have devolved upon children, it is our pleasure that such property be held under parental power in such a way that they may exercise only ownership of possession, but have no licence or power to alienate it. [Note: [Col. 0169B] c 8, 12, 13, 19 incorrectly: “When [something comes] from a father.”] [Note: [Col. 0169B] d 20, by a second hand, “creacione,” printed Ri.] [Note: [Col. 0169B] e 21, Sich., Til. omit “property.”] [Note: [Col. 0169B] f Many manuscripts have “to hold,” incorrectly.] [Note: [Col. 0169B] g 20 “of the possessor”; 10, 18 “they exercise.”] [Note: [Col. 0169B] h Til. “lecentiam.”] [Note: [Col. 0169B] i 21, Sich. “they have.”]

Thus, when the lawful ages of the children have invited their parents to emancipate them and the heads of households wish to see their children independent, the children shall offer their fathers one-third of the maternal property as a gift. [Note: [Col. 0169B] j All manuscripts have “the lawful ages … have invited,” and so also Cuj. 1—Ri*, from Lugd. I have therefore restored these words in place of “the lawful age … shall have invited,” [Col. 0169C] which reading Be. restored from Sich. and Til. Although it is not merely unobjectionable but even more elegant than ours, nevertheless, since not even one manuscript supports it, it seems to have arisen from Sichard’s conjecture.] [Note: [Col. 0169C] k 6–8, 10, 12, 14, 17, 18 “sons,” which I would have accepted because of the following “sons” and because of the Interpretation, had not the Lugdunensis manuscript and manuscripts 9, 15, 19—which I have often said agree with the genuine manuscripts of the Theodosian Code—had the reading “children.”] [Note: [Col. 0169C] l 19, 20 “his”; 18 “and.”] [Note: [Col. 0169C] m Incorrectly Cuj. 2—Ri*: “to the sons.”] [Note: [Col. 0169C] n 15 “in lieu of a gift.”]

If the fathers judge that this should be accepted, the decision concerning the division to be made must be entrusted to the equitable judgment of honourable men, [Note: [Col. 0169C] o Lugd. manuscript: “to be accepted.” 19, 20 “the share,” not badly, but the common reading is more suitable.] [Note: [Col. 0169C] p Go. asserts that these words, no less than those in ch. 1, “by the judgment of honourable men,” betray Anianism; I am surprised that Go. said this, since the example of the genuine Theodosian Code, that is, the Lugdunensis, does not in this reading [Col. 0169D] differ from the Breviary-Alaric manuscripts. Moreover, 10, 12, 13, 16, 18 have “justice.”] through whom, after the division is made, the parents shall receive the offered third share in such a manner that they also have power to alienate that share, provided only that someone can be found who wishes to accept this licence. [Note: [Col. 0169D] q Here begins folio CXXI of the Lugdunensis manuscript, whose upper portion is torn. Although the lacunae of the manuscript are here supplied from the Breviary-Alaric manuscripts, I have marked them with italic letters.] [Note: [Col. 0169D] r 10, 12, 18–20, Sich., Til. “may receive.”] [Note: [Col. 0169D] s I restored this reading, proposed by Go. and Be. but already printed by Sich. and Til., on the authority of manuscripts 9 (where, however, “shares”), 15, 19, 21, which frequently agree with the genuine Theodosian Code and seem to do so here as well. For in the Lugdunensis manuscript, though mutilated here, the syllable *tis* remains (*partis*). According to Go., *til* was written, but corrected by Ri. The remaining witnesses read, awkwardly, “the parents [have power] of alienating those [things].” For the preceding text is: “the parents shall thus receive the offered third share.” 20 has “shares” above the line. Moreover, 18 has “of alienating,” and 6, 7, 10, 14, 16–18 have “right” for “of that share.” In manuscript 13, “that … power” is omitted. A little below, 21 has “may be able to find,” and 15 “is able,” for “may have been able.”]

For it is advantageous in every respect for children to strive that, by dutiful affection and devoted service, they may deserve to receive the portion which they have given to their fathers. [Col. 0170A] [Note: [Col. 0170B] a 15 “in every way.”] [Note: [Col. 0170B] b 21, Sich. “is fitting”; 15 “to be lost”; 10, 18 “to be admitted.”] [Note: [Col. 0170B] c Go., in a note, “to receive.”]

Given on the seventh day before the Ides of September at Milan; received on the seventh day before the Nones of October, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0170B] d 6–8, 12, 14, 16, 17, Til. “third”; 10, 18 “fourth”; 13, [Col. 0170C] 32 “sixth”; 21, 24, 27, 40, 43, Sich. “eighth”; 42 “ninth”; 31, 35 omit “seventh.” I did not find the number II noted by Go.] [Note: [Col. 0170C] e Go. in the Chronology wishes “Milan” to be moved after “October”; 8 omits “Milan—October,” and 15, 19 have “received on the Nones of October.”] [Note: [Col. 0170C] f Some manuscripts have “ninth” for “Nones”; 21 “at Constantinople, Augustus.” In the following manuscripts either “A.” or “V.” is omitted, or, as happened in Sich. and Til., “C.”, or finally “Coss.” It is also written “Liciano” or “Licynio” for Licinius, and “most distinguished man” for “V. C.,” which some manuscripts have for “C.”]

INTERPRETATION. Upon the death of his wife, the father shall possess the maternal property of the children in such a way as to have usufruct of it; but a Novel constitution determines how much, or for how long, he may have it. [Note: [Col. 0170C] g Thus most and the best manuscripts; editions: “the father shall thus.”] [Note: [Col. 0170C] h Thus Cuj. 1—Lugd., “and” for “or.”] Yet the father shall have no power to sell or give away any of it. [Note: [Col. 0170C] i Many manuscripts: “Yet [he has no power] to sell any of it or to give [it away].” 21 “to dominate” (in the margin, “to alienate”) and omits “of it.” In the following passages most manuscripts have *mancipaverit*, *mancipati*, *mancipationis*.]

But if, after the mother’s death, he emancipates a son, the son himself shall offer, as a gift from the maternal property—that is, from the share of the emancipated son—one third of the maternal property. [Note: [Col. 0170C] k 21 adds “if” in the margin; 10 “a dead son.”] [Note: [Col. 0170C] j 19, 20 and other manuscripts, Sich., Cuj. 1—Lugd. add above, “emancipated.” 21 “the son above ca.”, but in the margin “as [in] Sich.”] [Note: [Col. 0170D] l 21, Sich., Cuj. 1—Lugd. “shall offer,” but 21 has “may offer” in the margin.] This share shall nevertheless remain his own property, so that the father may obtain it when honourable men make the division. [Note: [Col. 0170D] m 21 “or,” but in the margin “which”; 6, 7 “so.”] [Note: [Col. 0170D] n Sich., Cuj. 1—Lugd. “power”; shortly after, 20 “title.”]

But if a father can be brought only so far as to appropriate the children’s property out of impious greed or leave it to others, it is nevertheless fitting that the children strive to recover, by service and filial affection, that which they offered their parents on account of emancipation. [Col. 0170B] [Note: [Col. 0170D] o Thus many manuscripts and Sich.; the rest, “may be invoked.”] [Note: [Col. 0170D] p 6–9 and many other manuscripts: “he should strive to leave [it].” But the common reading accords with the law itself.] [Note: [Col. 0170D] q 20 “either by service or by favour and affection.”]

## ON FRAUD

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Symmachus, *vir clarissimus*. [Note: [Col. 0170D] r 19, 20, Sich., Cod. Just.: “Vicar”; 6, 7, 16 “vic.”, incorrectly; Go., whom see, 10, 15, 18, 44 “distinguished man.” Sich. in the margin, “V. Clariss.” Some manuscripts omit “V. C.” Moreover, the manuscripts usually have “Simacus.”]

We have judged it best that an action for fraud be brought, after examination of the case, not from the day on which each person declares that he learned of the fraud committed against him, nor within the period of a useful year, but rather from the day on which the fraud is alleged to have been committed, within the continuous period of a year, by those found to have the right to litigate. [Note: [Col. 0170D] s 20, 33 “we have said,” but 20 corrected to “we have judged.”] [Note: [Col. 0170D] t 10, 18 “that”; shortly after, 15 “lost.”] [Note: [Col. 0170D] u Cod. Just. “has commemorated.” Cf. Dirksen, cited work, p. 390.] [Col. 0171A] [Note: [Col. 0171B] a Thus Til., Cod. Just., and all manuscripts except 19, 20, which have “a useful year,” and 15, where “useful” is omitted. Editions except Til.: “useful.” Cf. Dirksen, cited work.] [Note: [Col. 0171B] b 33 “from that day.”] [Note: [Col. 0171B] c 9 “that.” Some manuscripts: “claimant.”] [Note: [Col. 0171B] d Cod. Just.: “an action for fraud may be brought within a continuous two-year period, whether the person who complains that he suffered fraud has been absent or is present.” Then all the rest immediately follows: “Therefore let all know,” etc. Cf. Dirksen, cited work, p. 391.] [Note: [Col. 0171B] e Thus 15, confirming Go.’s conjecture, who wishes to read “by those”; 9 “to the defendant.” The rest and editions: “to defendants.”] [Note: [Col. 0171B] f 20, Sich. “is”; 33 omits “to be.”] [Note: [Col. 0171B] g 6, 7, 14, 16–18 “is threatened”; [Col. 0171C] 8 “imenetur”; 10 “imminitur.”]

Thus, if perhaps the person against whom the action is brought has departed to some distant place by any means, the claimant shall neither be burdened by the necessity of giving notice, nor shall the presence of the absentee be required. [Note: [Col. 0171C] h Thus Til. and all manuscripts except 20, which has “of this kind,” as do Sich. and Cuj. 1—W.] [Note: [Col. 0171C] i 33 “to defer, the case having been heard”; 20, Sich. “to be deferred,” but Sich. has “to be brought” in the margin. Moreover Sich.: “to be deferred”; thus Cuj. 1—Ri.* “to be brought”; thus Til., W., “to be brought”; Be., “to be brought”; thus 10, 18 “to be brought, or if perhaps”; 20 omits “that.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] j 6–8, 16 add “who.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] k 20, Sich. “far,” but Sich. in the margin “more distant.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] l Many manuscripts, “necessity.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] m 19, 20 “the petitioner may be honoured,” others “may be honoured.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] n 19, 20, Sich., Til. “has departed”; 16 “had”; 33 “has had.”]

Nevertheless, no one who wishes to do so shall be prohibited from appearing at the hearing against whom an application for such a claim is sought to be determined. Thus, once the action for fraud has been granted, the case, transferred to its proper judge, shall be decided within the space of two years, with the time-limit observed, when it has been lawfully begun before that judge, after the example of other suits. [Note: [Col. 0171C] o 6–8, 10, 14, 16–18, Til., Aur.—Cuj. 2* in the margin “to assent”; Cuj. 1 “to ascend.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] p 16 “wished”; 15 “anyone may appear if he wishes, present.”] [Note: [Col. 0171C] q 20 “sought” or printed Sich. “has been”; “sought” (in margin: “applied for”). 9, 19 “sought” or “applied for”; 15, 33 omit “thus.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] r Sich., Til. “the space [of two years] shall be decided. With the calculation [of time].” 20 “the space shall be decided; [Col. 0171D] calculation.” 6, 7, 9, 10, 18 “spaces”; 33 “the space is given concerning this.” 19 “the space, let him observe the calculation.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] s 20 “ordered.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] t 15 adds “indeed”; 16 “litigation.”]

But it shall lapse into perpetual silence unless, from the day on which the action was granted, every suit has been decided within the continuous two-year period that follows. [Note: [Col. 0171D] u 20, Sich., others “perpetual,” but Sich. has “perpetually” in the margin; 15 omits “indeed.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] v 33 “silence.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] x 9 “had been.”] [Col. 0171B] [Note: [Col. 0171D] y 19, 20, Sich. omit “within.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] z 19, 20 “a daily two-year period”; Sich. “a daily two-year period,” but in the margin: “perhaps *continuato* ought to be read.” 33 “a continuous two-year period”; Noodt conjectures “within the continuous period of a year.” But cf. Gluck, cited work, vol. V, p. 434.] [Note: [Col. 0171D] aa 33 “cut short”; Sich., Til. “the suit shall have been decided.”]

Therefore let all know that no licence is granted to bring an action for fraud after two years, nor to finish after two years an action begun before the completion of the two-year period. [Note: [Col. 0171D] bb 7 “to receive”; 33 omits “let them know, nor,” and shortly after “before.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] cc 20, Sich. “an action to be begun after the following two-year period.”] [Note: [Col. 0171D] dd Cod. Just. adds “indeed.” 20 “to finish,” and omits “begun”; [Col. 0172B] “after the two-year period”; the same words are omitted in Sich.; 9 “to finish.” Moreover 8 “begun”; Go. “ceptae”; Ri. “coeptae,” by error.] [Col. 0172A] [Note: [Col. 0172C] a 8, 16, 19 “licence having been granted”; Cod. Just. “to be granted.”]

Given on the eighth day before the Kalends of August at Naissus, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0172C] b 26 “thirteenth”; 36 “ninth”; 40 not “ninth.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] c Thus most manuscripts and Til. Other manuscripts have Narso, Naissio, Naisio, Naiso, Nesio, Nesto, Natesso; Cuj. 1—Ri*, Nasso; Cod. Just., Nesso; 15 omits Naissus; Be., W., Naissi.] [Note: [Col. 0172C] d 33 omits “V.” and “and Lic.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] e Some manuscripts “VV, CC.”; others “VCC.”; 36, 40 “CC. SS.”; others, like 16 and Til., omit “Caesar” or “Caesars, consuls.”]

INTERPRETATION. Fraud (*dolus malus*) exists whenever matters that have been settled are altered by documentary devices or fraud through some written instrument. Or if someone, by the substitution or surreptitious introduction of documents, is induced to consent to something which seems likely to be against him; or when similar acts are proved to have been committed, the judge having investigated them. [Note: [Col. 0172C] f 6, 7, 10, 18 and other manuscripts add “through”; 9 omits “or surreptitious [introduction].”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] g 6, 7, 20, 42, 43 omit “that,” others, like 44, have “lest” for “that.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] h Some manuscripts, Cuj. 1—Lugd. add “old”; shortly after, 44 “induces.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] i 20 in the margin “otherwise, family,” and above *similia*: “and so on”; 43 “having learned”; Sich. “or things similar to these.”]

Accordingly, anyone who complains that he has been fraudulently injured shall both commence and conclude his actions within two years; he should know that beyond that period no time is granted him either to commence or to conclude them. [Note: [Col. 0172C] j 19, 20, Sich., Cuj. 1, Aur., Lugd. add “himself.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] k Cuj. 1, Aur., Lugd. “defrauded.”] [Note: [Col. 0172C] l 7, 10, 18 “and,” but 7 corrected to “and.”] [Note: [Col. 0172D] m Sich. in the margin “to terminate.”]

For if either the person said to have committed the fraud, or the person who suffered it, happens to be absent, he shall know that two years are allowed him to conclude the action, counting from the time when he began proceedings before the judge. [Note: [Col. 0172D] n 43 “that,” and omits “For if.”] [Note: [Col. 0172D] o 20 omits “fraud”; Sich., Cuj. 1, Aur., Lugd. add “evil”; shortly after, 20 “is said to have committed.”] [Col. 0172B]

## ON THE PRIVILEGES OF THOSE WHO HAVE SERVED IN THE SACRED PALACE

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Proculus, Proconsul of Africa. If any person from among our *memoriales* or palace officials has been assigned to conduct the affairs of a municipality or of another office, no presentation of horses shall be demanded from him. But those who have not performed services in the palace, but are from another class of persons, shall furnish the customary horses for an office of this kind. [Note: [Col. 0172D] p Go. incorrectly: “Procoulus.” Shortly after, the manuscript has *merialibus*, but corrected to *memorialibus*.] [Note: [Col. 0172D] q Go. conjectures *curatoricio*. Cf. C. Th. XI, 17, ch. 2, On the Collection of Horses. The manuscript has *equosollemnes*.]

Given on the sixth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fourth time and Licinius (319). [Note: [Col. 0172D] r Go. emends to “fifth” (319), because of C. Th. XV, 3, ch. 1, On Public Travel Duties, addressed in the same year to the same Proculus, Proconsul of Africa. Add C. Th. I, 12, ch. 2, On the Duties of Proconsuls. Be. proposes either “fifth and Licinius Caesar,” which returns to Go.’s view, or “Licinius for the fourth time” (315), printed by Go. in the Chronology under 319. The former conjecture is opposed by the fact that this constitution, contrary to the arrangement of the compilers of the Theodosian Code, would be later than the following one; the latter by the fact that Proculus is not found as Proconsul of Africa in 315. The error undoubtedly lies in the month.]

## ON PENALTIES

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Festus, Governor of Sardinia. [Col. 0173A] Whoever appears deserving of correction for non-serious causes shall be assigned to the mills of the city of Rome. Once Your Sincerity has begun to observe this, let all know that persons who, as stated, have deserved to undergo such a sentence for lighter causes are to be assigned to workhouses or mills and sent under suitable escort to the city of Rome—that is, to the prefect of the grain supply.

Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius (319). [Note: [Col. 0173B] a Go., in the Chronology, “third,” but notes: “Elsewhere, fourth.”]

## ON CONTRACTING A PURCHASE [Note: [Col. 0173B] b Cod. Just. adds “and sale.”]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Profuturus, prefect of the grain supply. [Note: [Col. 0173B] c Some manuscripts and the editions Sich.—Ri* omit “A.”] [Note: [Col. 0173B] d 20 “Profuturam, prefect of the grain supply, etc.” 42 “Prof., governor,” and omits “of the grain supply,” which word is also lacking in manuscripts 29, 36, and in manuscripts 10, 18, 19, 21 is transferred from the inscription into the text (“sale of the grain supply”). [Col. 0173C] 37 omits “prefect of the grain supply.”]

The good faith of a sale or purchase, when no coercion by overreaching has taken place, ought by no means to be broken. [Note: [Col. 0173C] e The following words are corruptly written both in the manuscripts and in the editions Sich.—Lugd. Our reading is found in manuscripts 9, 16, 17, 19, 20 and in editions Cuj. 2—W., except that those editions have “was made” for “having taken place,” and manuscript 20 “of things made” for “having taken place.” Manuscripts 6–8, 10, 14, 16, 18: “the same good faith of sale and purchase, no force of overreaching [having] been made”; 21: “sales and purchases of the grain supply, the same, no force of overreaching having taken place.” Sich.—Lugd.: “Sales and purchases, that is, none [having been] made by force of overreaching,” but in the margin Cuj. 1, Aur., Lugd., on “that is,” etc.: Greek: “Good faith, no overreaching or violence having taken place”; and in the margin Cuj. 2, 2*: Greek: “Sales and purchases, good faith, no overreaching or violence having taken place.” Go., in his commentary, proposes “by overreaching or violence.”] [Note: [Col. 0173C] f 17 “harms.”]

For a contract entered into without any fault is not to be disturbed by litigious clamour merely on the complaint that the price was too low. [Note: [Col. 0173C] g 15 adds “for.” In manuscript 20, after “for,” there is a lacuna of eight letters.] [Note: [Col. 0173C] h 17 “contract”; 9 “complaints [of prices] too low.”] [Col. 0173B] [Note: [Col. 0173D] i 8 “litigious.” 20 “litigious [clamour].”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] j 15 “to be vexed”; 16 “disturbed.”]

Posted on the Ides of August, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0173D] k 9, 19, 27, 29, 33, 42 “given on the Ides”; 20 “given on the second day before the Ides”; 28, 40 “given on the day before the Ides”; 39, 44 “given on the sixth day before the Ides”; 10, 18 “therefore, the same Augustus.” Sich.: “it is [posted] on the day before the Ides”; Til.: “it is posted on the day before the Ides.”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] l Some manuscripts omit “A.”; others “fifth” or “A. V.”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] m 10, 17, 18, 21, 28, 31, 33, 38 and the editions Sich.—Ri* omit “Caesar”; 9, 29, 42 “Licinius Augustus, consuls”; 20 “or Licinius for the fourth time, consuls.”]

INTERPRETATION. When a thing has been bought between buyer and seller at an agreed price, even if it is worth more than the price for which it is presently sold, the sole inquiry shall be whether the person proved to have bought it committed no fraud or violence. [Note: [Col. 0173D] n Sich., Cuj. 1, Aur., Lugd. “purchaser and seller,” but in the margin “buyer and seller.” 6, 7, 9, 20, 39, 43 and other manuscripts: “and seller.”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] o 20 “which thing has been purchased at a settled price.” Many manuscripts: “the thing has been.”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] p 6, 7 “sold.”] [Note: [Col. 0173D] q 9 “does”; 20 “has done,” and shortly after “is proved.”] If the person who sold it wishes to revoke the sale, he shall by no means be permitted to do so. [Note: [Col. 0173D] r Sich. adds “he”; 6, 7 “he wishes to revoke the thing sold by no means.”]

## ON BAKERS AND CATABOLENSES [Note: [Col. 0174B] a In Cod. Just. “and Catabolenses” is omitted. I am surprised that in the three copies of Cuj. 2 which I inspected, “V. Pistoribus” is incorrectly printed.]

[Col. 0174A]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Profuturus, prefect of the grain supply. All bakers must be notified that if anyone should think his estates ought to be transferred to others for the purpose of later asserting himself less able to perform the duty, after placing his resources in concealment, as though someone else were to be substituted in his place, this cunning and these detestable contrivances will avail him nothing. Rather, he shall remain in service at the mill without any excuse, nor shall he be restored to his former legal status if he has transferred any property by purchase. [Note: [Col. 0174C] b Ri., Ri*: “To all.” In the inscription of this chapter Go. has “Constantius” and Ri* “from Profut.,” incorrectly.] [Note: [Col. 0174C] c 4 “addito,” corrected by an earlier hand to “abdito.”] [Note: [Col. 0174C] d Cuj. 2, 2*: “of the former [mill],” Rein. emends “of the mill.”]

Posted on the Ides of August, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0174C] e 4, Til. “Augustus,” and in manuscript 4 after this word is a lacuna of approximately five letters. Go. and Be. rightly direct that “V.” be added, the numeral occurring in the first cited chapter. Shortly after, Aur., Lugd. “Cons.”]

## ON EXTRAORDINARY OR FILTHY PUBLIC DUTIES [Note: [Col. 0174C] f In some Breviary-Alaric manuscripts, as 14, 24, “duties” is omitted.]

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Catulinus, Proconsul of Africa. [Note: [Col. 0174C] g 4 “pu.”; Til., Cuj. 1 “P. V.”; Aur., Lugd. “p. v.” Cuj. 2 silently corrects to “Proc.” The same error in Catulinus’s rank occurred in C. Th. IX, 10, 1; 25, 1. Confusion of these same abbreviations occurs on the same matter in IX, 39, 3; IX, 40, 19; X, 10, 27 and 28; XI, 7, 1. Cf. also C. Th. VI, 4, 1, note u. Cod. Just. “to Ovinius,” absurdly; but Russardus had already restored “to Catulinus,” and Cuj. “to Catulinus, Proconsul of Africa.” Moreover 4 and the editions have “Catullinus.” See C. Th. II, 1, 1, note o.]

It is not proper that patrimonial estates be burdened with extraordinary charges or with duties amounting to one-half or one-third, since it is established that they pay both the gold tax and a very large quantity of grain. Thus, anyone who attempts to violate these regulations shall be punished. [Col. 0174B]

Posted on the sixth day before the Kalends of September at Carthage, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius (319). [Note: [Col. 0174C] h Be.: “at Carthage”; Cod. Just.: “at Carthage”; Cuj. 1: “Kathagini.” In Go. “Constantino” has erroneously dropped out.] [Note: [Col. 0174D] i Go. and Ri. refer this chapter back to 315 (“Constantine Augustus for the fourth time and Licinius for the fourth time”), because in 319 Proculus, not Catulinus, was Proconsul of Africa.]

## ON THE JULIAN LAW CONCERNING PUBLIC AND PRIVATE VIOLENCE

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Prefect of the City. [Note: [Col. 0174D] j See C. Th., ch. 1 On Guardians (III, 17), note y. 6–9, 12, 14, 16, 27, 32, 43 “po. s. ppo.”; 10 “praeposito”; 15, 29 “ppm.”]

If anyone asserts that an estate or anything else belongs to him and considers that restitution of possession is due to him, he shall proceed civilly concerning possession, or, after fulfilling the formalities of law, bring an accusation of violence; he must not be unaware that, if he cannot prove the accusation made, he will undergo the sentence which the defendant ought to incur. [Note: [Col. 0174D] k Aretine document, cited work, p. 466: “whatever,” incorrectly attributed to Wittius. 6: “If anyone asserts [something] belongs to him as against an estate.”] [Note: [Col. 0174D] l 20 “had belonged”; Sich. “belongs and [is] to be restored.”] [Note: [Col. 0174D] m Be., from Cod. Just. and Sich., adds “or.” I deleted “or,” for we neither need that particle nor is it in the manuscripts; it is also absent in Til.—Ri*. Whether “or” was in manuscript 4 is uncertain, since several letters at this place were erased, and a new hand put a red colon in their place.] [Note: [Col. 0174D] 20 “to be possessed.”] [Note: [Col. 0174D] o 10, 18, 20 “fulfil”; 15 “proceed so that, the formality having been fulfilled”; 20 “of the formality.” Shortly afterward it omits “himself.”] [Col. 0175A] [Note: [Col. 0175B] a 15 “if he proves it, [let him undergo] that which the defendant should incur”; 21 “receive.” 13 omits “if [he cannot prove] the accusation … defendant.”]

But if, without making a formal demand, he uses force against a possessor, we command that before all else the matter of violence be examined and that it be investigated who came against whom in possession, so that the rights of the possession lost may be restored to the person found to have been expelled. [Note: [Col. 0175B] b Aretine document: “appeal,” incorrectly attributed to Wittius, cited work; 10, 18 “omitted”; 20 “when the lost [thing] has come,” but corrected to “force.”] [Note: [Col. 0175B] c With the letters *olentiae* begins folio XXII of manuscript 1, or folio XXX of the entire Turin palimpsest, which continues to the words “whoever [acts] with soldiers or,” ch. 3 C. Th. On the Cornelian Law concerning Assassins (IX, 14).] [Note: [Col. 0175C] d 21 “we have commanded.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] e According to Go., some interpreters of Cod. Just.: “what.” 9 “who and.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] f Cod. Just. “came to,” incorrectly attributed to Go.] [Note: [Col. 0175C] g Sich. “excluded”; 21 “lost.”]

Once this restoration has immediately been made, the violent party, not undeservedly assigned to punishment, shall be deferred until the final determination of the entire suit, so that, once the principal case has been tried, if judgment is against him, he shall be deported to an island and all his property confiscated. [Note: [Col. 0175C] h Cod. Just. adds: “If a criminal inquiry is being conducted,” superfluously according to Go., who adds that this final sentence is mentioned in C. Th. XI, 36, ch. 14, On Appeals. 8, 10, 18 “and the same [possession] restored.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] i 6, 7, 10, 12–14, 17, 18 “violator”; 8, 16 “violated”; 4 “punishment,” but corrected to “of punishment” in red ink; 13 “not deservedly.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] j 10, 15, 18, 20 “be brought,” but 15 “limits”; shortly after, 20 “and” for “if.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] k Fol. 17 [ [Col. 0175B] b Aretine document: “appeal,” incorrectly attributed to Wittius, cited work; 10, 18 “omitted”; 20 “when the lost [thing] has come,” but corrected to “force.”] manuscript 4.] [Note: [Col. 0175C] l 9 “be assigned”; 20 “island.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] m 9 omits “confiscated”; 18 “confiscated.” The following material ends in Cod. Just.]

But if judgment is pronounced against the person proved to have been violent, one half of all the property concerning which litigation took place shall remain with him, while the rest shall be claimed by the resources of the fisc. [Note: [Col. 0175C] n 9 “they have been proved”; Ri. “has been proved,” by error.] [Note: [Col. 0175C] o 6–8, 12, 14, 17 “violated.”] [Note: [Col. 0175C] p 1, 7, 9, 16, 20 “is pronounced”; 6, 14 “is being pronounced”; 10 “is pronounced.” Shortly after, Aur., Lugd. “litigarum,” by error.] [Col. 0175B] [Note: [Col. 0175D] q 10, 16, 18 “shall be claimed.”]

Posted on the day before the Nones of October at Rome, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0175D] r Either write here, omitting “the day before,” “given on the Nones,” or repeat in C. Th. VIII, 12, ch. 4, On Donations, “posted on the day before the Nones,” so that both laws fall on the same day. See the cited ch. 4, note rr. I prefer that “posted on the day before the Nones” be written in the cited ch. 4 because of the agreement of almost all manuscripts here. Only three manuscripts, 30, 33, 34, omit “day before”; 31, 43 “third” for “day before”; 20 “given” for “posted.”] [Note: [Col. 0175D] s 40 omits “Rome”; 8 “Const.—and”; 33 “A. V.” Some manuscripts “Lycinio.”] [Note: [Col. 0175D] t “C.” is absent in many manuscripts and in Cod. Just.; 20 “uc. coss.”; 38 “vic. coss.”; Aur., Lugd. “Cons.”]

INTERPRETATION. If anyone believes that he must accuse his adversary before a judge by asserting that he has suffered violence, he must be held to proof of the matter. If he cannot prove that the person whom he called violent was so, he shall suffer the same penalty that the person whom he attacks, if convicted, could have incurred. [Note: [Col. 0175D] u 20 “to be accused,” but corrected.] [Note: [Col. 0175D] v Sich., Cuj. 1—Lugd. “to be held.”] [Note: [Col. 0175D] x Some manuscripts “attacked” or “has attacked.” Sich.: “could have incurred [it] when convicted.”] [Col. 0176A]

For the rest, this law is to be passed over, because it is set forth in the fourth book under the title *Unde vi* (“Whence by Violence”), although that provision was introduced later. [Note: [Col. 0176B] a 6–8 and others: “passed over.”] [Note: [Col. 0176B] b Go.: “who,” erroneously.] [Note: [Col. 0176B] c See C. Th. under this title, ch. 2, *Unde vi* (IV, 22), note d. Some manuscripts “On Violence”; 44 “VI On Violence”; 20 omits “Whence.”] [Note: [Col. 0176B] d Sich. omits “however.”] [Note: [Col. 0176B] e Sich. “was [introduced] at a later time,” but has “introduced”; 20, 21 “was introduced.”] [Note: [Col. 0176B] f Go. notes: “There is one who proposes, ‘having been rejected.’”]

## ON DONATIONS

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Prefect of the City. [Note: [Col. 0176C] g Be., from Go.’s note: “Since the list of Prefects of the City testifies that Bassus held the urban prefecture only until the Kalends of September, whereas this law was issued on the Nones of October, an error must adhere in one of the two places.” But see C. Th. III, 17, ch. 1, On Guardians, note y.]

In accordance with the enactments of the deified Pius, a most wise emperor, it is our pleasure that donations between children and parents shall be valid, in respect of any land and of anything whatsoever, when the liberality is proved to have existed—even though neither mancipation is said to have taken place nor delivery to have followed, but bare intention alone has been manifest. This intention must contain no doubtful agreement and express not an uncertain but such a judgment of mind that no question concerning the intention can arise. [Note: [Col. 0176C] h Bucch., cited work, p. 200; Hollw., cited work, p. 72, note 9, believe that this law is meant in Vat. Fr. §249: “a law was recently spoken, certain persons excepted.” Yet since the subscription in §249 restored by Mai is plainly false, and the consuls of the year 316 should rather be restored (see ch. 1 under this title), those words must necessarily relate to some unknown law.] [Note: [Col. 0176C] i These enactments of the deified Pius are not found in the sources. See Wenck, *Opp.*, p. 189, note *; cf. Vat. Fr. §314 and Hasse, *Rheinisches Museum für Jurisprudenz*, I, p. 220.] [Note: [Col. 0176C] j Here begins folio CXIV of the manuscript.] [Note: [Col. 0176C] k Aur., Lugd. omit “of intention.”]

And donations made among those persons exempted by the Cincian law shall retain their own validity, whether the formality of mancipation has been completed or the thing itself is demonstrably delivered. [Note: [Col. 0176C] l Go. emends “and” to “but.” Marcilius, on the title of the Institutes On Donations, p. 224, conjectures: “and, conferred among the other …, [they shall have] validity as [if] mancipation,” etc.; Go. admits that he does not know what these words mean. Racconerus (so Go.; Ri. “Racconetus”) read: “among persons excepted by the Cincian law.” Moreover, Marcilius’s words have been written in the margin by an early hand in the copy of Cuj. 2* which I use.] [Col. 0176D] [Col. 0176B]

We intend this law to apply to suits found to be pending at whatever time of our order, and to suits arising thereafter, so that concluded matters may not be reopened.

Given on the Nones of October, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0176D] m Either write here “posted on the day before the Nones” for “given on the Nones,” or in C. Th. IX, 10, ch. 3, On the Julian Law concerning Public Violence, cited above, “given on the Nones.” See cited ch. 3, note r.]

## ON THE APPOINTMENT OF GUARDIANS AND CURATORS [Note: [Col. 0176D] n The heading is omitted in manuscript 38, but the numbers of the following titles are not changed. 24, 44 “On Curators.” 12, 25, 26, 33, 40 omit “appointment.” Cod. Just. (V, 33): “On guardians or curators of persons of illustrious or most distinguished rank.”]

Emperor Constantine Augustus and Caesar to Bassus, Prefect of the City. [Note: [Col. 0176D] o Sich., Cuj. 1—Be. “Constantine.”] [Note: [Col. 0176D] p Cod. Just. adds “and Constantine.” In Cod. Just. V, 40, ch. 2, *Si ex pluribus tutoribus*, drawn from C. Th. II, 4, ch. 1, On Notice, and issued in the same year, “Licinius” is added. W. therefore doubts which Caesar is meant: Crispus, Constantine the Younger, or Licinius. Go. [Col. 0177B] wishes Crispus to be understood. See Reland, p. 303. 8 omits “and Caesar”; 15 “and Caesar ad.”; 33 “and Constantinople.”] [Col. 0177A] [Note: [Col. 0177B] a 15 “to Bassus”; 33, 34 “Prefect of the city of Rome.” Cod. Just. “Prefect of the City,” improbably, according to Go., Corsini p. 173, and W., since Maximus had already succeeded Bassus in the urban prefecture from the Kalends of September of that year. “Prefect of the City” seems right to me because the subject of the whole title concerns the jurisdiction of the urban prefect. It appears, therefore, that Bassus’s urban prefecture was extended to October of that year, especially since laws addressed to Maximus, Prefect of the City, are found only from the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November of that year onward; cf. C. Th. III, 5, ch. 2, On Betrothals. Nor does C. Th. IX, 16, ch. 1, On Malefactors, whose subscription is plainly false, oppose this. See C. Th. VIII, 12, ch. 4, On Donations; C. Th. IX, 10, ch. 3, On the Julian Law concerning Violence; and Corsini, cited work, p. 174. This conjecture is confirmed by manuscripts 33, 34, whose reading “Prefect of the city of Rome” can scarcely otherwise be explained. But I changed nothing because nearly all the other manuscripts have *ppo.*; 40 omits “Pf. P.”]

In all suits, it is our pleasure that a minor who has reached puberty shall not have legal standing unless, by an intervening decree, a curator has been appointed either for administering the estate or for litigation, so that the provisions of our previous foresight may lawfully bring controversies in properly initiated suits to an end in the courts. [Note: [Col. 0177C] b 10, 18 omit “in suits,” and shortly after 15 “of age.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] c Cod. Just. “for the suit.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] d 6–8, 10, 12, 13, 16–18, Til. “or,” which changes the sense of the law; 21, Sich. omit “so that.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] e Cod. Just. “of piety”; 15 “previous decrees”; 16 “provision and”; 9 “statutes.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] f 6–8, 10, 12, 13, 17 “initiator”; 14 “is initiated”; Ri* “curator, so that … the statutes [may be] given”: read “initiated.” Moreover 6, 7 “lawful.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] g 19 “the statutes of Our Serenity, lawfully initiated, [may cause] the controversies of the suit to be tried.”] [Note: [Col. 0177C] h 15, Cod. Just. “the controversy of the suit being tried may be ended”; 21 “are strengthened,” but in the margin “may be ended.”]

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of October at Aquileia, in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time and Licinius Caesar (319). [Note: [Col. 0177C] i 10, 18 “given on the Ides, fourth [day] of October, Aquileia”; 15, 28, 34, 36, 40, Sich. in the margin, Cod. Just. “third.” Go., notes c and l, wishes another month to be given, both for the reason explained in note x and because Constantine was not [Col. 0177D] at Aquileia in this month. But the manuscripts oppose this.] [Note: [Col. 0177D] j 32 “Constantius”; 21 “Constantine Augustus for the second time.” Some manuscripts omit “A.”] [Note: [Col. 0177D] k 30 omits “and Licinius Caesar.” Many manuscripts, Sich.—Lugd., and Cod. Just. omit “Caesar.”]

INTERPRETATION. If an action is brought against minors, although they appear to be adults, they cannot come into court unless their age is established by certification of the curia, or a curator has been appointed to protect the minor’s estate or legal business. [Note: [Col. 0177D] l Thus the manuscripts and editions Sich., Cuj. 1—Cuj. 2*; Go., Ri., Ri*: “estates,” incorrectly Ri.]

## ON BETROTHALS
The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Maximus, Prefect of the City. [Note: [Col. 0177D] m Some MSS: “to Maximus, praetorian prefect.” 10: “Publius.” 28: “Maximus, praetorian prefect.” 8 omits “Prefect of the City.” Editions: “Prefect of the City”; see the Code of Justinian: “Prefect of the City.”] Since the opinion of the ancients displeases us—the opinion which decreed that gifts to a betrothed woman should remain valid even where marriage did not follow [Note: [Col. 0177D] n W. wishes Vatican Fragments §262 and Digest V.1.1, On Gifts (XXXIX, 5), to be compared with this passage.]—we order that those gifts which are lawfully made between betrothed men and women in a spirit of generosity [Col. 0177B] [Note: [Col. 0177D] o 20: “to betrothed women,” with several MSS and Til.; “marriages,” and below “marriage.” This spelling is also retained elsewhere. Then 20: “spirit,” but “in a spirit” above the line.] be reduced to conditions of this sort: [Note: [Col. 0177D] p Some MSS: “the gift which … conditions of this sort, namely.” The Code of Justinian adds: “whether for the purpose of entering into affinity or otherwise”; or the reading which VV. W., in his note on this passage, thinks has been repeated from the Vatican Fragments cited above, discussing this issue at length.] [Col. 0178A] whether they live under the power of a father [Note: [Col. 0178B] a Be.: “equal,” a typographical error. 14: “of a father,” corrected.] or are deemed in any way to be of their own right, [Note: [Col. 0178B] b 6, 7, 14: “their own.”] and, as a gift on account of a future marriage, [Note: [Col. 0178B] c Code of Justinian: “living under authority, or constituted in any way of their own right, as though,” etc. 15: “are deemed to be of their own right.” 20: “to be of their own right.”] [Note: [Col. 0178B] d 6–8, 12, 14, 16, 17, Til. in margin: “of purchase.”] they bestow something upon themselves or upon one another with the consent of their parents; and if the man should not of his own will wish to take the woman as his wife, [Note: [Col. 0178B] e 9 omits “or.” 20: “something to himself,” but “something” inserted between the lines.] [Note: [Col. 0178B] f 19: “should not wish to take a wife.” 20 likewise. Code of Justinian: “if indeed the betrothed man, or his parents, should not wish to take a son a wife.” 15: “if the man voluntarily.” The remaining MSS have “betrothed man” for “voluntarily,” and 6–8, 10, 14, 16, 18 have “wife.”] what has been given by him [Note: [Col. 0178B] g 9 adds “more.”] [Note: [Col. 0178B] h 6–8, 10, 14, 18, 21, Sich.–Lugd.: “given.”] if delivered, is not to be reclaimed; and if anything remains with the donor, [Note: [Col. 0178B] i 16 omits “with.”] [Note: [Col. 0178C] j 10, 18: “lest.” Then some MSS: “remains.”] it shall be transferred to the betrothed woman, [Note: [Col. 0178C] k Code of Justinian adds: “and her heirs.”] with all evasions set aside. [Note: [Col. 0178C] l 6: “with those killed”; 20: “with those removed”; 8 omits both “all” and “evasion.”]

§ 1. But if it is discovered that the cause of not contracting the marriage [Note: [Col. 0178C] m 20: “marriage.”] [Note: [Col. 0178C] n 10, 18 omit “not.”] lay with the betrothed woman, [Note: [Col. 0178C] o 6, 7, 12, 14, 17, 20: “for the purpose of handing over to the betrothed woman,” but 20 inserts between the lines “by the betrothed man.” 15, 19: “by the betrothed man.” 10, 18: “to the betrothed woman.” 8, 16: “of drawing to the betrothed woman.”] or with the person under whose authority she acts, [Note: [Col. 0178C] p Most MSS: “authority,” which is not to be disregarded. 20: “is discovered.” 16 omits “under” after “or.” Code of Justinian: “But if the betrothed woman, or the person under whose authority she acts, has supplied the cause for not contracting the marriage: then to the betrothed man.” Then 15: “then to the betrothed woman.”] it shall then be restored to the betrothed man and his heirs without any diminution. [Note: [Col. 0178C] q 12: “impairment.” 20, Sich., Cuj. 1–Ri*, Code of Justinian: “diminution.” Code of Justinian adds: “by a condiction or by a useful real action.”] [Note: [Col. 0178C] r 9: “were restored”; 12: “were being restored”; 16: “be restored”; 19: “be returned”; 20: “will be returned.” The remaining MSS: “be reclaimed.” Editions before W. and the Code of Justinian: “be reclaimed.” W., conjecturing from Be., emends to “shall be restored.”]

§ 2. The same is likewise to be observed if a gift has been made by the betrothed woman to the betrothed man; [Note: [Col. 0178D] s Some MSS: “to the betrothed man,” which can be defended. 19, 20: “it is proper (omitting ‘and’) that, if a gift has been made from the part of the betrothed woman to her betrothed man.”] [Note: [Col. 0178D] t Here chapter 15 of the Code of Justinian ends, omitting the remainder; the interpreter also says that it is nullified by subsequent laws.] no further grounds are to be investigated, lest perhaps character or birth be alleged, or anything else be advanced which someone considers unsuitable to himself. [Note: [Col. 0178D] u 20: “investigated, lest perhaps death.” Then 15: “be alleged.”] [Note: [Col. 0178D] v 10, 18: “anything.” 12: “but if anyone.” 21: “that to himself.” Sich.: “whereby to himself it is not.” 8 omits “anything else … someone.”] For all these matters ought to have been considered long before the betrothal was contracted. [Col. 0178B] [Note: [Col. 0178D] x Many MSS: “considers.” 15: “may consider.” 21, Sich.: “considers.”] [Note: [Col. 0178D] y 6–8, 14, 16, 17: “are handed over.” 20: “contracted.”] Therefore intention alone shall be examined; and a changed decision of mind shall suffice for the restoration or recovery of the things given, [Note: [Col. 0178D] z Sich.–Lugd.: “perceived.” 9: “ought to have been considered.”] [Note: [Col. 0178D] aa Some MSS: “is needed.” 9: “the matter proceeds from that.”] [Note: [Col. 0178D] bb Thus 6–8, 10, 12, 14, 16–21, Sich.–Lugd.; but 20 inserts between the lines “unchanged,” as appears in the remaining MSS and editions.] [Note: [Col. 0178D] cc 20 inserts “reparation” between the lines, and likewise “decision.” [Col. 0179B] 14 omits “or recovery.” Then 19: “is sufficient.” Sich. has, corruptly, “about to give.”] [Col. 0179A] once every excuse has been excluded, [Note: [Col. 0179B] a Thus 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 16–20, Til., Aur., Lugd.; but Til. in margin has “excuses,” which appears in the remaining MSS and editions.] and nothing further need be established except that it appears that the person has declared that the marriage which he had said he would contract displeases him. [Note: [Col. 0179B] b 12 omits “nothing further.”] [Note: [Col. 0179B] c 6–8, 10, 14, 16, 18: “what he ought to contract for himself.” 15: “who.”]

§ 3. And since it can happen that one person dies while the other’s intention remains unchanged, before the marriage is contracted, [Note: [Col. 0179B] d Some MSS: “because,” and below “unharmed.”] [Note: [Col. 0179B] e 6–8, 14, 16, 17: “are handed over.”] we have considered it fitting that, when the person to whom the gift was made has died before the day of marriage, [Note: [Col. 0179C] f 9: “we have said”; 14: “we shall have considered.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] g 10, 18 omit “when.” 6–8, 14, 20: “him.” 9: “and in.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] h 10: “having died before the day of marriage”; 15: “having died before the marriage day”; 18: “or having died on the marriage day”; 20: “having died.” Perhaps: “having died before marriage.”] things given either under the title of betrothal or by any form whatsoever should be returned to the person who gave them; and, likewise, where the giver has died before the marriage, the gift shall immediately lose force and the things given shall be drawn back to his heirs without any difficulty. [Note: [Col. 0179C] i 6, 7, 10, 14, 18, 21, Sich., Til.: “or by one kind.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] j 20: “him also, to whom the things were given, having died before the marriage, to the person who gave them.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] k 6–8, 10, 12, 16–18, Til.–Ri*: “removed.” 14: “may you remove the gift.” 20: “to remove.” Go. conjectures “drawn back,” supported by MSS 9, 15, 19, 21 and Sich.]

§ 4. We decree that this benefit shall extend as far as the persons of father or mother, and also to children, if any exist from a prior marriage, [Note: [Col. 0179C] l Most MSS and Til.: “or”; the remainder: “and.” Moreover, 6, 7, 10: “person.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] m 10, 18: “if anyone”; 20: “also his, if any, from”; 21, Sich., Lugd.: “if indeed from a prior marriage.”] [Note: [Col. 0179C] n 9: “from his own marriage they were.”] provided that some person from among these succeeds to the deceased in any manner. [Note: [Col. 0179C] o 20 inserts “persons” between the lines. Then some MSS: “of the deceased”; others omit “if” after “provided that.”] But if none of these persons is found to be heir of the deceased, [Col. 0179B] [Note: [Col. 0179C] p Thus 6–8, 10, 12, 14, 16–18, 20: “is found”; but the editions have “will be,” as do 9, 15, 19, 21.] and someone succeeds from the remaining degrees of relationship, the gifts must remain valid even though the marriage has not followed because of death, since we believe provision should be made only for those persons. [Note: [Col. 0179D] q 15: “will be fitting.” 21: “of the gift.”] [Note: [Col. 0179D] r 9: “we believed.”] Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, [Note: [Col. 0179D] s 12, 24 omit “seventeenth”; 29: fifteenth; 20, 30, 33, 34: seventh; Anianus, of excellent authority in Go., and the Code of Justinian: sixteenth; Hal.: seventeenth; 31: eighth; 44: eighteenth.] published on the sixth day before the Kalends of Stassus [uncertain reading], [Note: [Col. 0179D] t 8, 12: tenth. Code of Justinian and Sich. in margin: “P.P.” for “Prop.”] [Note: [Col. 0179D] u Thus most MSS; perhaps there is an error in the date-marking of the subscription, which the editions reproduce. It is obscure, since the law could not have been published before it was given. Be. and W. think the names of the months should be reversed: “Given on the sixth day before the Kalends of September; published on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November.” 10, 18: “aforesaid.” Editions and Code of Justinian: “September.”] at Rome, [Note: [Col. 0179D] v MSS: “Rome” or “at Rome”; editions and Code of Justinian: “at Rome.”] in the consulship of Constantine Augustus for the fifth time [Note: [Col. 0179D] x 32: fifteenth; 43: tenth.] and Licinius Caesar. [Note: [Col. 0179D] y 6, 7, 9, 14, 21, Sich., Til.: “consuls V.C.” 24, 29: “L. VCC.” 19: “Licinius Augustus, consuls.” Moreover, “November … Kalends” is omitted in MSS 9, 33, 42; “published … Stassus” in MSS 19, 20, 24; “Kalends of Stassus … consuls” in MS 28; “at Rome” in MSS 16, 31, 32, 44; “fifth” in MSS 8, 10, 18, 40; “Caesar” in MSS 8, 15, 10, 30, 31, 33, 38, 40 and in the Code of Justinian.] (319).

[Col. 0180A] INTERPRETATION.
