## CONCERNING THE DIGNITY OF PERFECTISSIMATE RANK

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Paternus Valerianus.

> [Col. 0349C] s Go. notes: “Thus far the Theodosian manuscript; for what follows here Cujas supplied from the Justinian Code.” “But it is now clear from the manuscript which I collated that these words were wrongly inserted here by the editors. For it does not end here, but at the words ‘or not in any.’ All manuscripts of the Justinian Code read Justinian; Cujas printed Constantine.”  
> [Col. 0349D] t In the manuscript Valerianus’s rank is missing. Go. conjectures that Valerianus was prefect of the praetorium or vice-prefect of the city. The law may then conveniently be assigned to 330, since chapter 3 of the Theodosian Code, *Concerning Betrothals* (III.5), is addressed to Valerianus acting as vice-prefect. The rank is absent also from the Justinian Code; Aurelius and Lugdunensis read “the Emperors” for “the Emperor.”

Those who have obtained codicils of perfectissimate rank shall enjoy them, provided that they are free from servile status, are not liable to the fisc or to a curia, are not shepherds, are not engaged in any business or occupation [the manuscript leaf ends after *vel non in aliquo*, “or not in any”; the continuation is restored as explained in note v], have not purchased their honour by venal influence, and have not administered another person’s property . . . . . .

> [Col. 0349D] u Justinian Code, and also Cujas, read “shall enjoy, those who have obtained.”  
> [Col. 0349D] v Cujas restored what follows from the Justinian Code. In place of the asterisk by which Cujas 1—Cujas 2* marks a gap, I have placed dashes for the same purpose. At the words *vel non in aliquo*, “or not in any,” folio XLIV ends; it is the sixth leaf of quire XXXVII, whose number appears on folio XXXVIII. But the number of quire XXXVIII appears in the margin of folio XLVI; this shows that no leaf of this quire is missing. Nevertheless, after folio XLIV some inserted parchment was cut out. On it, besides the end of this constitution, was written the red rubric for Book VII; this circumstance provided the reason for cutting out the parchment. For when the copyist had left some blank space for the sake of neatness, this parchment was removed for another use, as happened elsewhere in the manuscript—for example, at the end of Book VII, where material that the copyist had not filled in for the sake of appearance was cut out by a barbarous hand. How much was lost with the cut-out parchment can, however, be determined by chance. It happened that on the second page of folio XLIV traces remained of the red colour which had been on the first page of that cut-out parchment. In that colour copyists customarily wrote the formula closing a book; here, therefore, Book VI. It is thus apparent that only one page is missing, containing the end of this constitution and the formula just mentioned; so that at this point the Theodosian Code agrees entirely with the Justinian Code, in which, immediately after this title, the text passes to military affairs, the subject of Book VII of the Theodosian Code. On the reverse side of the cut-out leaf there was beyond doubt, in highly ornate letters, the formula indicating the beginning of a new book, here Book VII. The preserved number of the title *Concerning Military Affairs*, which is first, proves that the beginning of Book VII is complete.

## CONCERNING THE JEWS

[Col. 0350A]

Constantine Augustus to Ablavius, Prefect of the Praetorium. Those who have devoted themselves wholly to the synagogues of the Jews, to patriarchs or presbyteries, and who, remaining in the aforesaid sect, themselves preside over the law, shall continue exempt from all duties, both personal and civic. Thus, those who perhaps are already decurions shall in no way be assigned to any official escort duties, since persons of this kind ought not to be compelled by any means to depart from the places in which they are established; while those who are not curiales at all shall enjoy perpetual immunity from the decurionate. Given on the third day before the Kalends of December at Constantinople, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Symmachus (330).

> [Col. 0350C] b Go. wishes to read *patriarchiis vel presbyteriis*, “patriarchies or presbyteries,” because these correspond to synagogues and because the words “from the places in which they are established” follow below. MS 11 reads *sinagogis*, “synagogues,” consistently.

> [Col. 0350D] f MS 11: *desinentur*. Go.: “Another reading, *designentur*, ‘be assigned.’”

> [Col. 0350D] h MS 4 reads *curianatus*, corrected in red ink to *curionatus*, which Til. has.

Go. too notes: “another reading, Bassus; wrongly.” In his commentary he demonstrates by many arguments that the consuls of 330 must be retained, even though this makes the law later than the following one. The compilers of the Theodosian Code made an error and disturbed the sequence of the laws. For this constitution ought to have been third under this title, whereas the third ought to have been placed here. Examples of this kind of error are not lacking in the Theodosian Code. See above VII.8.7–8; VII.18.16–17.

## CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF THE REC. [abbreviation retained in the source]

The Emperor Constantine Augustus to Valerianus, acting vice-prefect. Although the law is not ordinarily accustomed to assist women ignorant of their legal rights in matters of gain, nevertheless earlier enactments of the emperors declare that this rule has no place against age which is still imperfect. Given on the third day before the Kalends of May, in the consulship of Gallicanus and Symmachus, 330.

In the year of the Lord 331, in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius.

## CONCERNING APPEALS

Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Prefect of the Praetorium.

> [Col. 0351B] a MS 39 and Sichard in the margin read “proconsul”; MSS 10 and 18, “official in charge”; MS 20, “prefect”; MS 21, “prefect of the city”; MS 15 and other manuscripts omit “Prefect of the Praetorium.” Go., in his chronology for this year, notes “Prefect of the City, wrongly.”

The promulgation of the law which protects, by a prescription of sixteen years, those who have remained in freedom in good faith during that period against persons who disturb them, does not assist those born of slave mothers and freeborn fathers who have remained, together with their parents, in the appearance of freedom for that period. For, when no just beginning of lawful possession preceded, a bare claim of freedom is asserted, since neither redemption from slavery nor delivery of a substitute slave nor assignment of a peculium can be shown—titles which might free from the bonds of servitude the person against whom suit is brought, if by any one of these means he had remained in the enjoyment of freedom for sixteen years. For by common law a child necessarily follows the condition of the mother, so that, even if a slave woman has concealed her master’s bed, she bears offspring for the master, not as free persons but as slaves. Given on the day before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

Go. nevertheless correctly believes that some lost law of Constantine is indicated; Unterholzner accepts this view, *Development of the Entire Law of Prescription*, Leipzig, 1828, octavo, vol. II, p. 396, note 809.

INTERPRETATION. A law had at one time been promulgated that, if anyone [Note: [Col. 0351D] x Many manuscripts: “who.”] had lived for sixteen years without any [Note: [Col. 0351D] y Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “some.”] disturbance, with no one reclaiming or bringing suit against him, and [Note: [Col. 0351D] z *et* is absent in many manuscripts; in others, as in MS 8, it occurs later. MS 43 has *but* for *and*.] thereafter did not come into slavery [Col. 0352A]. But this [Note: [Col. 0352B] a MSS 9, 42, and others: “nor.”] will not be able to benefit those whom [Note: [Col. 0352B] b Some manuscripts: “because.”] it is established were begotten by freeborn fathers [Note: [Col. 0352B] c MS 8: “parents”; MS 20: “fathers or from the column,” and shortly afterwards “begotten,” with others, “into union.”] and colona women or female slaves, unless perhaps their fathers, for the person of their sons, have paid to the masters whose female slaves they have in union either substitute slaves with their peculia or the redemption price of their status. But if the fathers [Note: [Col. 0352B] d MSS 7, 8: “shares,” but MS 7 corrected to “fathers”; MS 20 adds: “fathers or substitute slaves or the things mentioned above” [corrected from “are” to “are mentioned”], and omits “this.”] do not show that they have paid this, they will not be able to alter the condition of their mothers [Note: [Col. 0352B] e Thus most manuscripts; editions: “will not be able,” “the mothers’ condition.”] or cause slaves [Note: [Col. 0352C] f MS 20: “to render others from their own [above the line: another’s] property likewise,” and omits “to perish to their masters”; MSS 6, 7, 21: “from the former,” but MS 7 corrected to “to perish.”] to cease belonging to their masters, even if they are born from their own masters [Note: [Col. 0352C] g The following text is absent from MS 15. Many manuscripts: “are born.”], unless by manumission they can cease to be subject to servile condition [Note: [Col. 0352C] h MSS 6–10, 20, 42–44, and others: “servile condition … can”; MS 21, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “to receive servile condition” [thus MS 21 in the margin], “not able”; MS 20: “can.” The following text is absent from MSS 6–10, 13, 17–21, 25–34, 36–40, 42–44; from Sich.; and from the old books cited by Go. It also ends in the epitomes Br. and Al., except L, R, and U. In MS 47 only the following words are transmitted, the preceding words being omitted. In MS 14 there is grave confusion at this point; this is nevertheless not alien to Go.’s opinion, which refers these words to some lost constitution. For in MS 14, after “not able,” the rubric “If anyone living in freedom” is first placed; after that rubric follows the inscription of chapter 9 of this title, as though a new law began. In place of the text of the law occur the words of the Interpretation, “A female slave … origin”; and in place of the Interpretation, immediately after “origin,” occur the words of law 9 of this title itself. [Col. 0352D]]. If anyone living in freedom has joined a female slave to himself in marriage, and children have been born of them, their origin shall follow the mother. Likewise, if a freedwoman takes a slave as husband, descent shall follow the slave, because origin passes to the lower-status person.

## CONCERNING EXPOSED CHILDREN

[Col. 0352B]

Emperor Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0352D] i MSS 6, 7, 10, 18, 21, 40, 44, Sich., Til.: “the same Augustus,” doubtless because of the constitution preceding this title; Cuj. 1 and Be.: “Constantine.”] to Ablavius, Praetorian Prefect [Note: [Col. 0352D] j Some manuscripts: “Ablavius”; MS 19: “to Albinus, PPO.”]. Whoever takes up a boy or girl cast out [Note: [Col. 0352D] k MS 15: “those cast out.”] from a house, with the consent and knowledge of father or master, and brings the child up by his own maintenance to strength [Note: [Col. 0352D] l MS 12: “with the knowledge of those who take up from their own”; MS 14: “with willing knowledge and takes up”; MS 15: “with his knowledge takes up”; MS 20: “with knowledge who takes up,” corrected to “with knowledge takes up.”] [Note: [Col. 0352D] m The words “to strength” are absent from MSS 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, and from Sich. and Til.; the preceding words are received in Cuj. 1.], shall retain that person in whatever status [Note: [Col. 0352D] n The words “the status which he prefers” were transposed by the scribe of MS 29 into the following, sole chapter of the next title, after “owed.”] he wishes for one taken into his household [Note: [Col. 0352D] o Be. and W. rightly restored *collectum* (“taken up”), which had passed from Cuj. 2 into the editions of Go., Ri., and Ri*.; but all manuscripts inspected by the editor, and Sich. and Lugd., read *collectum*.], to treat [Note: [Col. 0352D] p MSS 10, 18 omit “to treat as he wishes.”] him—namely, whether he wishes him to be a son or a slave. Every disturbance of reclamation [Note: [Col. 0352D] q MS 15 omits “of reclamation.”] on the part of those who knowingly and voluntarily cast out of their house slaves or freeborn children [Col. 0353A] [Note: [Col. 0353B] a Most manuscripts, Sich., Lugd.: “slaves and freeborn children.”] newly born [Note: [Col. 0353B] b MS 20: “masters.”] is to be wholly removed [Note: [Col. 0353C] c MS 15: “ejected”; MS 20: “removed,” but above the line “cast out,” as in MS 19.]. Given on the fifteenth [Note: [Col. 0353C] d MSS 13, 15: “twelfth”; MS 19: “sixteenth”; MS 20, 40, and Sich. in the margin; Go. in the note to the chronology: “fifth.”] day before the Kalends of May [Note: [Col. 0353C] e Many manuscripts and Mad.; MS 8 omits “May”; “Constantine.”] at Constantinople [Note: [Col. 0353C] f MS 20 and others: “to Constantinople”; many manuscripts, Sich., and Lugd. omit “Constantinople.”], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

INTERPRETATION. Whoever takes up a child exposed immediately after birth, with the knowledge of father, mother, or master, and raises it by his own labor, shall remain in the power of the person by whom he was taken up, whether that person wishes the child whom he has nourished to be freeborn or a slave [Note: [Col. 0353C] g The following text is absent from all manuscripts seen by the editor and from Sich., Cuj. 1, and Lugd. Since its subject-matter is not found in this law, these words are either spurious or added by a scribe who used a manuscript fuller at this point. They were first published in Cuj. 2. The reading is, moreover, “slavery.”], and, if he wishes to adopt the child as a son or freedman, or to remain in slavery, he shall exercise his own authority.

## CONCERNING REPUDIATION

[Note: [Col. 0353C] h Codex Justinianus V.17 adds: “and with the action concerning morals removed.”]

Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0353C] i Editions, Sich., Cuj. 1–2*: “Constantine.” This chapter begins in MS 13. MSS 8, 15, 25: “to Ablavius”; MSS 14, 34: “to Albinus”; MS 26: “to Flavius.”] Augustus to Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0353C] j MS 32: “to Albino”; MS 33: “to Libanus”; MS 38: “to Bravius.”], Praetorian Prefect [Note: [Col. 0353C] k Some manuscripts omit “Praetorian Prefect,” and others have “to the prefect.”]. It is our pleasure that a woman not be permitted, because of her own improper [Note: [Col. 0353C] l MS 13: “It is our pleasure and woman.”] desires [Note: [Col. 0353D] m MS 9: “small”; Sich.: “evil.”], to send repudiation to her husband except for an established cause [Note: [Col. 0353D] n MS 19: “to send unless established.”], such as his being a drunkard, gambler [Note: [Col. 0353D] o MS 9: “flatterer”; MS 10: “aleator”; MSS 15, 18: “elator”; MS 21 shortly afterwards: “of little women.”], or womanizer; nor, indeed, may husbands dismiss their wives upon any pretexts [Note: [Col. 0353D] p MSS 6, 7, 14, 16, 17 omit “upon any pretexts”; MS 8: “upon any accusation.”] whatsoever [Note: [Col. 0353D] q MS 10: “dismiss their wives”; MS 9: “shall dismiss.”]. But when repudiation is sent by a woman, only these crimes are to be investigated: whether she proves her husband to be a murderer, poisoner, or violator of tombs [Note: [Col. 0353D] r MS 15, the Seld. manuscript cited by Go.: “violator”; MS 17: “poisoner, but tombs”; MS 13 subsequently omits “that.”] [Note: [Col. 0353D] s MS 14: “her husband.”], so that only then, being commended, she receives back all her dowry [Note: [Col. 0353D] t MSS 15, 18: “her dowry.”]. For if, apart from these [Note: [Col. 0353D] u MS 12 omits “these.”] three crimes, she sends repudiation to her husband, she must leave in her husband’s house everything down to the hairpin [Note: [Col. 0353D] v Sich. and Til.: *aciculam*, “little needle,” though Til. in the margin has *acuculam*, “hairpin”; some manuscripts: *ucuculam*; MS 15, according to Go.: *acticulam*; in MS 21 this word was added by a second hand.] on her head, and, for such great presumption on her part, be deported to an island [Note: [Col. 0353D] x MSS 15, 19: “into the house.”] [Note: [Col. 0353D] y Some manuscripts: “assigned on an island.”].

Likewise, in the case of men [Note: [Col. 0353D] z MS 12: “in male persons.”] who send repudiation, these three crimes are to be investigated: whether he wishes to repudiate an adulteress [Col. 0354A] [Note: [Col. 0354B] a Manuscripts: *mecam*, *moecam*, *moccam*; MS 14: “if [he wishes to repudiate] an adulteress or a poisoner or a procuress.”], poisoner, or procuress [Note: [Col. 0354C] b MSS 6, 7, 10, 16, 18: plural, “they wish,” not wrongly.]. For if he casts her out free of these [Note: [Col. 0354C] c Sich., Cuj. 1–Ri*: “these.”] crimes [Note: [Col. 0354C] d MS 13: “elicits”; MS 15 adds “someone.”], he must restore the whole dowry [Note: [Col. 0354C] e MS 19: “ought.”] and not take another wife. But if he does so, the former wife [Note: [Col. 0354C] f MS 9: “of the former marriage.”] shall have authority to enter his house [Note: [Col. 0354C] g Thus most manuscripts and Eill.; other editions: “his house”; MS 9: “his houses”; MS 18: “shall be given, his house.”] and transfer to herself the whole dowry of the later wife [Note: [Col. 0354C] h MS 15 omits “wife.”] [Note: [Col. 0354C] i MS 16: “to himself.”], because of the injury done to her. Given on the third day before the Nones of May [Note: [Col. 0354C] j MSS 10, 18 and manuscripts cited by Go.’s note: “given on the tenth day before the Kalends of June”; MSS 28, 36, 40: “given on the tenth day before the Kalends of July”; MS 36: “given on the seventh day before the Kalends of July, at Toledo”; manuscripts cited by Go.: “given on the third day before the Kalends of July”; Sich. in the margin: “Kalends of July”; Til. in the margin: “Kalends of July”; MS 19: “Nones of December.” Til.: “given … May–July.” MSS 9, 13–16, 14, 27, 29–35, 38, 43, 44 omit “third day before the Nones of May,” though some manuscripts, such as 6 and 7, leave a space. Thus only few manuscripts support the date printed in editions. The origin of “at Toledo” in MS 39 is unknown to the editor.], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

INTERPRETATION. Repudiation between wife and husband is available on the basis of specific matters and established causes; for they are forbidden to dissolve marriage on a slight accusation [Note: [Col. 0354D] k Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “to be dissolved is forbidden”; MS 43 adds “not.”]. If, perhaps, a woman says that her husband is either drunken [Note: [Col. 0354D] l Some manuscripts omit “either drunken”; subsequently MS 6 has “if perhaps” for “unless perhaps,” and MS 21: “violator of tombs.”] or given to debauchery, he is not therefore to be repudiated, unless perhaps she proves him to be either a murderer, a sorcerer (*maleficus*), or a violator of a tomb. Convicted of these crimes [Col. 0354B], he rightly seems to be excluded without fault on the woman’s part, and the woman departs after recovering her dowry. But if the woman cannot establish these crimes, she is punished [Note: [Col. 0354D] m Some manuscripts, Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “changed”; MS 43: “let her be changed.”] in this manner: she loses both the dowry that she gave, or [Note: [Col. 0354D] n Sich. in the margin: “or”; in MS 21 substituted by a second hand.] which had been given on her behalf, and the gift that she received; she is also held under relegation into exile.

But if a woman is rejected by her husband, he likewise may not, unless he proves her guilty of definite crimes [Note: [Col. 0354D] o MS 44: “will be rejected, nor will he prove”; MS 21 and Sich.: “prove her.”], repudiate her for a slight quarrel, as commonly happens [Note: [Col. 0354D] p Many manuscripts: “commonly happens.”] [Note: [Col. 0354D] q MSS 6–8, 10, 14, 18 and other manuscripts, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd., add “not”; Ri. approves. Cuj. 2–Ri* omit it wrongly.], unless perhaps [Note: [Col. 0354D] r Many manuscripts: “perhaps.”] it suffices to prove her an adulteress, sorceress, or procuress [Note: [Col. 0354D] s MSS 6–8, 43, and others omit “her,” though MS 6 has “to prove.”] [Note: [Col. 0354D] t Aur. and Lugd. here add: “for then he may recover the gift for himself and may dismiss her.”]. But if [Note: [Col. 0354D] u Sich. adds “this”; subsequently MSS 6, 7: “will be able.”] he cannot prove this, he shall restore the dowry to the woman and shall not presume to take another wife [Note: [Col. 0354D] v Some manuscripts: “take another wife not presume.”]. But if he perhaps attempts this, the woman [Col. 0355A] who was innocently cast out shall have free [Note: [Col. 0355C] a Some manuscripts omit “free,” and subsequently “all.”] power to claim for herself her husband’s house and all his property. This is known to have been ordained so that a woman unjustly repudiated [Note: [Col. 0355C] b MS 21 and Sich.: “repudiated woman.”] may also be ordered to acquire the dowry of the second wife.

## CONCERNING HONORARY CODICILS

Constantine Augustus . . . . . [Note: [Col. 0355C] c In place of the asterisk printed in editions, six dots have been placed: a gap of that many letters appears in the manuscript, though nothing has been erased or cut away. Go., because of the subscription to some praetorian prefect of Gaul, whose seat was Trier, believes this law was addressed to him.] That those [Note: [Col. 0355C] d The manuscript and editions before Be. read “hii.”] who are far from the service of your Sublimity, displaying no merit through diligence or services, may not seize a position owed to those who have labored, it is our pleasure that clerks advance to the registers according to their place and rank, be appointed to their administration, and, with the others passed over [the transmitted *prosultatis* is uncertain] [Note: [Col. 0355C] e Go. emends “into a place … seize” or “a place … pre-empt,” without cause.], so that each among the clerks may attain, according to the place that he has deserved to acquire by time, advancement in rank and merit [Note: [Col. 0355C] f Be. approves the conjunction; Go. laments it in his notes.]. Given [Note: [Col. 0355C] g Go. and Bon., loc. cit. p. 747, note a, have “returned” for “given.”] on the Kalends of July at Trier [Note: [Col. 0355C] h Manuscript, Go., Bon.: “Triberis”; Cuj. 1–Cuj. 2*, Ri., Ri*: “Triveris.”], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Col. 0355B] (331).

Constantine Augustus to all provincials. After other matters: If there is a boundary dispute, then [Note: [Col. 0355C] i Barb.: “you.”] and only then an arbiter [Note: [Col. 0355C] j Pith., Barb.: “arbiters”; Laur.: “arbitres.”] shall not be denied [Note: [Col. 0355D] k Pith., Laur., Barb.: “shall not be denied,” plural.], when it is established that the place at issue before the governor lies within [Note: [Col. 0355D] l Barb.: “against.”] five feet. But when a case concerns a larger area [Note: [Col. 0355D] m The following text is absent from Laur. and Barb. as far as “governor.”] [Note: [Col. 0355D] n Goes. in the margin conjectures: “a certain space that is not boundary land.”] and is not a boundary case but one of ownership [Note: [Col. 0355D] o Pith. in the margin: “which now”;] [Note: [Col. 0355D] p Pith., Gud. in the margin, and Sich. add “is.”], it must be decided before the governor himself. And if one partner seeks anything from another, the governor must first decide whether anything ought to be rendered; only then shall that which is established [Note: [Col. 0355D] q Barb.: “who,” corrected to “what.”] [Note: [Col. 0355D] r Barb., by a second hand: “if anything.”] [Note: [Col. 0355D] s Goes. in the margin conjectures “shall have established.”] to be payable be restored through arbiters. Given on the Kalends of August [Note: [Col. 0355D] t Chapter 17 and chapter 1 cited add “posted on the Kalends of September,” and chapter 16 “posted on the Kalends of September, at Constantinople.”], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0355D] u Thus rightly Sich., Gud. in the margin, Laur., Barb., Cuj. 1–Cuj. 2*; Rig.: “Abladius”; Goes.: “Abladeus”; Go.–Ri*: “Albavius.”] (331).

## CONCERNING THE ADMINISTRATION AND LIABILITY OF GUARDIANS AND CURATORS

Constantine Augustus to [Note: [Col. 0355D] v MS 1 has “niversos provinciales,” the letters “Id. A. ad u.” having been torn away. In what follows all the letters in the fourth leaf of MS 1 have been torn away and restored by editors; for brevity, the editor indicates them with italics [Col. 0356B]. P. and Pu. customarily enclose their restorations in brackets; this is stated once for all.] all provincials. After [Col. 0356A] other matters: If defenders of minors, as also [Note: [Col. 0356B] a MS 1: “defenders . . . . . t.” Four further letters have perished, restored by P.; Bijdr., loc. cit., p. 325, conjectures *velut*, “such as,” on Gaius’s authority.] tutors or curators, being participants in the property sought by litigation [Note: [Col. 0356B] b MS 1: “litae.”], refuse, as ordered, to enter them in the record [Note: [Col. 0356B] c At this point MS 1 has a gap of about six letters. P. conjectures *pos(citur ac)ta*, “the property sought [in the] record”; so also Pu. But W., in E. L. L. 1824, p. 1903, and in his edition of the Theodosian Code, more correctly reads *poscitur ad acta*, “is sought, [enter it] in the record.”] [Note: [Col. 0356B] d MS 1: “detractaverint.”] and name them contrary to the truth [Note: [Col. 0356B] e P., in notes, prefers “and the same,” not “the same,” as Pu., note b, maintains.] [Note: [Col. 0356B] f MS 1 reads “named contrary to truth.” P. wishes to read “named [them] for sale,” attempting an implausibly contorted explanation from Cod. Just. VIII.37.4; W. and Bijdr., loc. cit., reject it. See W., p. 192, note b. Pu. indicates a triple gap, enclosing a dot in brackets. W., in E. L. L., loc. cit., and his Theodosian Code, supplies “contrary to truth”; the editor confesses he knows no more suitable supplement, especially since W.’s remarks are very plausible: this passage coheres with the sole constitution of C. Th. IV.4, *Concerning Litigious Property*, and refers to a requirement imposed on defendants, under loss of a third part, to name in the record defendants who share in the litigated property, although no other trace of this requirement is found in Roman law. Whether it is connected with the subject of C. Th. II.14, *That the Names of More Powerful Persons [Not Be Used]*, is doubtful.]—since nothing ought to be lost by a pupil or adult in any outcome of litigation [Note: [Col. 0356C] g MS 1: “eventus,” corrected to “eventu.”]—they shall pay into the public treasury from their own funds a sum equal, after valuation [Note: [Col. 0356C] h MS 1: “valuation.”], to one-third of the assessed amount. But if they are poor [Note: [Col. 0356C] i P., on the word “poor,” notes: “Before the letters *eres* there appears such an end-stroke of a letter [Col. 0356D] as suggests either *d* or *p*.”], let them be punished by diminution of civic status and cease to be Roman citizens, while the full right is reserved to the minors themselves, etc. Given [Note: [Col. 0356D] j The letters “etc. Given” have been torn from the manuscript.] on the Kalends of August, under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0356D] k MS 1 and P.: “Ablatio”; Pu.: “Ablutis,” absurdly.] (331).

## CONCERNING LITIGIOUS PROPERTY

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the provincials. After other matters [Note: [Col. 0356D] l Some manuscripts omit “to the provincials. After other matters”; others have merely “after other matters,” as Cod. Just.; or merely “to the provincials.”]: While litigation is pending [Note: [Col. 0356D] m MSS 6, 7, 21: “pandente”; MSS 10, 18: “pensante.”], that which is brought into [Note: [Col. 0356D] n MSS 10, 18 omit “into”; MSS 6, 7, 16: “dispute.”] controversy [Note: [Col. 0356D] o Cod. Just.: “While litigation is pending, actions brought into judgment, or things for which the plaintiff brings an action against the defendant holding them”; MS 15 omits “is brought”; MS 9: “is brought if joined.”] may by no means be transferred, whether to a connected person or [Note: [Col. 0356D] p MSS 10, 18: “connected and only or.”] an outsider [Col. 0356B], by gifts, purchases, or any other contracts [Note: [Col. 0356D] q MS 18: “contractions”; subsequently MS 12: “the suit to be pursued.”], since the suit is nevertheless to be pursued as though nothing [Note: [Col. 0356D] r Cod. Just.: “may be transferred by that plaintiff, as though if nothing.”] had been done [Note: [Col. 0356D] s Here ends chapter 2 of the cited Codex Justinianus. What follows is wholly fugitive; Go. thinks, because arbiters are mentioned, that it belongs to C. Th. II.26.3, *On Boundaries*; Wenck assigns it to C. Th. *On the Administration of Guardians*.].

§ 1. But if the matter concerns guardianship [Note: [Col. 0357C] a MSS 8, 12, 16: “what is useful” for “if the matter concerns guardianship”; MS 19: “if a useful case appears.” Some manuscripts in what follows transpose “after examination … arbiters are to be appointed.”], after examination by the judge, arbiters shall be appointed to supplement the judgment; they are to be regarded not now [Note: [Col. 0357C] b MS 15: “now not”; Sich. and Til. subsequently omit “etc.”] as arbiters, but as executors, etc. Given on the Kalends [Note: [Col. 0357C] c MSS 16, 28, 35, 36, 40, Sich.–Cuj. 2, and Be. add “tenth”; Ri., Ri., and W., with Go.’s authority, rightly delete that number. In all laws of C. Th. that the editor said should be joined with this chapter, “tenth” is absent. Moreover all manuscripts agree with W. except the five named.] of August [Note: [Col. 0357C] d Cod. Just.: “Given on the Kalends of March … Ablabius,” wrongly.], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

INTERPRETATION. Property claimed by an action already brought cannot be transferred by the possessor to another through any contracts; nor may any document concerning it be made unless the suit at issue has first been settled by judgment [Note: [Col. 0357C] e Some manuscripts: “it is not permitted, if the suit at issue has not first been settled in judgment.” Aur., Lugd., Go., Ri., Ri. add: “Or thus: Litigious property cannot in any way be given or sold before the case is litigated.” Those words drawn from the *Regulae* cannot be regarded as an Interpretation.].

## CONCERNING EXACTIONS

Constantine Augustus to all provincials. We permit appeals from proconsuls, counts, and those who hear cases in the place of prefects, whether they have judged upon appeal, by delegation [Note: [Col. 0357D] f Ri*, wrongly: “are heard.”] [Note: [Col. 0357D] g Cod. Just.: “from delegation.”], or in the ordinary course; provided that the judge gives the appellant a copy of his opinion [Note: [Col. 0357D] h Folio 186a of MS 4.] [Col. 0357B] and sends the record, together with the period for reply and his own letters, to us. But from praetorian prefects, who alone may truly be said to hear cases by vice-sacral authority [Note: [Col. 0357D] i Ri., not in the vulgate as Be. asserts: “From prefects,” a typographical error.] [Note: [Col. 0357D] j Cod. Just. omits “who … are.”], we do not permit appeal [Note: [Col. 0357D] k Cod. Just.: “to appeal.”], lest our veneration now seem to be touched. But if the defeated party asserts that he offered an appeal which the judge did not receive, let him approach the prefects so that he may litigate anew before them as though the appeal had been accepted. For if the defeated party is found to have appealed [Note: [Col. 0357D] l Cod. Just.: “to appeal.”] unjustly, he shall depart marked by loss of the suit; but [Note: [Col. 0357D] m MS 4 and Til.–Ri*: “but.” At Be.’s direction Go. restored “but” from Cod. Just.; yet “or” can be retained, although “but” is undeniably more pointed. Russian editions of Cod. Just. read “or” with C. Th. and, after Go., some Cod. Just. editions and manuscripts.] if he prevails, it is necessary that the matter be reported to us against the judge who had not received [Note: [Col. 0357D] n Rio. and Cod. Just.: “had received.”] the appeal, so that he may be punished by an appropriate penalty. Given on the Kalends of August, posted on the Kalends of September, at Constantinople, under the consulship of Bassus and [Note: [Col. 0357D] o Aur. and Lugd.: “consuls.”] Ablavius (331).

Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0357D] p In Ri* “Augustus” has dropped out.] to all provincials. Whoever omits a lawful appeal must remain silent forever [Col. 0357C] and must not insolently seek assistance from us by petition [Col. 0358A]. If he does so, he is to be punished by deportation [Note: [Col. 0358C] a Cod. Just.: “If he does so, he shall be deprived of his request and marked by the penalty of disgrace.”]. Given on the Kalends of August, posted on the Kalends of September, at Constantinople [Note: [Col. 0358C] b From laws to be joined with this chapter. In MS 4 and editions “Constantine” is absent.], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

## CONCERNING THOSE WHO DID NOT APPEAL THROUGH FEAR OF THE JUDGE

[Note: [Col. 0358D] c Thus MS 4 and Til.–Cuj. 2v; Cod. Just. and the index of titles in Go.–Rio.: “appealed.” Go.–Be.: “appealed.” Subsequently MS 4 and editions before Be.: “hii.”]

Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0358D] d Cuj. 2, 2*: “Constantius.”] Augustus to all provincials. Those who, having omitted an appeal, attempt to reopen a suit against the judgments of counts and other persons who have pronounced judgment in our voice, asserting relief because the appeal was omitted through fear [the transmitted phrase is defective: *firmantes, se per metum appellationis omissae auxilium*] [Note: [Col. 0358D] e Go. and Be. emend to *omisisse*, “to have omitted,” as in the margin of Cuj. 1–Cuj. 2*, rightly. Til.–Cuj. 2* omit “relief in this matter.” Go.–Ri* omit “relief: in this matter.”], are to be deported to an island with loss of all property, which is to be assigned to the treasury. In this matter judgment shall belong either to us or, by our command, to the praetorian prefects. Given on the Kalends of August, posted on the Kalends of September [Note: [Col. 0358D] f Add “at Constantinople.” See C. Th. XI.30.16, *On Appeals*.], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

[Col. 0358B] Emperor Constantine Augustus to all provincials. If anyone possesses an immovable thing in another’s name in any fashion and is sued by someone through a real action, he must immediately name the owner in court, whether that owner lives in the same city, in the countryside, or in another province. Within a fixed number of days, to be determined by the judge and brought to his notice [the source’s *nationem* is an apparent OCR corruption], the owner must either himself come to the places where the estate is situated or send an agent to answer the plaintiff’s claims. [The source marks a textual boundary here with “+”.] But if, after such time has been granted, he chooses not to do what has been ordered, then the suit brought against him shall be deemed joined, from the day when the possessor was summoned to court, so as to interrupt prescription by long time. After this indulgence, if the owner of the possession fails to appear [Col. 0358C] [the transmitted wording appears to omit the necessary negation], the judge shall ensure that he is summoned by lawful edicts being posted. If he persists in the same intention, the judge, summarily examining the matter, shall not delay in putting the plaintiff into possession of the property, while preserving for the absent party every allegation concerning the principal issue. Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of August, under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius, 331.

## CONCERNING THE SONS OF MILITARY APPARITORS

Constantine Augustus to Evagrius [Note: [Col. 0358D] g The dignity is absent from editions and also from the manuscript, but without any sign of a gap. Cod. Just.: “Emperor Constantine Augustus to Evagrius.” Evagrius was Praetorian Prefect; see cited chapter 20, *On Decurions*.]. Those born of officials of whatever offices [Note: [Col. 0358D] h Thus Be., rightly printed from Cod. Just. on Go.’s authority; manuscript and Cuj. 1–Ri*: “of whatever.”], while their parents are still bound by their oath of service, or after they have already been discharged [Note: [Col. 0358D] i Cod. Just.: “have been discharged shall be summoned into their parents’ service.” Go. regards the transmitted wording as more elegant.], shall advance into their parents’ positions. Given [Col. 0359A] on the day before the Nones [Note: [Col. 0359B] a Chapter 20, *On Decurions*: “the day before the Ides,” which must be changed to “the day before the Nones.”] of August, under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

## CONCERNING DECURIONS

Constantine Augustus to Evagrius, Praetorian Prefect [Note: [Col. 0359B] b “Praetorian Prefect” restored from MS 9 and chapter 20 of this title. Go. and Be. agree. MSS 4, Sich.–Cuj. 2*: the dignity is omitted; Be. do not indicate its omission. Go. and Ri. print six dots, Ri* five. MSS 9, 20, 29, 36, 40: “Ebargius”; MS 11: “Evacrius” and omits “to”; in the following chapter: “Curagrius.”]. Since certain curiales of different cities improperly [Note: [Col. 0359B] c MS 11: “because”; in MS 40 the words “Since certain,” the only surviving words of the law itself, are joined to the inscription.] summon [Note: [Col. 0359B] d MS 16 omits “cities, curiales”; MS 11: “curialis.”] minors [Note: [Col. 0359B] e MSS 6, 7, 10, 16–18, 21, Sich.: “intemperate”; MS 20: “inteperantes,” with “intemperate” added above the line; Rein. emends “incompetently.”] [Note: [Col. 0359B] f MS 16: “customs”; MS 17: “strange.”] to membership in the curia, although public protection [Note: [Col. 0359B] g MS 15: “public care”; MS 11: “owed.”] is due to them, and are shown to have nominated some who are seven or eight years old [Note: [Col. 0359C] h MS 20 and Sich.: “and”; MSS 6, 7, 10, 14, 16–18: “as in seven.”] [Note: [Col. 0359C] i MS 20: “having been constituted”; MS 25: “is constituted.”] [Note: [Col. 0359C] j MSS 10, 18: “of no established nomination”; MSS 6, 7, 14, 17: “establishment”; MS 16: “is established”; Sich.: “they shall have nominated, they affirm firmly.” Go. interprets *firmentur* as “are affirmed.” MS 25 omits “some … nominated … are shown”; MS 6: “some.”], we decree [Note: [Col. 0359C] k MSS 6, 7, 10, 14, 17: “we have decreed.”] that absolutely no one is to be summoned into a curia by nominations [Note: [Col. 0359C] l MS 11: “by dominations,” MS 20: “shall be summoned”; MSS 10, 18: “not into a curia by actions”; MS 15: “no one in the curia is nominated.”] or compelled to undergo the duties of public functions [Note: [Col. 0359C] m See Vatican Fragments §248.] unless he has entered his eighteenth year of age [Note: [Col. 0359C] n MS 11 adds “his”; MSS 10, 18 omit “has entered.” “That … year of age”; Sich.: “year of age.”]. We wish this also to be prevented in future [Note: [Col. 0359C] o MS 9: “That among less future”; MS 23 omits “also”; subsequently MS 11: “excellent,” Sich.: “exempt.”], and those already nominated while below that age limit are to be exempted and released from curial bonds [Note: [Col. 0359C] p MSS 6, 7, 14, 16, 17: “within.”] [Note: [Col. 0359C] q MSS 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14, 16, 17, 20, 21, 25, Sich. omit “so that”; MS 4 repeats it by an earlier hand; MS 15: “so that curial bonds”; Aur. and Lugd.: “and bonds.”]. For when they have entered their eighteenth year of age [Note: [Col. 0359D] r MS 21 and Sich.: “the year of age”; MS 25: “year.” See chapter 7 of this title.] [Note: [Col. 0359D] s MSS 9, 11: singular; MS 20: “has entered”; MS 16: “thus military service”; MS 25: “if in the name of military service.”], if they cannot enter their names for military service according to the law [Col. 0359B] given [Note: [Col. 0359D] t See C. Th. chapter 18 of this title, note **.] [Note: [Col. 0359D] u MS 4: “may be open,” corrected by an earlier hand to “may be able”; MS 20 singular; MS 14 omits “or … may be able.”], or decline to do so, they may be assigned to municipal service [Note: [Col. 0359D] v MSS 6, 7, 16: “were able”; MSS 10, 18: “may be able to give”; MS 11: “municipal … could give”; MS 25 omits “may be assigned municipally”; MS 20: “to give”; MS 21: “municipal”; Sich.: “may be able.”]. Given on the day before [Note: [Col. 0359D] x Some manuscripts: “second” for “day before”; MS 9: “given on the Ides of the Nones”; MSS 29, 33, 42: “given on the day before the Ides of the Nones”; MSS 20, 32: “given on the third”; MSS 31, 34 omit “day before,” and MS 38 “Nones”; MS 16: “Kalends” for “Nones.”] the Nones of August [Note: [Col. 0359D] y MS 20: “April.”], under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0359D] z MSS 6, 7, 10, 14, 18, 21, 32, Sich.: “Abundantius” or “Abundancius”; MSS 16, 43: “Habundantius, consuls”; MS 20: “habundancius”; Sich. in the margin restores “Ablavius.” Some manuscripts have “consul,” and MS 16 “consuls,” for *Coss.*] (331).

[Col. 0360A] INTERPRETATION. Curiales below eighteen years of age [Note: [Col. 0360B] a MS 11: “This law says [this] of one under ten.”] [Note: [Col. 0360B] b Some manuscripts, including 6, 7, 21, omit “of age”; MS 20: “curiales of age neither nominate by anyone.”] ought neither to be nominated by anyone [Note: [Col. 0360B] c MS 43: “or.”] nor assigned to services [Note: [Col. 0360B] d MS 11: “service”; MSS 6, 7: “publicly”; in MS 7 a second hand adds above the line “be applied.”], because this law considers it sufficient [Note: [Col. 0360B] e Sich.: “this law is sufficient, is believed,” but in the margin agrees with our text; MSS 20, 43: “this.”] that from [Note: [Col. 0360B] f Cuj. 2–Ri*: “from”; MSS 6, 7, 43: “so that from eighteen”; MSS 11, 20: “so that to eighteen”; MS 21, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd. omit “from.” Go. disapproves this part of the Interpretation. Under C. Th., sons of military apparitors are not assigned to the curia after completing their eighteenth year, but as soon as they enter that year.] eighteen years [Note: [Col. 0360B] g Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “years”; MSS 20, 21: “years,” as do many manuscripts.] they may, if necessary, be assigned to public obligations [Note: [Col. 0360B] h MSS 6, 7, 10, 16, 18: plural, “have been necessary.”], provided that those [Note: [Col. 0360B] i Sich., Cuj. 1, Cuj. 2, 3*: singular “anyone”; Rein. corrects to plural; MSS 6, 7, 10, 18, 44 and many others: “within.”] below this age who have already been nominated [Note: [Col. 0360C] j MSS 6, 7, 11, 21, 42, 43 and many others: “had been”; MS 20: “were”; some manuscripts: “shall be released.”] shall be released.

The same Augustus to Evagrius [Note: [Col. 0360C] k See C. Th. chapter 19 of this title, note h; MS 26: “PP”; MSS 9, 21, 25 omit “Praetorian Prefect”; MSS 10, 18: “prefect”; MS 15: “the same Augustus to the same.”], Praetorian Prefect. No decurion [Note: [Col. 0360C] l MS 21: “curion.”] may undertake procuratorships [Note: [Col. 0360C] m MSS 9, 11, 12, 25, Sich.: “appeals”; MSS 10, 18: “appeal.” Summary of C. Th.: “Curiales residing in the country may not become procurators.” The words added here, “residing in the country,” are absent from C. Th.; the Interpretation reads “the office of curator.”] or curatorships [Note: [Col. 0360C] n MS 15 omits “or curatorships”; MS 15: “of the city”; Ri*: “curias.”] of cities [Note: [Col. 0360C] o MSS 16, 20: plural.] unless he has completely discharged every duty owed to his native community [Note: [Col. 0360C] p See below chapter 65 of this title.] [Note: [Col. 0360C] q MS 15: “has discharged his native community”; MS 20: plural.] either by age or by merits. But whoever has attained this office through influence, wishing to administer it, shall not only be repelled from the office sought [Note: [Col. 0360C] r MSS 19, 18: “from the office sought”; MS 21: “from the expected.”], but his letter [Note: [Col. 0360C] s MSS 15, 20: plural; many manuscripts: “codicils.”] or codicils shall immediately be taken from him [Note: [Col. 0360C] t MS 16: “shall take away”; MSS 10, 18: “shall offer.”] and sent to [Note: [Col. 0360C] u MS 4: “shall be taken away and to”; the words “and to” are deleted in red [Col. 0360D] || fol. 224b || and are therefore written twice.] the imperial court [Note: [Col. 0360D] v MSS 4, 6, 7, 10–12, 14, 17, 18, 21, 25, Sich.–Cuj. 2*: plural, “shall be sent”; MS 20: “distinetur”; the rest: singular. The word *destinentur* coheres with the preceding words: “Whoever … has attained [office] through influence, wishing to administer, shall not only be repelled … and be sent to court,” though the construction is defective. Yet *destinentur* does not seem suitable to W., who thinks “and be sent to court” refers to the curial, not to the codicils taken from him. But if *destinentur* means “be remitted” or “be sent,” the emperor orders the codicils to be sent or remitted to the imperial court, so that the court—interpreted as “the lords of affairs,” that is, the emperors—may know that the curial has been rejected from office. This view pleases the editor; he therefore restores the reading of the oldest manuscripts, such as 4, 6, and 7.]. Given on the day before [Note: [Col. 0360D] x Some manuscripts: “second”; MSS 27, 31, 35: “third”; MS 40 omits “day before.”] the Ides [Note: [Col. 0360D] y MSS 28, 36, 40: “October”; subsequently MS 20: “forgetfulness.”] of August, under the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Col. 0360B] (331).

[Col. 0361A] INTERPRETATION. This law commands [Note: [Col. 0361B] a MSS 6, 7, 9, 10, 18, 10 and many others: “commands”; similarly MSS 21, 42–44; editions: “orders”; MS 11: “says”; some manuscripts, such as 11, 20, 21, 42–44: “This law.”] that no curial, unless he has performed in due order every duty of the curia, may undertake the office of curator [Note: [Col. 0361B] b MS 11: “performed, and either curators or defenders”; so also other manuscripts, but not “by curators.”] or defender, unless he has first discharged all the obligations, as stated, that are owed to his native community [Note: [Col. 0361B] c MS 7, by a second hand, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “native”; MS 9: “has been, which [are owed] to the native community.”] in due order [Note: [Col. 0361B] d MSS 6, 11: “and to order”; MSS 7, 21, Sich.–Lugd.: “to the order.” Subsequently MS 9 has “private” for “aforesaid” [MS 11, “aforesaid”], and some manuscripts have “influence … duty,” for “to protect himself.”]. For if the aforesaid person wishes, contrary to this command, to protect himself by any influence or under any pretext of office, he shall lose what he has obtained and be sent to where the lords of affairs are [Note: [Col. 0361C] e MS 11 and editions except Go.: plural “shall be sent.” The sense requires singular, and so read the manuscripts, including 6, 7, 20, 21. The Visigoths therefore referred the word *destinentur*—see above, note a—to the curial. Some manuscripts read “has been sent”; MS 11: “guilty” for “of affairs.”].

## TO THE SENATUS CONSULTUM CLAUDIANUM
Imp. Constantine . . . [Note: [Col. 0361C] f This law also, hitherto unknown, is owed to folio VII of the Turin manuscript. The heading, together with the margin of the folio, has been torn away. “The same Augustus” should be restored; P. restored this reading in folio VII itself, and W. adopted it. But P., in his transcript, and Pu. read “Emperor Constantine,” contrary to scribal practice: if a law of the same emperor precedes in the same title, they write “The same Augustus” and do not repeat the emperor’s name. Here, however, that some law of Constantine preceded is inferred from the subscription, with which folio VII begins.] Any woman who, after this law, joins herself to the contubernium of slaves and has not been formally warned by denunciations, as ancient law prescribed, shall lose her status of freedom. [Note: [Col. 0361C] g P., in his commentary, reads *pro et* and appears to have wished to restore *etiam*, “also.”] Given on the day before the Nones of October, in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0361C] h 1, P., Pu.: *Ablabio*.] (331).

## CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF THE PRAETORIAN PREFECTS

[Col. 0361B] Emperor Constantine Augustus to Bassus, Praetorian Prefect. [Note: [Col. 0361C] i 20: *ppu.* 28, 40 omit “to Bassus, Praetorian Prefect.” 27: “Emperor Const. Constantine, Praetorian Prefect.” 44: “Emperor C. to Constantius, Praetorian Prefect.” 8 adds “in place of the law itself.”] Concerning those who request that a judgment pronounced by a governor or by any other judge [Note: [Col. 0361D] j 16: “Concerning those who are proud.” 19, 20, 21: *que*. k 5: “by any other judge.” l 19: “a judgment pronounced.” Several manuscripts subsequently have *infirmare*, “to invalidate.”] be invalidated, let examination come before Your Sublimity with this limitation: if, after the internal proceedings [Note: [Col. 0361D] m 8: *examini*, “for examination.” n 14, 19: “internal business.” 20, 21, Sich.: “among proceedings”; but Sich., from the Augsburg manuscript, reads as we do, though omitting “in every respect.” *Interna negotia*, like *interna causae* in C. Th. IV, 22, c. 1, and X, 12, c. 2.] have in every respect run their course [Note: [Col. 0361D] o 19: *decursi*. Sich.: *decursa*. 21: *diversis*. In his correction, p. 178, Sich., from the Augsburg manuscript, gives *decursis*.] it has become clear from the evidence [Note: [Col. 0361D] p 8: *caruerit*. 5: *evidenti*.] that the judgment departs from law [Note: [Col. 0361D] q 6, 8, 10, 18: “the judgment from greater [authority].” 20, 21, Sich., Til.: “the judgment, from law”; Til. adds *majore* in the margin. 5, 14: “the judgment from greater [authority].” Sich.: “from justice also.”] and justice, then, once it has been wholly quashed [Note: [Col. 0361D] r 18, Til. in the margin: *discere et*. Sich. in the margin: *et*.] the controversy shall receive its conclusion according to equity. [Note: [Col. 0361D] s Sich., Til.: “having been quashed, the controversy, according to.” 5: *aequalitate*, “equality.”] [Col. 0362A] But if the judgment already issued [Note: [Col. 0362B] a 9, 18: *tam pr.* 19: “already provided.” 21: “advanced, or already provided.” 20: “laws . . . provided in readiness,” but “or already” is added above *prompta*. Sich., Til.: “provided, or already issued.” One reading arose from a gloss; but *prompta*, i.e. “issued,” is preferable.] is consistent with the laws, its unscrupulous assailant, if he possesses abundant property [Note: [Col. 0362B] b Most manuscripts read thus; editions: *circumfluat*. Others: *oppugnatur*. 8: *adpugnatur*.] shall be punished by relegation to an island for two years, [Note: [Col. 0362C] c Many manuscripts: *biennii*. W. conjectures *bienni*, which can readily be dispensed with. Several manuscripts subsequently add *in insula*.] and half his goods shall pass, assigned to the fiscal revenues. But if he lives a rustic life [Note: [Col. 0362C] d 9: *vita*. Shortly above Sich.: “one part.”] or is even indigent, [Note: [Col. 0362C] e 5, 8–10, 14, 18–21 omit *etiam*, “even”; several manuscripts have *ad*.] he shall be sent to the mines for two years. [Note: [Col. 0362C] f Thus 19, and Aur. Lugd. in the margin; similarly 5: *detruendus*, and 8: *detruendus*. 20, 21, Sich.: *detrahendus*; the common reading is *retrudendus*.] You must also observe this law in our annotations concerning a renewed trial after judgment. [Note: [Col. 0362C] g 21, Sich.: *dexterando*; but, in his correction, p. 178, Sich. gives from the Augsburg manuscript *de iterando*. Compare Biener, *Geschichte der Novellen Justinians*, p. 40, and his discussion of the Augsburg Theodosian Code, § 6.] Given on the thirteenth [Note: [Col. 0362C] h 20, 21, 28, 36, 40, Sich.: sixth; 5, 35, 44: seventh; 8, 9: fifteenth; 19, 24, 25, 29, 30, 32, 33, 39, 42, 43, Cuj. 2, 2*: sixteenth; 27, 38: seventeenth.] day before the Kalends of November, [Note: [Col. 0362C] i 28, Sich., Til., Cuj. 1, Aur. Lugd. in the margin: December. Add “at Constantinople.” See C. Th. I, 16, cc. 6 and 7.] in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius [Note: [Col. 0362C] j 5, 20, 21, 44, Sich.: Albianus. 19: Blavius. 25: Ableveus. 38: Aluvius; but Sich. has Ablavius in the margin.] (331).

### INTERPRETATION

Whoever, after a case has been heard and the matter examined [Note: [Col. 0362D] k 8 adds “in court.”], has been defeated by anyone, and afterwards attempts to reopen that same suit—if a judgment has been rendered according to the laws in favour of that same person who was previously ruled against [Note: [Col. 0362D] l Most manuscripts: “formerly.” m Sich.: *dictus*, “declared.” Cuj. 1, Aur. Lugd.: *victus*, “defeated.” 20, 21: “who has previously been declared by the laws”; *dictus* is added above the line after *supra*.]—the first judgment shall not stand. For if he is defeated before another judge also, [Note: [Col. 0362D] n Sich. and many manuscripts: *etsi*, “although.”] then, if he is a person of standing and means, [Note: [Col. 0362D] o Most manuscripts: *est*, “is,” followed by “in exile, in the mines.”] he shall be sent into exile for two years, and the fisc shall acquire half [Note: [Col. 0362D] p Thus 8, 9, 19–21, Sich., Lugd. d. 1, A., Cuj. 1. The remaining editions read *media*, “a half.”] his property. But if he is a person of low standing and poorer means, he shall be sent to the mines for two years.

## CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF A PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the Provincials. Let governors conduct public hearings [Note: [Col. 0362D] q *Naciones*. Cl., Pu.: *rationes*, incorrectly. W. corrected to *notiones*, approved by Schroeder. See C. Th. IX, 37, c. 3.] in tribunals frequented for hearings, and, when they are to hear civil controversies, let them not hide themselves in their secretariats, [Note: [Col. 0362D] r 5: “Let them hide themselves in secretarial hearing-rooms.” Cl. and Pu. place *sese* in brackets; deleting it, W. thinks *auditorii* or *auditoriis* and *secretariis* require emendation. W. attempts to remedy the passage by punctuating after *auditoriis*, which does not help. Hu. conjectures *controversiae*. Bijdr. conjectures *audituri*, approved by W., *Opp.*, p. 432; this correction has been adopted, but with *in* inserted after *audituri*, since the Theodosian Code undoubtedly previously read *auditurii secretariis*. Similarly, in the following c. 9: “The judge—in hearing and examining suits—shall not report in the seclusion of his house, but with the doors of the secretariat open.”] so that one wishing to litigate may not be unable to obtain access to them except by payment. And when they have given a hearing to all matters brought before them, and the frequent proclamation of the crier, [Note: [Col. 0363B] a Thus correctly 5, Cl., Pu.; W. corrected to *sed*, incorrectly. b Thus as emended by W.; 5, Cl., Pu.: *praeconiis*, wrongly printed by Schroeder.] as is customary, finds no one wishing to make a petition, they shall withdraw after all public and private business has been completed.

Moreover, we grant everyone the power to praise most just and vigilant judges by public acclamations, [Note: [Col. 0363B] c At “most just” begins C. Just. cited, c. 3, where *autem* is omitted.] so that we may advance them to higher stages of honour; [Note: [Col. 0363B] d Thus Cl., Pu.; W. from C. Just.; but Pl. 1 has “and honour,” 5 “by honour.” Hu. conjectures *honorum*, as manuscript Bg.] conversely, unjust and criminal judges are to be accused by the voices of complainants, [Note: [Col. 0363C] e 5, Cl., Pu., and W. from C. Just.: *et*, “and.” f Thus 5 and Pu., approved by Hu.; Cl. and W., from C. Just.: “unjust and criminal [men].” g Thus 5, Pu., approved by Hu.; Cl., W., from C. Just.: “to accuse.”] so that the force of our censure may consume them. [Note: [Col. 0363C] h 5: *asumat*.] For if those voices are true [Note: [Col. 0363C] i 5: *st.*, i.e. *sunt*, which Cl. and Pu. also correctly have, though Schroeder printed it wrongly. W., from C. Just., prints *sint*, “may be”; but there too the best manuscripts have *sunt*. Neither here nor above, I, 12, 2, note m, does *si* mean “whether,” as W. thought.] and have not been poured forth arbitrarily through factions, [Note: [Col. 0363C] j 5: *effage*.] we shall investigate carefully, [Note: [Col. 0363C] k 5: *investigavimus*, “we investigated.”] while the praetorian prefects and the counts established in the provinces report to our knowledge the voices of our provincials. Published [Note: [Col. 0363B] PP. l C. Just.: “Given,” more correctly, since this constitution was to be posted not at Constantinople but in the provinces. See also the following constitution, given on the same day, not posted. Hal.: “Given on the day before the Kalends,” and omits “Constantinople.”] on the Kalends of November at Constantinople, [Note: [Col. 0363C] m 5: “at Constantine’s.” Here end the additions to the Theodosian Code owed to the Ambrosian manuscript (5). In the following material the scribe copied only the Breviary and supplies no supplement; therefore Pu. omits all that follows, and continues only from the title *On Holidays* (II, 8) in publishing supplements from the Turin palimpsest.] in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

Emperor Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0363D] n Thus it must now be written from manuscript 5; formerly the editions, because this was the first constitution under the title, read “Emperor Constantine.”] to the Provincials. [Note: [Col. 0363D] o Some manuscripts omit “to the Provincials”; others have “to the provincials.”] Let the rapacious hands of officials now cease—let them cease, I say; for if, having been warned, they do not cease, [Note: [Col. 0363D] p Some manuscripts: *tunc*, “then.” Sich. subsequently: *officilium*. q 5: “I say, unless warned, they cease” (omitting *non*); 6, 7, 9, 14, 16: “unless warned, they do not cease.”] they shall be cut off by the sword. [Note: [Col. 0363D] r 10, 18: “shall be cut off.” 5: *precedentur*.] Let neither the judge’s curtain [Note: [Col. 0363D] s 6, 8, 17, Til.: *venalis*, “venal.” 9, 10, 14, R.: “let judges be venal.” t 8, 20, 21, Sich.: *verbum*, “word.”] be for sale, nor entrance be purchased, [Note: [Col. 0363D] u 19: *redemptio*, “purchase.”] [Col. 0364A] nor the secretariat be disgraced by bidding, [Note: [Col. 0364B] a 6: “disgraceful solicitation.” 10, 14, 17, 18, R., Til.: *licitationis*. 19: *infamet*. 20, 21, Sich.: “may he disgrace [it] by bidding.” 21: *scietarium*.] nor the very sight of the governor be subject to payment; let the ears [Note: [Col. 0364B] b 8: “and precious.” 19: “and ears at a price.” c 6, 16, 17: *auctores*, “authors.”] of the judge [Note: [Col. 0364B] d Thus all editions except W., who silently corrected to “of judges”; but manuscripts have either “of the judge” or “of judges,” and 21 alone *judicadis*. 8 subsequently: “to the poorest.”] be open alike to the poorest and the rich. Let there be no plundering in introducing the person called chief of the office. [Note: [Col. 0364B] e 21, R.: *indicendo*, “in proclaiming.” 20, above the line: “as from seduction.” Cuj. 1, Lugd. in the margin: *ob inducendum*. Some manuscripts: *eos*, “them.”] Let no exactions by the assistants of those same chiefs of office be inflicted upon litigants. [Note: [Col. 0364B] f 21, Sich., Til.: “some plundering.” L.: “Assistants.” But Sich., in his correction from the Augsburg manuscript: “plundering. Let no assistants [of] litigants . . .”; Til. in the margin: *depraed.* 20: *ulla*, perhaps previously *nulla*. 6, 9: “No assistant of a litigant.” 10, 16, 18: “litigants.” 14: “of a litigant’s assistant.” g Some manuscripts: *officium*; others, forms of *concussiones*, “extortions.” 21: *commissiones*.] Let the intolerable assaults of centurions and other officials who demand small and great sums be restrained; [Note: [Col. 0364C] h 19: “or others.” Sich., Til.: “Let the assaults of centurions and others be inflicted”; but Sich. corrects the text. i 20, 21, Sich.: “while demanding, the intolerable assault must be restrained, of those who”; in his correction, Sich. from the Augsburg manuscript has “the intolerable assaults of those demanding are to be restrained, [and] of those who.” 19: “Let intolerable demands be abolished.” 10, 18, R.: *impetus obligantur*.] and let the unrestrained greed of those who restore records to litigants [Note: [Col. 0364C] j Some manuscripts, R.: *praestituunt*; subsequently: “let him watch.”] be curbed. Let the diligence of the governor always be watchful, lest anything [Note: [Col. 0364C] k Most manuscripts, R.: “and lest anyone.” 5: “and lest anything.” 16: “the governor, or lest anyone.”] be taken from a litigant by the aforesaid classes of persons. If they suppose that anything ought to be demanded in civil cases, [Note: [Col. 0364C] l 8: *potuerint*, “have been able,” and omits *esse*.] armed censure shall be at hand to cut off the heads and necks of the impious; all persons who have been subjected to extortion [Note: [Col. 0364C] m 14: *culpa*, “fault.” n 5: *confusi*, “confused.” 8: *concursi*.] are granted the opportunity to inform the governor’s judicial authority. [Note: [Col. 0364D] o 8: “may inform the nation.” 18: “inform the notation.”] If those persons connive at it, we open to all the right of complaint concerning it before any of the provincial counts or before the praetorian prefect, if he is nearer, [Note: [Col. 0364B] p 8: “of seeking them out.” 20, 21, Sich.: “of seeking the same [matter] out.” 16 subsequently: *aper.* or *apud*. q 8 omits “counts.” 5, 10, 14, 16, 17, 19 omit “all.” 8: “to all.” 9: “we open [a complaint] which [belongs] to all before the provincial counts.” r 5, 6, 16, 17: “prefects”; subsequently others have “of the praetorium” or “praetorium,” as Sich., Til. s 5, 6, 8, 10, 18: *fuerint*, plural. t 8 omits *ut*.] so that, when informed by their reports, we may pronounce punishments for such acts of brigandage. [Note: [Col. 0364D] u All manuscripts and editions read *super*, “concerning”; W. silently corrected to *de*. But Go., followed by Ri., correctly revealed the sense by punctuating after *latrociniis*, “acts of brigandage”; the rest punctuate after *edocti*, “informed.” v 8: *supplicio*, singular. x Til. and Aur. Lugd. in the margin, Be., W., and 5: *proferamus*, “we may pronounce”; the other editions and manuscripts 8, 20, 21, R.: *referamus*, “we may report”; 19: *deferamus*, “we may bring.”] [Col. 0365A] Given on the Kalends [Note: [Col. 0365C] a 38: “Given on the tenth day before the Kalends”; Anianus’s manuscript in Go.: eleventh.] of November, at Constantinople, [Note: [Col. 0365C] b 20, 39 omit “Constantinople.” 10, 18: “at Constantine’s, Prefect B.”] in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius, [Note: [Col. 0365C] c 20, 39, Sich.: Albino; Sich. in the margin: Albio.] men of highest rank [Note: [Col. 0365C] d Most manuscripts omit *VV. CC.*] (331).

### INTERPRETATION

Let officials of all judges not dare to be venal, nor demand payment for the entry or departure of persons arriving or litigants. [Note: [Col. 0365C] e Several manuscripts and some editions: *nec*—“nor”—instead of *neque*; “of persons arriving or litigants.”] Let petitioners, both rich and poor, be heard without any payment. [Note: [Col. 0365C] f Very many manuscripts, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “But”; in other manuscripts, as in 5, the words “both rich and poor” are transposed to after “without any payment.”] If they choose to be rapacious, let them be punished by the sword, or at least let their rapacity be reported to the imperial ears.

## CONCERNING THE JEWS

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the *hiereis* (“priests”), archisynagogues, fathers of synagogues, and all others [Note: [Col. 0365D] g 4: *ceteros*, corrected in red to *ceteris*. 11: “The same Augusti to priests” (omitting *et*); also Cuj. 2–Go. omit *et*: “archisynagogues and fathers of synagogues.”] who serve in the same place. We command that priests, archisynagogues, fathers of synagogues, and all others serving synagogues shall be free from every compulsory bodily service. [Note: [Col. 0365D] h Cuj. 1–Lugd.: *Hieros*. Go. incorrectly: *Archisynagos*. i 11: “archisynagogues and fathers of synagogues—synagogues—of bodily [services]—we command.”] Given on the Kalends of December, at Constantinople, in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius (331).

## CONCERNING THE JURISDICTION OF ALL JUDGES

Emperor Constantine Augustus to all provincials. After the joining of issue, no one shall evade the examination of the ordinary court; nor, before doing so, shall he seek the aid of the praetorian prefect, the Count of the East, or another judge of *spectabilis* rank, but, having made an appeal according to law, shall come before the sacred audience. Given on the Kalends of October, in the consulship of Bassus and Ablavius, 331. (From the Code of Justinian.)

In the year of the Lord 332, in the consulship of Pacatianus and Hilarianus.

## CONCERNING THE SONS OF SOLDIERS

Emperor Constantine Augustus to Leontius, Praetorian Prefect. We have long since enacted [Note: [Col. 0365D] j Go. refers to C. Th. VII, 20, c. 2, *On Veterans*.] that the sons of veterans [Note: [Col. 0365D] k Go.: *vereranorum*, an error.] who, after sixteen [Col. 0365C] years, are unable to undertake military service or prove unfit to bear arms, shall be assigned to the municipal councils. [Note: [Col. 0365D] l The Code reads *extiterit*; in c. 4, copied in cited c. 35, it reads: “By a repeated law we enact that sons of veterans, if after . . . they cannot . . . are not fit, shall be assigned to municipal councils.”] Given on the third day before the Ides of April, in the consulship of Pacatianus and Hilarianus [Note: [Col. 0365D] m Aur. Lugd.: *Cons.*] (332).

## CONCERNING BETROTHALS

Emperor Constantine Augustus [Note: [Col. 0365D] n Code of Justinian: “Emperor Constantius Augustus and Constans Caesar,” incorrectly.] to Pacatianus, Urban Prefect. [Note: [Col. 0365D] o 9, 15, 29, 42: *ppo.* Code of Justinian: *P. P.*, approved by Go. and W.; compare Corsini, cited work, p. 184. Be. conjectures *PPf. U.*, which the editor does not understand. 16, 28 omit *Pf. U.* Editions variously read “Prefect V.,” “Praef. V.,” or “Praef. U.,” except Til., who has *P. V.* Moreover 15, 25: *Pacationo*; 34: *Agatiano*. Go. says this constitution was interpolated by Tribonian; W. denies this because of the difference in wording and therefore believes that c. 2 of the Code of Justinian originally stood elsewhere in the Theodosian Code. Perhaps Tribonian combined c. 2 from two Theodosian constitutions. The words of constitution 2 are: “If one who has promised a girl in marriage to himself, while living in the same province, has delayed for two years to celebrate the marriage, and, once that period has elapsed, the girl afterwards enters into union with another, no fraud shall attach to her, since, by hastening marriage, she has not allowed her hopes to be mocked any longer.”]

The girl’s father [Note: [Col. 0366A–C] a Ri., by conjecture in the Preface to vol. I of the Theodosian Code, p. XV: manuscripts 6–9, 12, 14, 16, 17, 21, and editions Sich.–Lugd. read “the father or mother of the girl”; but Ri., prompted by Bestius, observes that *aut* has been misplaced by scribes. Cuj. 2, followed by later editions, first printed “the father or mother of the girl.” Bestius therefore errs, p. 280, in believing that Go. silently added *matri*. Bestius also proposes “the father, grandfather of the girl,” because *aut* could easily have arisen from *avo*; but this conjecture does not accord with the manuscripts. 19 omits *aut*. From all this it appears that both *aut* and *matri* are suspect and should be deleted. The interpreter makes no mention of the mother, as he would have done had *matri* stood in the law, as he does in the interpretation of c. 6 under this title. The editor therefore did not hesitate, following Ri., to delete *aut matri* and restore “the girl’s father,” especially as five manuscripts, 10, 15, 18–20, support that reading.] or tutor or [Note: [Col. 0366C] b Thus 6–10, 12, 15, 18–21, Til.; Aur. Lugd. omits *aut*. The remaining editions have *vel*, “or.”] curator or any [Note: [Col. 0366C] c 8: “of any person.”] relative of hers may not, after first betrothing the girl to a soldier, give her in marriage to another. [Note: [Col. 0366C] d 6, 7, 14, 16 omit *non*. 21: “her relative may not.” e 15: “to anyone,” a noteworthy reading. f 6–10, 12, 14, 18: plural *desponderint*, “have betrothed,” not badly.] If this occurs within two years, [Note: [Col. 0366C–D] g Thus most manuscripts and all editions. Bestius, approved by Ri., reads: “If within two years he is guilty of bad faith, let him be relegated to an island.” Co. conjectures *fiat* or *fecerit* (“has completed two years”). *Fecerit* is supported by three manuscripts, 10, 14, 18, which also add *quis* after *quod si*; but the common text suits the idiom of Latin, which not infrequently omits a verb supplied of itself from the preceding member. 20 has *sit* above the line for *si* in *quodsi*. 12: *infra*.] he shall be guilty of bad faith [Note: [Col. 0366D] h 15: “guilty of bad faith.”] and relegated to an island. But if, after marriage has been agreed upon, two years having elapsed, the person who betrothed the girl joins her to another, the fault shall be attributed rather to the betrothed man than to the girl; nor [Note: [Col. 0366D] i 15: “But if marriage has been agreed upon.” j 8, 10, 18: *ne*, “nor.”] shall any harm come to the person who, after two years, gave the girl to another husband. [Note: [Col. 0366D] k 6–10, 14–18, 20, Til.: *tradidit*, “gave”; remaining manuscripts and editions: *tradiderit*, “shall have given.”] Given on the day before [Note: [Col. 0366D] l Some manuscripts omit “the day before.” 10: “Given on the first”; 18, 32, 39, 43: “Given on the fifth.”] the Ides of April, at Martianopolis, in the consulship of Pacatianus and Hilarianus [Note: [Col. 0366D] m 8, 16 omit “and Hilarianus.” 10, 18: “April, Martianus, prefect, Pacatianus and . . .” 26: “Martianus, Praetorian Prefect, Pacatianus and Hilarianus.” 21, Sich.: “April, Martianus and Hilarianus, consuls.” 33: Gratianus and Hilarianus.] (332).

### INTERPRETATION

If anyone, civilian or soldier, after making a betrothal has settled the matter of the girl’s marriage with her parents, tutor, or curator [Note: [Col. 0366D] n 21 and editions under this title add *et*, which disturbs the sentence. o 20: *procuratore*. 6, 7: “father, tutor, or procurator.”] or relatives, he must celebrate the marriage within two years after the agreement. [Note: [Col. 0366D–0367B] p 6, 7, 9, 10, 18, 20, 42, 44 and many other manuscripts, Sich., Cuj. 1–Lugd., omit “if age permits,” which is foreign to the law itself and was added here in Cuj. 2–Ri*.] [Col. 0367A] If, through the tardiness or negligence [Note: [Col. 0367B] a 6, 7: “or through negligence”; others: “through tardiness or negligence.” 6, following Ri.: “If through tardiness by negligence.”] of the betrothed man, the two-year period has passed and the girl marries another man, [Note: [Col. 0367B] b Thus manuscripts, wrongly printed by Go.; *alio viro* is ablative and properly depends upon *conjunxerit*, “has joined herself.”] she and anyone among her people who gave her in marriage shall be free from liability; [Note: [Col. 0367C] c 20 omits *a*, “from.” d Some manuscripts add *qui*, “who.”] for the fault lies with him who, by delaying his own marriage, made room for her marriage to another. But if she is given in marriage within two years, what is to be observed will be learned more clearly from the following law. [Note: [Col. 0367C] e Compare c. 6 under this title. f 6, 7, 20, 21, 44 and many other manuscripts: *cognoscitur*, “is learned.”]

## CONCERNING AN UNDUTIFUL WILL

Emperor Constantine Augustus to the Council of Byzacena. [Note: [Col. 0367C] g 20, Sich.: Baianorum; Sich. in the margin: Bizantinorum, as 25, 29 and Til. in the margin. 19: Bissacinorum. 42: Bracianorum. 18: Bizancinorum. 15: Bizacenorum. The remaining manuscripts mostly have Bizacinorum, as Til.–Ri*. See Go. on this passage.] A necessary slave must be instituted heir, [Note: [Col. 0367C] h 15: “a necessary heir instituted,” omitting “is because”; a noteworthy reading. 33 omits “heir.”] because [Note: [Col. 0367C] i 20, Sich.: *qui non*, “who does not.”] he appears to acquire not so much an estate as disgrace. Hence it is clear [Note: [Col. 0367C] j 9, Sich.: “that it may be clear.” 10, 18: “hence [it] lacks.” 33: “hence let it be clear.”] that the action for an undutiful will is granted to brothers [Note: [Col. 0367C] k 20: *inofficiosis*. 40, 41: “the actions for an undutiful will are granted.”] when the person who became heir is stained by the blemishes of disgrace, [Note: [Col. 0367C] l 15: “reserved for brothers, when he is sprinkled with disgrace,” omitting “blemishes.” m 20, Sich.: *respergitur*. 6, 7, 10, 18: *aspergetur*.] and that all things which the instituted heir cannot receive because of baseness or some slight stigma are to pass to the brothers. [Note: [Col. 0367C–D] n 6, 7, 9, 10, 14, 16–18, 28, 33, 40, 41 omit *is*, “he.” 20: *his*, “these.” o 15 and Go. in the note: *existit*, “is.” 33: *instituit*, “institutes.” p 6, 7, 10, 14, 17: *aliquem*, masculine. 40, 41 omit *aut*.] Likewise, in this matter too, whenever brothers are passed over in favour of freedmen instituted as heirs, [Note: [Col. 0367D] q 20, Sich. omit *ita*, “likewise.” r 15: *alienati*, “alienated.”] they shall prevail, upon bringing the action for an undutiful will, in acquiring all the estate [Note: [Col. 0367D] s 15: “property acquired.”] of the deceased, which he had wrongly wished [Note: [Col. 0367D] t 41: *pro persona*, “for the person.”] to pass to freedmen. [Note: [Col. 0367D] u 20, Sich.: *voluerit*, “shall have wished.”] Given [Note: [Col. 0367D] v Go.: “That is, once it has been delivered.” 14 omits “Given.”] on the seventh [Note: [Col. 0367D] x 15, 33: sixth. Go., in his chronology: “elsewhere, on the sixth.” Compare C. Th. IV, 10, c. 1, note g.] day before the Kalends of August, at Cologne Agrippina, [Note: [Col. 0367D] y Go., in commentary on this constitution, emends to Hadrumetum. 9: “almost Cologne.”] in the consulship of Pacatianus [Note: [Col. 0367D] z Manuscripts mostly: Pagatianus. 8, 10, 18: Paccatianus. 38: Picatianus.] and Hilarianus [Note: [Col. 0367D] aa 16: Elarianus. 38: Hylarianus. Ri*: Hilarion. 20: “Agrippina, Pacatinus and Hilarianus, Cologne exile.”] (332).

### INTERPRETATION

If an inheritance has been left by a master, together with freedom, to a necessary slave on account of debt, [Note: [Col. 0367D–0368B] bb Many manuscripts, Sich., Cuj. 1, Aur. Lugd.: *per necessitatem*, “through necessity.”] since a person of this kind is regarded as disgraced, the full brothers who were passed over are granted the right to proceed against the will; so that, once the disgraced person has been removed—while preserving nevertheless the freedom which he deserved—the full brothers must claim the inheritance for themselves. [Note: [Col. 0368B] a Aur. Lugd.: *demissa*, “sent down.”] And if freedmen have been instituted heirs by will while the brothers were passed over, the deceased’s full brothers shall likewise exclude them from the property of the fraternal inheritance [Note: [Col. 0368B] b 20: “them from all [property] or from the property,” with “gloss” above the line; likewise *fraternitate*, “brotherhood.” c Many manuscripts: *excludut*. 20, Sich.: *excludant*, subjunctive.] and claim for themselves everything he left. [Note: [Col. 0368B] d 6, 7, 9, 20, 42: plural *reliquerint*. 43: *requirant*, “may claim.”]

## CONCERNING FREEDMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN

[Note: [Col. 0368B–C] e 6–8, 10, 12, 16–18, 38, Til.: “Concerning freedmen and their conduct,” which Go. criticizes but Ri. defends because of the subject of these constitutions. Compare c. 3 under this title. Cuj. 1–Lugd.: “Concerning freedmen and their children; elsewhere, conduct.” 15: “Of the same persons.”]

Emperor Constantine [Note: [Col. 0368C] f Sich.–Be.: Constantine. Code of Justinian: Constantius.] Augustus to the Council of Byzacena. [Note: [Col. 0368C] g Most manuscripts: Bizacinorum, as also Til. 8, 10, 18: Bizazinorum. 13: Bizantinum. 14: Bizaniorum. 15: Bizancenorum. 16: Bezazinorum. 25: Bitazinorum. 26: Bizanorum. 20, 40, 43: Bizancinorum. 21, Sich.: Byzantinorum. Cuj. 1–Be.: Byzacinorum. Code of Justinian: “to Maximus, Urban Prefect.”] The law is so hostile to ungrateful freedmen [Note: [Col. 0368C] h 9: “not freely.”] that, if through a certain arrogance or insolence they raise their necks [Note: [Col. 0368C] i 12, omitting *si*: *quisdam*, “someone.”] or incur guilt through even a slight offence, [Note: [Col. 0368C–D] j 10, 16, 18–20: “through a slight offence.” 21: “slight offences.” Fornerius, on Digest L, 16, l. 70, believes *haud levis offensae*, “not a slight offence,” should be read, incorrectly: the law speaks not of grave fault but of any offence, for which the interpreter uses *laeserit*, “has injured,” i.e. if the freedman has committed something or acted against his patron. See Go. on this constitution. The Code of Justinian reads: “If a manumitted person has proved ungrateful toward his patron and has in some arrogance raised his neck against him, or has incurred the guilt of a slight offence, let him be returned by his patron to subjection and authority”; much that follows does not belong here and seems transferred from another constitution, as the differing heading and subscription in the Code of Justinian also indicate.] they shall be returned by their patrons to subjection and authority. [Note: [Col. 0368D] k 19: *imperiali*, “imperial.” 10, 18: “under authority and control.”] Given on the sixth day before the Kalends of August, at Cologne Agrippina, in the consulship of Pacatianus and Hilarianus [Note: [Col. 0368D] l 20, 24, 28, 40, Sich. in the margin: fifth; 32, 33: seventh; 8, 31 omit sixth. Either seventh was written, or sixth was repeated from c. 3 of C. Th. II, 19, so that it is the same day. Both alternatives are supported by manuscripts. 8 omits “Agrippina, Pacatianus and”; 28: “Agrippina and Hilarianus”; 33, 34: Pacatianus. Some manuscripts: Pagatianus and Elarianus. Go. wishes Hadrumetum to be written for Agrippina. The Code of Justinian: “Given on the Ides of April, at Rome, in the fifth consulship of Constantius Augustus and the consulship of Constans Caesar” (319), which, though false, agrees with the heading.] (332).

### INTERPRETATION

Any person of servile status who has obtained freedom from his master, if [Note: [Col. 0368D] m 6, 7 omit *si*. Other manuscripts: “freedom,” omitting *si*. Aur. Lugd.: *postea*, “afterwards.”] he afterwards begins to behave proudly or injures his patron—that is, his manumitter—[Col. 0369A] shall, having lost [Note: [Col. 0369B] a Aur. Lugd.: *missa*, “sent.” 6, 7 subsequently: *eruit*, “snatches away.”] the freedom which he deserved, rightly be recalled into slavery. [Note: [Col. 0369B] b 6, 7, 20, 43: *servitio*, dative or ablative. c 6–8 and many other manuscripts omit *merito*, “rightly.” d Most manuscripts have *revocetur*, which better suits the whole sentence than the printed reading *revocetur*.]

## CONCERNING A FREE-STATUS CASE

Emperor Constantine Augustus . . . [Note: [Col. 0369C] e Go., because of C. Th. V, 9, c. 1, wishes “to the Provincials” to be supplied.
